children.title: Regional Domain Representations
children.top_down_role: Box, simplicial, polyhedral, conical, and mixed-domain descriptions carried by search nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Regional Domain Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional representations of a search node’s regional domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the ambient space be \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\). A regional domain \(R\subseteq X\) may be represented as a box \(R=\{x:\ell\le x\le u\}\), a simplex \(R=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\), a polyhedron \(R=\{x:Ax\le b\}\), or a conic set \(R=\{x:b-Ax\in K\}\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone. A mixed representation is a finite intersection or union of such sets, possibly augmented by integrality restrictions \(x_i\in\mathbb{Z}\). The node representation must provide a membership predicate and sufficient data to construct child regions whose union covers \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search region is encoded by explicit box, simplex, polyhedral, conic, or mixed constraints, together with membership and subdivision operations that preserve coverage.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\).
All representation data are finite.
Each child produced by subdivision is a subset of its parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R=\bigcup_{j=1}^m R_j\) for every covering subdivision \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) returned by the representation.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

children.title: Regional Relaxation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Node-local connections to valid lower-bounding models whose strength depends on the current region.

knowledge_statements.title: Regional Relaxation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity contract for a node-local lower-bounding relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with regional feasible set \(F_R\) and objective \(f\), a regional relaxation interface returns a set \(Y_R\), an objective \(\phi_R:Y_R\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), and an embedding \(\iota_R:F_R\to Y_R\). It is valid when \(\phi_R(\iota_R(x))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_R\). Consequently, the reported value \(L(R)=\inf_{y\in Y_R}\phi_R(y)\) satisfies \(L(R)\le\inf_{x\in F_R}f(x)\). If the relaxation solver returns only a certified value \(\widehat L(R)\le L(R)\), then \(\widehat L(R)\) is also a valid regional lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regional relaxation is valid when every feasible regional point embeds into the relaxation without increasing its objective, making the relaxation optimum a certified lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F_R\subseteq R\).
The original problem is a minimization problem.
The reported relaxation value is solved or bounded with certified direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat L(R)\le L(R)\le\inf_{x\in F_R}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: feasible set restricted to region R

children.title: Regional Feasible-Search Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Node-local connections to feasible-point discovery, repair, and incumbent improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Regional Feasible-Search Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contract for regional candidate generation, repair, validation, and incumbent improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a region \(R\), problem data, and incumbent value \(U\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\). A regional feasible-search interface generates a trial point \(z\in R\), optionally applies a repair map \(P_R\) to obtain \(x=P_R(z)\in R\), and invokes a feasibility validator. If the validator certifies \(x\in F_R\) and returns a certified objective upper enclosure \(\overline f(x)\), update \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,\overline f(x)\}\) and return \(x\); otherwise retain \(U\). Stopping may be triggered by a prescribed evaluation, iteration, or time budget, but an uncertified trial never changes the incumbent bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface generates or repairs regional candidates, validates feasibility and objective value, and updates the incumbent only with a certified feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(F_R\subseteq R\).
The validator is sound.
The objective enclosure satisfies \(f(x)\le\overline f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_{\mathrm{new}}=\min\{U,\overline f(x)\}\) only when \(x\in F_R\) is certified; otherwise \(U_{\mathrm{new}}=U\).

children.title: Regional Lower-Bound Families

children.title: Convex-Relaxation Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds supplied by convexification, outer approximation, and related relaxation families.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Relaxation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds obtained from convex outer approximations of regional epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_R\) be the feasible set in region \(R\), and define its objective epigraph \(E_R=\{(x,t):x\in F_R,\ t\ge f(x)\}\). If \(C_R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\) is convex and satisfies \(E_R\subseteq C_R\), then \(L_C(R)=\inf\{t:(x,t)\in C_R\}\) is a valid lower bound on the regional optimum \(p_R=\inf_{x\in F_R}f(x)\). For two valid relaxations satisfying \(C_R^{(1)}\subseteq C_R^{(2)}\), the tighter relaxation gives the stronger bound: \(L_{C^{(1)}}(R)\ge L_{C^{(2)}}(R)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing over a convex outer approximation of the regional epigraph gives a lower bound; a smaller valid outer approximation yields a bound at least as strong.
assumptions_latex: \(E_R\subseteq C_R\).
\(C_R\) is convex.
The relaxation infimum is interpreted in the extended real line.

children.title: Enclosure-Regularity Bound Family
children.top_down_role: Bounds supplied by interval enclosures, Lipschitz information, and other regional regularity models.

children.title: Interval-Enclosure Bounds
children.top_down_role: Regional lower bounds supplied by validated interval enclosures.

knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Enclosure Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional lower bounds from inclusion-monotone interval extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=[\ell,u]\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a box and let \(F(B)=[\underline F(B),\overline F(B)]\) be an interval extension of \(f:B\to\mathbb{R}\). If \(f(x)\in F(B)\) for every \(x\in B\), then \(\underline F(B)\le\inf_{x\in B}f(x)\). If feasibility restricts the region to \(S_B\subseteq B\), the same endpoint remains valid: \(\underline F(B)\le\inf_{x\in S_B}f(x)\), provided \(S_B\ne\varnothing\). Under an inclusion-monotone extension, \(B_1\subseteq B_2\) implies \(F(B_1)\subseteq F(B_2)\), so subdivision cannot decrease the lower endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower endpoint of an interval containing every objective value on a box is a valid regional lower bound, and inclusion monotonicity strengthens it under subdivision.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a nonempty compact box.
\(F(B)\) encloses \(f(B)\).
For the monotonicity claim, the interval extension is inclusion-monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline F(B)\le\inf_{x\in S_B}f(x)\), and \(B_1\subseteq B_2\) implies \(\underline F(B_1)\ge\underline F(B_2)\).

children.title: Regularity-Based Bounds
children.top_down_role: Regional lower bounds supplied by Lipschitz or related regularity information.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularity-Based Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz lower bounds centered at an evaluated regional point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be nonempty, let \(c\in R\), and suppose \(f:R\to\mathbb{R}\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz with respect to a norm \(\|\cdot\|\), where \(L\ge0\). Define \(\rho_R(c)=\sup_{x\in R}\|x-c\|\). Then every \(x\in R\) satisfies \(f(x)\ge f(c)-L\|x-c\|\ge f(c)-L\rho_R(c)\). Hence \(L_{\mathrm{reg}}(R)=f(c)-L\rho_R(c)\) is a regional lower bound. The conclusion remains valid for a feasible subset \(F_R\subseteq R\), with its optimum replacing the unconstrained regional infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lipschitz constant, one evaluated point, and the region’s radius give the lower bound equal to the center value minus constant times radius.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(R\).
\(c\in R\).
\(\rho_R(c)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(c)-L\rho_R(c)\le\inf_{x\in F_R}f(x)\) for every nonempty \(F_R\subseteq R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Lipschitz-radius lower bound is mathematically precise and fits the container, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Hybrid Enclosure-Regularity Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bound constructions combining enclosure information with regional regularity estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Enclosure-Regularity Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combination of independently valid interval and regularity lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be a regional domain. Suppose \(L_{\mathrm{enc}}(R)\) is an enclosure-derived bound and \(L_{\mathrm{reg}}(R)\) is a regularity-derived bound, each satisfying \(L_i(R)\le p_R\), where \(p_R=\inf_{x\in F_R}f(x)\). Then the hybrid value \(L_{\mathrm{hyb}}(R)=\max\{L_{\mathrm{enc}}(R),L_{\mathrm{reg}}(R)\}\) is valid and dominates both component bounds. More generally, the maximum of any finite family of valid regional lower bounds is valid. No independence between the bounding procedures is required; validity of every component for the same regional feasible problem is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking the maximum of valid enclosure and regularity lower bounds preserves validity and is never weaker than either component bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F_R\ne\varnothing\).
\(L_{\mathrm{enc}}(R)\le p_R\).
\(L_{\mathrm{reg}}(R)\le p_R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{L_{\mathrm{enc}}(R),L_{\mathrm{reg}}(R)\}\le p_R\).

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Algorithms Based on Interval Methods p. 46

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Algorithms Based on Interval Methods p. 46

children.title: Dual-Decomposition Bound Family
children.top_down_role: Bounds supplied by Lagrangian, decomposition, and structured dual constructions.

children.title: Lagrangian Dual Bounds
children.top_down_role: Regional bounds obtained from Lagrangian dual constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Dual Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality lower bound for a regionally restricted minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X_R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(f:X_R	o\mathbb{R}\), \(g:X_R	o\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(h:X_R	o\mathbb{R}^q\). Define \(p_R=\inf\{f(x):x\in X_R,\ g(x)\le0,\ h(x)=0\}\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) and \(
u\in\mathbb{R}^q\), define \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda,
u)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)+
u^{\mathsf T}h(x)\) and \(d_R(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in X_R}\mathcal L(x,\lambda,
u)\). Then \(d_R(\lambda,
u)\le p_R\). Consequently, \(d_R^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m,
u\in\mathbb{R}^q}d_R(\lambda,
u)\le p_R\), without requiring convexity or strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a regionally restricted minimization problem, every nonnegative inequality multiplier and unrestricted equality multiplier produces a Lagrangian lower bound, and optimizing these bounds preserves validity without requiring convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(X_R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(f:X_R\to\mathbb{R}\), \(g:X_R\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(h:X_R\to\mathbb{R}^q\).
Inequalities use \(g(x)\le0\), with \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_R(\lambda,\nu)\le d_R^*\le p_R\).

source_refs.locator: 8. Dual Methods in Reverse Convex Programming p. 181

source_witnesses.locator: 8. Dual Methods in Reverse Convex Programming p. 181

children.title: Decomposition Bounds
children.top_down_role: Regional bounds assembled through separable or block-structured decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable Lagrangian bound for block-structured regional problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,r\in\mathbb{N}\). For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(X_{i,R}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\), \(f_i:X_{i,R}\to\mathbb{R}\), and \(A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n_i}\), and let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^r\). Define \(p_R=\inf\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_{i,R},\ \sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\}\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^r\), define \(D_R(\lambda)=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_{i=1}^m\inf_{x_i\in X_{i,R}}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_i x_i\bigr)\). The block infima are separable, and weak duality gives \(D_R(\lambda)\le p_R\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^r\). Hence \(\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^r}D_R(\lambda)\le p_R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing the coupling equality separates the regional problem into independent block infima, and their Lagrangian dual value is a valid regional lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X_{i,R}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) and \(f_i:X_{i,R}\to\mathbb{R}\) for every block \(i\).
The objective is block-separable and the coupling constraint is \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\).
All infima are interpreted in the extended real line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_R(\lambda)\le p_R\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^r\), and \(\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^r}D_R(\lambda)\le p_R\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 3. The GOP Primal-Relaxed Dual Decomposition Approach: Theory p. 67

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 3. The GOP Primal-Relaxed Dual Decomposition Approach: Theory p. 67

children.title: Structured Dual-Decomposition Bounds
children.top_down_role: Interfaces coupling structured dual information with decomposed regional subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Dual-Decomposition Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual decomposition combining block structure with valid local underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the regional problem minimize \(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(x_i\in X_{i,R}\) and \(Bx=0\), with block columns \(B_i\). Suppose \(q_{i,R}(x_i)\le f_i(x_i)\) on \(X_{i,R}\). For \(\lambda\) compatible with the coupling equations, define \(D_R^q(\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^m\inf_{x_i\in X_{i,R}}\bigl(q_{i,R}(x_i)+(B_i^{\mathsf T}\lambda)^{\mathsf T}x_i\bigr)\). Then \(D_R^q(\lambda)\le p_R\), and maximizing over \(\lambda\) preserves the bound. Thus local convexification or enclosure can be composed with coupling dualization without sacrificing validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid block underestimators can be combined with dualized coupling constraints; the resulting separable dual objective remains a regional lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(q_{i,R}(x_i)\le f_i(x_i)\) on every block domain.
Feasible points satisfy \(Bx=0\).
All block infima are certified from below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\lambda}D_R^q(\lambda)\le p_R\).

notation.meaning: valid regional underestimator for block i

children.title: Incumbent Upper Bound
children.top_down_role: Validated feasible-objective information used for cutoffs and proof-gap control.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: αBB rectangle-search procedure for protein folding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes the bound-update, subdivision, pruning, selection, and stopping logic; named solvers and energy evaluators are implementation interfaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original bounded domain be a rectangle \(R_0\), let \(f\) be the total energy objective, and for each current rectangle \(R\) let \(L_R\) be a convex lower-bounding function. Obtain a feasible local minimizer of \(f\) in \(R\) and use its total energy, including the selected solvation contribution when applicable, as an upper bound; update the incumbent \(U\) to the smallest stored upper bound. Partition \(R\), for example by bisection, and minimize \(L_{R'}\) on every child rectangle \(R'\). Fathom \(R'\) when its resulting lower-bound value is strictly greater than \(U\), and otherwise retain it. Select a retained rectangle having minimum lower-bound value for further partitioning. With \(B\) denoting the best current lower bound, terminate when \(U-B\leq\epsilon\); otherwise repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a bounded rectangular domain, find a feasible local energy minimum to obtain an upper bound and retain the best such bound. Subdivide the current rectangle, minimize a convex lower-bounding model on each child, discard a child whose lower bound is strictly greater than the incumbent upper bound, and next subdivide a retained child with minimum lower bound. Stop when the best upper and lower bounds differ by at most epsilon; otherwise repeat. The applicable hydration contribution is included in the evaluated total energy.
assumptions_latex: R_0\text{ is a bounded rectangle defined by the original variable bounds.}
L_R(x)\leq f(x)\quad\text{for all }x\in R\text{ and every processed rectangle }R.
\text{Each local-solver candidate used to update }U\text{ is feasible for its rectangle.}
\epsilon\geq 0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{R'}>U\implies R'\text{ may be fathomed},\qquad U-B\leq\epsilon\implies\text{termination}.

children.title: Incumbent Generation
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for local optimization, repair, rounding, diving, and neighborhood search.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generation and acceptance of improving feasible solutions during spatial search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an active region \(R\), incumbent value \(U\), and a finite search budget. Generate trial points by one or more prescribed operators: local optimization from a regional seed, constraint repair, discrete rounding, a fixing-based dive, or neighborhood search. For each trial \(z\), construct a candidate \(x\in R\) and invoke the incumbent validator. If it certifies \(x\in F_R\) and a value \(\overline f(x)<U\), set \(U\leftarrow\overline f(x)\) and store \(x\); otherwise discard the candidate as an incumbent. Stop when the budget is exhausted and output the best validated pair, or the original incumbent if none improves it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regional heuristics generate candidates by local search, repair, rounding, diving, or neighborhoods; only validated improving candidates replace the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
Every accepted objective value is a certified upper enclosure.
The search budget is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_{\mathrm{out}}\le U_{\mathrm{in}}\), and any strict decrease is supported by a validated feasible point.

children.title: Incumbent Validation
children.top_down_role: Feasibility and numerical-status checks governing whether a candidate may define a global upper bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound certificate permitting a candidate to define a global upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization problem with domain \(D\), inequalities \(g_j(x)\le0\), and equalities \(h_k(x)=0\), an incumbent certificate for a candidate \(x\) consists of verifiable assertions \(x\in D\), \(g_j(x)\le0\) for every \(j\), and \(h_k(x)=0\) for every \(k\), together with a certified enclosure \(f(x)\le\overline f(x)\). Exact arithmetic, directed interval evaluation, or another sound validation mechanism may supply these assertions. Once validated, \(U=\overline f(x)\) is a global upper bound on the optimal value. Tolerance-only residual tests do not provide this conclusion unless the optimization problem explicitly defines tolerance-feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate becomes an incumbent only after sound domain and constraint checks plus a certified objective upper enclosure; residual tolerances alone do not certify exact feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
All feasibility assertions use a sound validation mechanism.
The certified objective enclosure satisfies \(f(x)\le\overline f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*\le f(x)\le\overline f(x)=U\).

notation.meaning: certified upper enclosure of the objective

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and upper-bound implication are coherent, but no authoritative source is supplied for the sound numerical-validation requirements or the distinction between exact and tolerance-defined feasibility.

children.title: Incumbent Cutoff Feedback
children.top_down_role: Reuse of improved primal information in reduction, relaxation strengthening, and fathoming.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Cutoff Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization cutoff feedback in a valid spatial branch-and-bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be the objective value of a validated feasible incumbent and let a search region \(R\) have valid lower bound \(L(R)\). Replacing \(U\) by an improved value \(U'\le U\) permits every regional relaxation and contractor to include the cutoff \(f(x)\le U'\). Any region satisfying \(L(R)\ge U'\) may then be fathomed without losing a strictly improving feasible point. Cutoff-derived contractions must remain valid supersets of \(\{x\in R:x\text{ is feasible},\ f(x)<U'\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A better feasible incumbent strengthens cutoff propagation and allows every region whose lower bound reaches the incumbent value to be safely discarded.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is minimized over a feasible set \(F\).
\(U'=f(\bar x)\) for some validated \(\bar x\in F\).
\(L(R)\le \inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap R\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(R)\ge U'\Longrightarrow \nexists x\in F\cap R\text{ with }f(x)<U'\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound on region R

children.title: Global Dual Bound
children.top_down_role: Search-wide aggregation of valid bounds from unresolved regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Dual Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-wide lower bound for a minimization problem with an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be the current incumbent value and let \(\mathcal A\) be the finite family of unresolved regions. For each \(R\in\mathcal A\), let \(L(R)\) be a valid lower bound on feasible objective values in \(R\). With \(\min\varnothing=+\infty\), the global dual bound is \(D=\min\{U,\min_{R\in\mathcal A}L(R)\}\). If every feasible point better than \(U\) lies in some active region, then \(D\le f^*\le U\). Consequently, \(U-D\) is a valid absolute optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global dual bound is the smaller of the incumbent value and the least valid lower bound among all unresolved regions.
assumptions_latex: \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\) is finite.
\(L(R)\le\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)\) for every \(R\in\mathcal A\).
\(\{x\in F:f(x)<U\}\subseteq\bigcup_{R\in\mathcal A}R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D=\min\{U,\min_{R\in\mathcal A}L(R)\}\le f^*\le U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Partition–Relaxation Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone lower-bound strengthening under compatible regional subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a parent region \(R\) is replaced by children \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) whose union covers \(R\). Let \(Q(R)\) and \(Q(R_i)\) be relaxation feasible sets, with objective \(f_{\mathrm{rel}}\), such that \(Q(R_i)\subseteq Q(R)\) and \(F\cap R_i\subseteq Q(R_i)\). Defining \(L(R)=\inf_{x\in Q(R)}f_{\mathrm{rel}}(x)\), each child satisfies \(L(R_i)\ge L(R)\); hence the replacement bound \(\min_i L(R_i)\) cannot be weaker than the parent bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When child relaxations are valid restrictions of the parent relaxation, subdivision can only maintain or improve the aggregate regional lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(R=\bigcup_{i=1}^m R_i\).
\(F\cap R_i\subseteq Q(R_i)\subseteq Q(R)\).
\(L(S)=\inf_{x\in Q(S)}f_{\mathrm{rel}}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{1\le i\le m}L(R_i)\ge L(R)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Search Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone gap feedback in deterministic minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(U_k\) be the best validated feasible value and let \(D_k\) be the global dual bound. Incumbent discovery updates \(U_{k+1}\le U_k\); valid contraction, fathoming, and child replacement satisfying bound monotonicity update \(D_{k+1}\ge D_k\). Node priorities may use regional gaps \(U_k-L(R)\), so either primal or dual improvement changes subsequent selection. If \(U_k-D_k\le\varepsilon\), the incumbent is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal in absolute objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal improvements lower the incumbent, dual progress raises the global lower bound, and their gap drives priorities and certifies termination.
assumptions_latex: \(D_k\le f^*\le U_k\) for every iteration \(k\).
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k-D_k\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow 0\le U_k-f^*\le\varepsilon\).

children.title: Forward Range Propagation

knowledge_statements.title: Forward Range Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outward-rounded interval evaluation on an acyclic expression graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an acyclic expression graph with input intervals \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), process its noninput nodes in topological order. If node \(v\) represents an operation \(\phi_v\) with predecessor intervals \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_p\), assign \(Y_v\leftarrow Y_v\cap[\phi_v](Y_1,\ldots,Y_p)\), where \([\phi_v]\) is an outward-rounded inclusion function. Stop with infeasibility if an intersection is empty; otherwise output the interval at every node. Every value generated by any input \(x_i\in X_i\) remains contained in its corresponding propagated interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate the expression graph from inputs to outputs with inclusion-preserving interval operations, intersecting existing ranges and detecting empty ranges.
assumptions_latex: The expression graph is finite and acyclic.
Each \([\phi_v]\) encloses \(\phi_v\) on its argument intervals.
All interval arithmetic is outward rounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i\in X_i\ \forall i\Longrightarrow v(x)\in Y_v\) for every graph node \(v\).

children.title: Reverse Range Propagation

knowledge_statements.title: Reverse Range Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound backward contraction through an expression graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After forward propagation, process noninput nodes in reverse topological order. For each relation \(y=\phi_v(z_1,\ldots,z_p)\), replace every predecessor interval \(Z_j\) by \(Z_j\cap C_{v,j}(Y,Z_1,\ldots,Z_p)\), where \(C_{v,j}\) encloses all \(z_j\) extendable to arguments satisfying \(\phi_v(z)=y\) for some \(y\in Y\). Repeat forward and reverse sweeps until no material contraction occurs or an interval becomes empty. The final input box contains every original input consistent with the restricted root range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate an output restriction backward through inverse relation contractors, alternating with forward evaluation until stable or infeasibility is detected.
assumptions_latex: Forward node ranges are valid enclosures.
Each inverse contractor \(C_{v,j}\) is solution preserving.
The root interval encodes the required output range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in X:v_{\mathrm{root}}(x)\in Y_{\mathrm{root}}\}\subseteq X'\subseteq X\).

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Row Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds-consistency update for one linear inequality over a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the row \(\sum_{j=1}^n a_jx_j\le b\) with \(x_j\in[\ell_j,u_j]\), compute \(r_i=b-\sum_{j\ne i}\min\{a_j\ell_j,a_ju_j\}\) for each \(a_i\ne0\). If \(a_i>0\), update \(u_i\leftarrow\min\{u_i,r_i/a_i\}\); if \(a_i<0\), update \(\ell_i\leftarrow\max\{\ell_i,r_i/a_i\}\). Declare infeasibility when some \(\ell_i>u_i\), and repeat until stable. An equality row is propagated by applying the rule to both inequality orientations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each variable bound is tightened using the smallest possible contribution of all other terms in the linear row.
assumptions_latex: \(x_j\in[\ell_j,u_j]\) for \(j=1,\ldots,n\).
The row is \(\sum_j a_jx_j\le b\).
Arithmetic updates are conservatively rounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in[\ell,u]:a^Tx\le b\}\subseteq[\ell',u']\subseteq[\ell,u]\).

Iterate forward enclosure and row updates until stable or until a domain is empty. Every tuple satisfying the affine relation is preserved.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Row-Expression Propagation

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity-Based Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility contraction using certified derivative signs on a current box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a constraint \(g(x)\le 0\) on a box \(B=\prod_i X_i\), suppose interval differentiation certifies that \(g\) is nondecreasing in \(x_i\) throughout \(B\). Define a certified slice lower bound \(L_i(t)\le\inf\{g(x):x\in B,\ x_i=t\}\). Remove every terminal upper subinterval \(T\subseteq X_i\) for which \(L_i(\inf T)>0\). For a nonincreasing coordinate, analogously remove terminal lower intervals using the corresponding endpoint. Repeat after each contraction; if the retained coordinate interval is empty, reject \(B\). Equality constraints apply the rule to both \(g\le0\) and \(-g\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified derivative sign lets the propagator discard an endpoint region whose best possible constraint value is already infeasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagator Scheduling Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fair worklist scheduling for a finite family of contracting propagators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}\) be contracting, solution-preserving propagators on boxes. Initialize a worklist \(W\) with every propagator. Repeatedly select an element according to a scheduling policy \(\sigma(W,B)\), apply it to the current box \(B\), and enqueue every propagator whose watched inputs changed materially. Stop when \(W\) is empty or \(B=\varnothing\). The policy is fair if every propagator that remains continuously eligible is eventually selected. FIFO, round-robin, and priority selection are admissible provided fairness is retained; scheduling changes execution order but not the validity of any individual contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fair scheduler repeatedly runs eligible solution-preserving propagators and requeues affected ones until the worklist empties or infeasibility is found.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is finite.
Every propagator is contracting and solution preserving.
Reactivation tests do not permanently suppress a materially affected propagator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every intermediate box preserves all solutions in the initial box, and a fair empty-worklist termination is propagation-stable under the adopted triggers.

children.title: Propagator Reactivation Triggers

knowledge_statements.title: Propagator Reactivation Triggers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency-based condition for returning a propagator to the worklist.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each propagator \(p\), let \(R_p\) be the set of domains it reads and let \(S_p\subseteq R_p\) be an optional watched subset. After a box update from \(B\) to \(B'\subseteq B\), reactivate \(p\) whenever \[\exists i\in S_p:\quad X_i'\subsetneq X_i\quad\text{and}\quad \Delta(X_i,X_i')>\tau_i,\] where \(\Delta\) measures the relevant bound change and \(\tau_i\ge0\) is its trigger tolerance. A sound watched-set design must ensure that any unobserved domain change cannot strengthen the contraction computed by \(p\); otherwise one must take \(S_p=R_p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requeue a propagator when a watched input contracts beyond tolerance, unless dependency analysis proves that the ignored change cannot strengthen it.
assumptions_latex: Each propagator declares the domains it reads.
The change measure and tolerance are fixed for the current propagation regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trigger is closure-safe when watched-set omissions are certified irrelevant to the propagator output.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Worklist Priorities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Priority queue rule favoring propagators with larger predicted contraction benefit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each eligible propagator \(p\) a finite score \[q_p=w_1a_p+w_2c_p-w_3d_p,\] where \(a_p\) is a recency or activity estimate, \(c_p\) estimates attainable contraction, \(d_p\) estimates evaluation cost, and \(w_k\ge0\). Extract a maximum-score propagator, apply it, update affected scores, and enqueue newly triggered propagators. Break ties by insertion age. To preserve fairness, promote any item waiting more than \(H<\infty\) extractions above all non-overdue items. Stop when the queue is empty or the box is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prioritize predicted high-impact, low-cost propagators, while an aging rule prevents any continuously eligible propagator from starving.
assumptions_latex: All priority scores and cost estimates are finite.
A finite aging threshold \(H\) is enforced.
Applied propagators are solution preserving.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy is fair and preserves the soundness of propagation while altering only execution order.

children.title: Propagation Stabilization

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate common-fixed-point condition under absolute and relative bound tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a finite propagator family and \(B=\prod_i[\ell_i,u_i]\). For tolerances \(\varepsilon_i^{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_i^{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\), define \(B\) to be propagation-stable when, for every \(p\in P\), writing \(p(B)=\prod_i[\ell_i^p,u_i^p]\), \[\max\{\ell_i^p-\ell_i,\ u_i-u_i^p\}\le \varepsilon_i^{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_i^{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|\ell_i|,|u_i|\}\quad\text{for every }i.\] With zero tolerances this is a common fixed point. A worklist implementation may terminate at this condition if all propagators have been tested after the last material update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagation is stable when no propagator can improve any bound beyond its combined absolute-relative tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Each \(p\in P\) maps boxes to subboxes.
All box endpoints are finite.
Every propagator has been tested after the last material contraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No single propagator produces a bound improvement exceeding the prescribed tolerance at \(B\).

Relative stabilization tolerance for coordinate i.

children.title: Propagation Tolerance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerical thresholds governing material contraction and closure.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Tolerance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact, absolute, relative, and mixed regimes for recognizing material contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an old interval \(X=[\ell,u]\) and contracted interval \(X'=[\ell',u']\subseteq X\), define the bound gain \(g(X,X')=\max\{\ell'-\ell,u-u'\}\). An exact regime declares material change iff \(g(X,X')>0\). An absolute regime uses \(g(X,X')>\varepsilon^{\mathrm{abs}}\); a relative regime uses \(g(X,X')>\varepsilon^{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|\ell|,|u|\}\); and a mixed regime uses the sum of these thresholds. Coordinate-dependent tolerances are permitted. These tests govern reactivation or termination only and must not enlarge a contracted interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tolerance regimes classify a bound contraction as material using exact, absolute, relative, or combined thresholds without changing the contracted domain itself.
assumptions_latex: \(X'\subseteq X\) and all endpoints are finite.
All tolerances are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each regime defines a reproducible predicate for material interval contraction.

notation.meaning: Largest inward movement of either interval endpoint.

review_flags: Tolerance conventions vary across solvers and require a selected authoritative specification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the tolerance-regimes leaf, but the exact gain measure, scaling convention, and material-change predicates are solver-dependent and have no supporting source.

children.title: Tolerance-Induced Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Regimes where numerical thresholds obscure useful progress or prolong repeated passes.

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Induced Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Premature closure caused by suppressing individually small but cumulatively significant contractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an absolute trigger tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). On the scalar interval \(X_0=[0,1]\), consider a sound contracting update \(p([0,u])=[0,\max\{0,u-\delta\}]\) with \(0<\delta\le\varepsilon\). If reactivation or iteration stops whenever a single endpoint movement is at most \(\varepsilon\), propagation halts after at most one application, although repeated exact applications reach \([0,0]\) after \(\lceil1/\delta\rceil\) steps. Thus per-update tolerance suppression can prevent attainment of the exact propagation fixed point even when every update is sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every useful contraction is smaller than the trigger tolerance, propagation may stop far from the fixed point despite large cumulative possible reduction.
assumptions_latex: The stopping test considers only the most recent endpoint movement.
\(0<\delta\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tolerance-based termination need not imply an exact common fixed point.
review_flags: Concrete countermechanism is self-contained, but an external source is required by the evidence contract.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary classification is correct and the countermechanism is self-contained, but no evidence record or cited source supports its inclusion as candidate-review knowledge.

children.title: Optimization-Based Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Contraction obtained from auxiliary optimization over valid regional relaxations.

children.title: Full-Variable Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Systematic tightening of both sides of selected variable domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Variable Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-based tightening of both bounds of every selected variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) be the feasible set and let \(R\) be a tractable relaxation satisfying \(F\subseteq R\subseteq B\). For every selected coordinate \(i\), solve globally over \(R\) the two problems \[L_i=\inf_{x\in R}x_i,\qquad U_i=\sup_{x\in R}x_i.\] Replace \(X_i\) by \(X_i'=[\max\{\ell_i,L_i\},\min\{u_i,U_i\}]\), using valid outward rounding or certified optimization bounds. If any subproblem proves \(R=\varnothing\), reject the box; otherwise output the simultaneously or sequentially updated box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each chosen variable, minimize and maximize it over a valid relaxation, then intersect its domain with the certified extrema.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\subseteq B\).
Each extremum or optimization bound is globally valid.
Endpoint updates use safe numerical rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated box contains \(F\), and an empty relaxation certifies that \(B\) contains no feasible point.

notation.meaning: Feasible set within the current box.
Tractable relaxation containing the feasible set.
Relaxation-based lower and upper extrema of coordinate i.

review_flags: The supplied source locators do not specifically identify optimization-based bound tightening.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits full-variable optimization-based bound tightening and its containment directions are sound, but no cited locator supports the OBBT formulation, certified extrema requirements, or infeasibility conclusion.

children.title: Priority-Driven Selective Tightening
children.top_down_role: Target selection based on width, relaxation impact, activity, or search context.

children.title: Selective Target Tightening
children.top_down_role: Restriction of auxiliary tightening solves to chosen variables or bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Selective Target Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-based bound tightening restricted to a chosen coordinate-side target set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation \(F\subseteq R\subseteq B\) and a target set \(T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{-,+\}\), process only the listed coordinate sides. For \((i,-)\in T\), compute a certified lower bound \(L_i\le\inf_{x\in R}x_i\) and set \(\ell_i\leftarrow\max\{\ell_i,L_i\}\). For \((i,+)\in T\), compute a certified upper bound \(U_i\ge\sup_{x\in R}x_i\) and set \(u_i\leftarrow\min\{u_i,U_i\}\). Untargeted sides remain unchanged. Reject the box if an updated interval is empty or the relaxation is certified infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run bound-tightening subproblems only for selected variable sides, preserving untargeted sides and rejecting the box when certified infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\subseteq B\).
All optimization bounds used for updates are globally valid.
The target set \(T\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selective tightening preserves every point in \(F\) while limiting optimization effort to \(T\).
review_flags: Selective OBBT formulation needs a directly supporting source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm correctly targets selected coordinate sides and uses safe relaxation-bound directions, but selective OBBT and its certification semantics lack a directly supporting source.

children.title: Priority-Scored Tightening
children.top_down_role: Ranking of tightening targets by width, impact, activity, or search context.

knowledge_statements.title: Priority-Scored Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted selection of bound-tightening targets using estimated benefit and cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each candidate target \(t=(i,s)\), maintain nonnegative estimates \(b_t\) of expected bound improvement, \(r_t\) of downstream relaxation benefit, and \(c_t>0\) of computational cost. Define \[q_t=\frac{\alpha b_t+\beta r_t}{c_t},\qquad \alpha,\beta\ge0.\] Insert candidates into a maximum-priority queue, solve the tightening subproblem for the largest \(q_t\), apply any certified contraction, and debit its measured cost from a finite budget. Continue until the queue is empty, the box is infeasible, or the budget is exhausted. Scores determine selection only; they do not affect validity of computed bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank tightening targets by estimated contraction and downstream benefit per unit cost, then process the best targets within a finite budget.
assumptions_latex: Every applied bound update is independently certified.
\(c_t>0\) and all scores are finite.
The tightening budget is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a solution-preserving box regardless of score-prediction accuracy.
review_flags: The score is a formal policy template requiring a source or implementation specification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record belongs in the priority-scored tightening leaf, but its benefit-per-cost formula and budgeted selection procedure are an unsourced policy template rather than established cited knowledge.

children.title: Tightening Priority Refresh
children.top_down_role: Revision of target priorities as regional or search-wide information changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Tightening Priority Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven recomputation of target priorities after relaxation or domain changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_t(B,R,h_t)\) be the score of tightening target \(t\), depending on the current box \(B\), relaxation \(R\), and its history \(h_t\). After processing a target or materially changing a domain or relaxation constraint, mark every score whose dependency set intersects the changed data as stale. Before a stale target can be selected, recompute \(q_t\) from the current state and restore its queue position. Update \(h_t\) with realized contraction and cost. If eager refresh is not used, lazy refresh must revalidate the extracted maximum and repeat extraction until its score is current.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After relevant state changes, invalidate affected target scores and recompute them before selection so priorities reflect the current relaxation and observed performance.
assumptions_latex: Each score has a declared dependency set.
State changes and target histories are observable.
Only current scores may authorize target selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every selected target is maximal under the refreshed scores of the implemented eager or lazy queue policy.

notation.meaning: Dynamic priority score for target t.
Recorded cost and contraction history of target t.

review_flags: Refresh semantics are implementation-dependent and need a supporting source or project specification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits tightening-priority refresh, but dependency invalidation, history updates, and eager or lazy maximum revalidation are implementation-specific and unsupported by a source or project specification.

children.title: Relaxation Regimes for Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: LP, conic, nonlinear-convex, and mixed-integer auxiliary bounding interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Regimes for Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified optimization-based tightening interface for several relaxation classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=[l,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\), let \(F_B\) be the original feasible set in \(B\), and let \(U\) be a valid incumbent cutoff for minimization. Choose an auxiliary relaxation \(R_B\supseteq F_B\) and a relaxation objective \(\phi_B\) satisfying \(\phi_B(x)\le f(x)\) on \(F_B\). The interface may use an LP, conic, convex-nonlinear, or mixed-integer relaxation. For each coordinate \(i\), set \[l_i'=\min\{x_i:x\in R_B,\ \phi_B(x)\le U\},\qquad u_i'=\max\{x_i:x\in R_B,\ \phi_B(x)\le U\}.\] Infeasibility of either common restricted relaxation certifies that no improving feasible point remains in \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any valid relaxation class may tighten a coordinate by minimizing and maximizing it over the relaxation restricted by the incumbent cutoff.
assumptions_latex: \(F_B\subseteq R_B\).
\(\phi_B(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_B\).
\(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_B\cap\{x:f(x)\le U\}\subseteq[l',u']\subseteq B\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No inspectable citation supports the unified relaxation interface. Also, the conclusion [l',u']⊆B requires explicitly imposing R_B⊆B or intersecting the auxiliary coordinate optima with B.

children.title: Tightening Placement Regimes
children.top_down_role: Placement regimes balancing contraction strength against auxiliary-solve cost.

children.title: Root-Level Tightening
children.top_down_role: Concentrated tightening performed before substantial tree expansion.

knowledge_statements.title: Root-Level Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-based tightening performed once before spatial branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a root box \(B^0=[l^0,u^0]\), a valid relaxation \(R_{B^0}\), and an incumbent cutoff \(U\). Before branching, solve the selected auxiliary coordinate-minimization and coordinate-maximization problems over \(R_{B^0}\cap\{x:\phi_{B^0}(x)\le U\}\). Replace each root bound by the corresponding valid auxiliary optimum, iterating until a prescribed pass limit or bound-change tolerance is reached. If the restricted relaxation is infeasible, terminate the root as fathomed. Otherwise output the contracted root \(\widehat B^0\) and initialize every descendant domain by intersecting its branching restrictions with \(\widehat B^0\); do not rerun this tightening routine below the root.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tighten once at the root, then inherit the contracted bounds throughout the search tree without repeating the routine at descendants.
assumptions_latex: The auxiliary feasible region contains every root-feasible point with \(f(x)\le U\).
Auxiliary optima are globally valid for their relaxation.
Branching produces descendant boxes contained in \(B^0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every improving feasible descendant point belongs to \(\widehat B^0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard root preprocessing placement regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The root-only algorithm fits the terminal container and is mathematically plausible, but no source with a specific locator supports this placement regime or its prescribed inheritance behavior.

children.title: Node-Local Tightening
children.top_down_role: Tightening invoked within selected regional subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Local Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-based tightening recomputed for each processed search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At every processed node \(v\), input its box \(B^v\), current incumbent cutoff \(U\), and a valid node relaxation \(R_v\). Before bounding or branching, minimize and maximize selected coordinates over \(R_v\cap\{x:\phi_v(x)\le U\}\), replace \(B^v\) by the resulting coordinate hull \(\widehat B^v\), and rebuild any relaxation terms affected by changed bounds. Repeat until a pass limit or contraction tolerance is met. Fathom \(v\) if the restricted relaxation is infeasible or its lower bound exceeds \(U\); otherwise compute the node bound and branch from \(\widehat B^v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute valid bound tightening from the current relaxation at every processed node before bounding and branching.
assumptions_latex: \(R_v\) contains all original feasible points in \(B^v\).
\(\phi_v\) lower-bounds the original objective on node-feasible points.
Each relaxation rebuild preserves validity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap B^v\cap\{x:f(x)\le U\}\subseteq\widehat B^v\subseteq B^v\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard node-wise optimization-based tightening regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No inspectable source supports the node-local algorithm. The conclusion additionally uses F without introducing it, so the eventual sourced version should define the original feasible set explicitly.

children.title: Periodic Retightening
children.top_down_role: Tightening revisited at scheduled search intervals or milestones.

knowledge_statements.title: Periodic Retightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tightening scheduled at selected nodes rather than only once or everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a node-selection schedule \(S\), such as depths divisible by an integer \(q\ge1\), and a contraction tolerance \(\tau\ge0\). Process each node \(v\) using inherited valid bounds. If \(v\in S\), run valid optimization-based bound tightening on its current relaxation, update the node box and affected relaxation terms, and repeat while the maximum relative bound change exceeds \(\tau\) and the pass limit is not reached. If \(v\notin S\), omit the auxiliary solves. Fathom any scheduled node whose cutoff-restricted relaxation is infeasible; otherwise bound and branch from the current contracted box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run bound tightening only at nodes selected by a fixed depth, count, or contraction-trigger schedule.
assumptions_latex: Every scheduled tightening operation preserves all improving feasible points.
The schedule \(S\) is fixed or determined from information available at the node.
Relaxations are updated after material bound changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No point in \(F\cap B^v\cap\{x:f(x)\le U\}\) is removed at any scheduled node \(v\).

notation.meaning: set of nodes scheduled for retightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the periodic placement regime. The conclusion uses F, B^v, U, and f without introducing them in the statement, and the relative-bound-change measure is not defined.

children.title: Dual-Sensitivity Tightening Family
children.top_down_role: Contraction driven by relaxation sensitivity, multipliers, and incumbent cutoffs.

children.title: Reduced-Cost Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Contraction using relaxation reduced costs and valid cutoff information.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP reduced-cost contraction under a valid incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an LP relaxation with optimum \(z_L\) and a valid dual certificate implying \[c^Tx\ge z_L+r_j(x_j-l_j)\] for every relaxation-feasible \(x\), where \(r_j>0\) and the optimal LP solution has \(x_j=l_j\). Every feasible point capable of meeting cutoff \(U\) then satisfies \[x_j\le l_j+\frac{U-z_L}{r_j}.\] Symmetrically, if a certificate gives \(c^Tx\ge z_L+(-r_j)(u_j-x_j)\) with \(r_j<0\) at \(x_j=u_j\), then \(x_j\ge u_j-(U-z_L)/(-r_j)\). The derived bound is intersected with the current interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero reduced cost converts the incumbent gap into a valid displacement limit from an active variable bound.
assumptions_latex: The LP is a valid relaxation of the node problem.
\(z_L\le U\), with \(U\) a valid incumbent cutoff.
The displayed reduced-cost inequality is certified by a dual-feasible LP solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated upper or lower bound retains every relaxation-feasible point satisfying \(c^Tx\le U\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard reduced-cost fixing and tightening inequality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost inequalities are consistent with standard LP reduced-cost tightening and the content kind fits, but no authoritative source and locator are supplied for the sign conventions and resulting bounds.

children.title: Lagrangian Range Reduction
children.top_down_role: Contraction derived from valid multipliers and regional dual information.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Range Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range contraction from a valid Lagrangian lower function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the node constraints include \(g(x)\le0\), and choose multipliers \(\lambda\ge0\). Define the Lagrangian lower function \(L_\lambda(x)=f(x)+\lambda^Tg(x)\). For every original feasible \(x\), \(L_\lambda(x)\le f(x)\); hence any feasible point satisfying the incumbent cutoff \(f(x)\le U\) belongs to \(D_\lambda=B\cap\{x:L_\lambda(x)\le U\}\). Consequently, each coordinate may be contracted to \[\left[\inf_{x\in D_\lambda}x_i,\ \sup_{x\in D_\lambda}x_i\right].\] Any certified lower bound greater than \(U\) for \(L_\lambda\) on a subregion excludes that subregion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative constraint multipliers yield a Lagrangian lower function whose cutoff sublevel set safely contains all improving feasible points.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with constraints \(g(x)\le0\).
\(\lambda\ge0\) is fixed and valid on the entire region \(B\).
\(U\) is a feasible incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap B\cap\{x:f(x)\le U\}\subseteq D_\lambda\), so the coordinate hull of \(D_\lambda\) is valid.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weak-duality contraction is plausible for g(x)≤0 and λ≥0, but no supporting citation is provided. The conclusion also uses F without defining it explicitly.

children.title: Dual Information Reuse Across Nodes
children.top_down_role: Inheritance and updating of sensitivity information along the search tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Information Reuse Across Nodes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for inheriting parent dual sensitivity certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let child node \(w\) have domain \(B^w\subseteq B^v\). A dual vector \(y^v\) from parent node \(v\) may be reused at \(w\) only if it remains feasible for the child's relaxation dual and its associated inequality \(\phi_w(x)\ge\beta(y^v,x)\) holds for every \(x\) feasible in the child relaxation. Under these conditions, cutoff or reduced-cost contractions derived from \(y^v\) remain valid on \(B^w\). If bound-dependent coefficients, convexification terms, or dual constraints change, dual feasibility and the bounding inequality must be rechecked or repaired before reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parent dual certificate is reusable at a child only when it remains dual feasible and its bounding inequality stays valid there.
assumptions_latex: \(B^w\subseteq B^v\).
The child relaxation and its dual are explicitly specified.
Any inherited cutoff remains valid at node \(w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual information is safely reusable exactly when child dual feasibility and the certified child bounding inequality are preserved.

notation.meaning: bound induced by the inherited certificate

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dual certificates require preserved feasibility under inheritance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the precise cross-node reuse conditions. The phrase “exactly when” overstates necessity unless reuse is narrowly defined as reuse of this same dual certificate; other arguments could validate a contraction even when this certificate is not child-dual feasible.

children.title: Restriction-Based Domain Inference
children.top_down_role: Temporary domain restrictions used to infer permanent contractions or exclusions.

children.title: Continuous-Domain Shaving
children.top_down_role: Testing subintervals and boundary slabs for removable regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Domain Shaving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-slab tests for continuous-variable domain contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a box \(B=[l,u]\), a coordinate \(i\), a shaving width \(\delta>0\), a valid relaxation operator \(R(\cdot)\), and cutoff \(U\). Test the lower slab \(S^- = B\cap\{x:x_i\le l_i+\delta\}\). If \(R(S^-)\cap\{x:\phi(x)\le U\}\) is certified infeasible, replace \(l_i\) by \(l_i+\delta\). Test the upper slab \(S^+ = B\cap\{x:x_i\ge u_i-\delta\}\) analogously and, upon certified infeasibility, replace \(u_i\) by \(u_i-\delta\). Repeat over selected coordinates and widths until no tested slab is removable or a stopping limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporarily restrict a variable to a boundary slab and remove that slab when valid inference proves it cannot contain an improving feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(R(S)\) contains every original feasible point in each tested slab \(S\).
\(\phi\) lower-bounds the objective on the tested relaxation.
Only certified infeasibility or a lower bound exceeding \(U\) triggers removal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every removed slab contains no point in \(F\cap\{x:f(x)\le U\}\).

notation.meaning: valid relaxation of a tested slab

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard continuous shaving by temporary slab restriction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shaving algorithm matches the container, but no inspectable citation supports it. The conclusion uses F without defining the original feasible set in the statement.

children.title: Integer-Value Probing
children.top_down_role: Temporary discrete restrictions and their propagated consequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Value Probing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporary integer assignments followed by valid propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a mixed-integer node domain, an integer variable \(x_i\), and a candidate value \(k\in[l_i,u_i]\cap\mathbb Z\). Temporarily impose \(x_i=k\), propagate all valid constraint and bound implications to a fixed point or prescribed limit, and evaluate feasibility. If propagation certifies infeasibility, delete \(k\) from the domain of \(x_i\). If probing implies a bound or relation \(C_k\), store it conditionally under \(x_i=k\); an implication common to every remaining candidate value may be installed unconditionally. Restore temporary state before probing another value, and stop after the selected values or resource limit are exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporarily fix an integer variable, propagate consequences, delete infeasible values, and retain only logically valid conditional or common implications.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\) is integer with finite current candidate set.
Every propagation rule is valid for the original node constraints under the temporary fixing.
A value is deleted only after certified infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deleting a probed value \(k\) preserves every feasible integer point of the node.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard integer probing and implication propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm correctly distinguishes conditional implications from implications established across all remaining values, but no source with a specific locator supports the probing procedure.

children.title: Relaxation-Assisted Probing
children.top_down_role: Probe evaluation through lower bounds, infeasibility detection, and relaxation changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Assisted Probing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction probing evaluated through valid relaxation information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a node domain \(B\), a temporary restriction \(P\), a valid relaxation \(R(B\cap P)\), and incumbent cutoff \(U\). Solve or bound the restricted relaxation. Reject \(P\) if the relaxation is certified infeasible or its certified lower bound exceeds \(U\). Otherwise compare its solution, dual certificate, and implied bounds with the unrestricted relaxation; retain only implications proved valid under \(P\), or implications valid across an exhaustive family of probes. Restore the original node state after each test. Output the reduced domain, conditional implications, and any valid relaxation modifications generated by the probes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate a temporary restriction with a valid relaxation, rejecting it by infeasibility or cutoff dominance and retaining only certified consequences.
assumptions_latex: \(R(B\cap P)\) contains all original feasible points satisfying \(P\).
Every reported lower bound is certified for the restricted relaxation.
\(U\) is a valid feasible incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A rejected probe contains no feasible point with objective at most \(U\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: valid relaxation inference under temporary restrictions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relaxation-assisted rejection rule is mathematically plausible and fits the algorithm container, but its lower-bound and implication-retention claims lack an inspectable citation.

children.title: Cutoff-Infeasibility Domain Reduction
children.top_down_role: Contraction or removal driven by objective cutoffs and regional infeasibility information.

children.title: Objective-Cutoff Range Reduction
children.top_down_role: Contraction to portions of a region still capable of improving the incumbent.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Cutoff Range Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contraction to the region capable of matching the incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem on a current region \(B\), let \(U\) be the objective value of a feasible incumbent. Every point capable of improving or matching the incumbent lies in \(F_U=F\cap B\cap\{x:f(x)\le U\}\). If a tractable function \(\underline f_B\) satisfies \(\underline f_B(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\cap B\), then \(F_U\subseteq D_U=B\cap\{x:\underline f_B(x)\le U\}\). Replacing each interval by \[\left[\inf_{x\in D_U}x_i,\ \sup_{x\in D_U}x_i\right]\] is therefore valid; an empty \(D_U\) permits fathoming.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect the region with a valid lower-estimator cutoff sublevel set and retain only its coordinate ranges.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(U\) is attained by a feasible incumbent.
\(\underline f_B\) is a valid lower estimator on all feasible points in \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_U\subseteq D_U\), so the coordinate hull of \(D_U\) preserves every point that can match or improve \(U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cutoff-sublevel inclusion is plausible and fits the terminal topic, but no supporting citation is supplied. The feasible set F should also be introduced explicitly in the eventual sourced statement.

children.title: Constraint-Infeasibility Exclusion
children.top_down_role: Removal of regions certified incompatible with the original constraint system.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Infeasibility Exclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate excluding a subregion using the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq B\) be a candidate subregion and let the original constraint system be \(g_j(x)\le0\) for \(j\in J\) and \(h_k(x)=0\) for \(k\in K\). A valid exclusion certificate is any finite, checkable derivation establishing that every \(x\in S\) violates at least one original constraint; equivalently, \[S\cap\{x:g_j(x)\le0\ \forall j\in J,\ h_k(x)=0\ \forall k\in K\}=\varnothing.\] Examples of certificate forms include a verified range bound \(\inf_{x\in S}g_j(x)>0\), an equality range excluding zero, or a sound infeasibility certificate for a restriction containing the original feasible set on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subregion may be removed when a checkable certificate proves that no point there satisfies the original constraint system.
assumptions_latex: All bounds used by the certificate are valid over the entire subregion \(S\).
The certified restriction does not exclude any original feasible point in \(S\).
Numerical comparisons include any required rigorous tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\cap F=\varnothing\), so deleting \(S\) cannot remove an original feasible solution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: infeasible-set exclusion by a sound constraint certificate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the exact container and the exclusion criterion is plausible, but no source supports the listed certificate forms. The conclusion uses F without explicitly defining it.

children.title: Relaxation-Infeasibility Exclusion
children.top_down_role: Removal of regions whose valid relaxation is infeasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Infeasibility Exclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe regional exclusion using an outer relaxation of the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a regional box, let \(F\) be the feasible set, and let \(R_B\) be a relaxation satisfying \(F\cap B\subseteq R_B\). If a reliable feasibility procedure certifies \(R_B=\varnothing\), then \(F\cap B=\varnothing\). Consequently, removing \(B\) from a spatial branch-and-bound search cannot remove any feasible point or global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region may be discarded when a valid outer relaxation is certified infeasible, because the original regional feasible set is then empty.
assumptions_latex: \(F\cap B\subseteq R_B\).
The reported infeasibility of \(R_B\) is rigorous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_B=\varnothing\Longrightarrow F\cap B=\varnothing\), so \(B\) is safely excluded.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is mathematically correct, matches the relaxation-infeasibility leaf, and uses appropriate content_kind, but no inspectable authoritative source and locator are supplied.

children.title: Domain-Reduction Safety Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Validity, numerical reliability, and cost-effectiveness limits of contraction mechanisms.

children.title: Verified Enclosure Rounding Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Safeguards for interval and propagation-based contractions.

children.title: Safe Regional Enclosures
children.top_down_role: Validated enclosure regimes supporting safe regional contraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Regional Enclosures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion condition required for rigorous interval-based regional bounds and exclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a box \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and function \(g:B\to\mathbb{R}\), a computed interval \(G(B)=[\underline g_B,\overline g_B]\) is safe precisely when \(g(B)=\{g(x):x\in B\}\subseteq G(B)\). Hence \(\underline g_B\leq\inf_{x\in B}g(x)\) and \(\overline g_B\geq\sup_{x\in B}g(x)\); deductions based solely on these inequalities cannot exclude a point because of enclosure error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regional interval is safe when it contains every function value on the region, making its lower and upper bounds rigorous.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is nonempty.
\(g\) is defined at every point of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(B)\subseteq G(B)\), with rigorous lower and upper regional bounds.

notation.meaning: computed regional enclosure of the range

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inclusion condition is precise, internally consistent, and appropriate for Safe Regional Enclosures, but it has no cited authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Directed-Rounding Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Rounding controls used to preserve enclosure validity during numerical evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Directed-Rounding Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outward rounding rule for retaining range inclusion under finite-precision interval arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an interval expression is evaluated from enclosing input intervals using inclusion-isotone interval extensions of its primitive operations. At every operation, round the computed lower endpoint toward \(-\infty\) and the upper endpoint toward \(+\infty\). If overflow, exceptional values, and elementary-function rounding are handled conservatively, the resulting interval \(G(B)\) contains the exact real-arithmetic range \(g(B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding lower endpoints downward and upper endpoints upward preserves rigorous interval inclusion when every primitive operation is implemented conservatively.
assumptions_latex: Each input interval contains its exact real quantity.
Every primitive interval operation is inclusion-isotone and outward rounded.
Exceptional floating-point cases are handled conservatively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(B)\subseteq G(B)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The outward-rounding principle fits the leaf and states the necessary implementation qualifications, but no authoritative interval-arithmetic source and locator support it.

children.title: Enclosure Safety Failures
children.top_down_role: Numerical conditions that can invalidate enclosure-based contractions.

knowledge_statements.title: Enclosure Safety Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of safe exclusion when a computed interval fails to contain the exact range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=[a,b]\), let \(g(x)=x-a\), and impose the equality constraint \(g(x)=0\). The point \(x=a\) is feasible and \(g(B)=[0,b-a]\). If inward rounding or an unsound elementary operation returns \(\widehat G(B)=[\eta,b-a]\) with \(\eta>0\), then \(0\notin\widehat G(B)\), so an interval infeasibility test discards \(B\) although it contains a feasible point. Range inclusion is therefore indispensable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interval missing even a boundary value can falsely certify infeasibility and delete a region containing a feasible point.
assumptions_latex: The exclusion test discards \(B\) whenever \(0\notin\widehat G(B)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of \(g(B)\subseteq\widehat G(B)\) can make regional exclusion unsound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constructed failure example is mathematically coherent and correctly classified as a failure boundary, but it lacks an authoritative cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Dual-Reduction Validity Failures
children.top_down_role: Unsafe contraction caused by unsuitable multipliers, unreliable relaxations, or invalid cutoff information.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Reduction Validity Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing that invalid multiplier signs can make dual cutoff contraction unsafe.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)=x\) over \(X=[0,1]\) subject to \(g(x)=x-1\leq0\). The optimum is \(0\). A valid Lagrangian lower bound requires \(\lambda\geq0\), but choosing \(\lambda=-2\) gives \(\inf_{x\in X}(f(x)+\lambda g(x))=\inf_{x\in[0,1]}(2-x)=1\). Using this invalid value with a feasible cutoff \(U=1/2\) falsely excludes \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier violating the dual sign condition can produce a false lower bound and cause an entire feasible region to be deleted.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with constraints written as \(g(x)\leq0\).
Regional exclusion occurs when the alleged lower bound exceeds the cutoff \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without \(\lambda\geq0\), the dual value need not be a lower bound, and cutoff reduction may be invalid.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly demonstrates failure from an invalid multiplier sign and fits the stated leaf, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Reduction Cost-Contraction Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Regimes where tightening cost is excessive relative to achieved contraction.

children.title: Reduction Overhead Regimes
children.top_down_role: Search contexts where reduction work consumes disproportionate computational effort.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Overhead Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-cost model separating beneficial and overhead-dominated domain reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a reduction procedure cost \(C_r>0\) at a node, let processing one unreduced descendant cost on average \(C_n>0\), and let reduction avoid an expected \(\Delta N\geq0\) descendant nodes. Under this additive cost model, reduction has nonpositive expected net overhead exactly when \(C_r\leq\Delta N C_n\); it is overhead-dominated when \(C_r>\Delta N C_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduction is worthwhile in the additive model only when its cost does not exceed the expected cost of the descendants it avoids.
assumptions_latex: Expected processing costs are additive.
The estimate \(\Delta N\) refers to descendants avoided because of reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reduction is beneficial when \(C_r\leq\Delta N C_n\) and overhead-dominated when \(C_r>\Delta N C_n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inequality follows under the explicitly stated additive expected-cost model and the principle fits the overhead-regime leaf, but the model and criterion have no supporting source.

children.title: Reduction Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Repeated tightening regimes that produce negligible domain contraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point and asymptotic criteria for failure of repeated contraction to shrink a region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be a safe reduction operator on nonempty boxes, with \(R(B)\subseteq B\), and define \(B_{k+1}=R(B_k)\). Exact stagnation occurs at iteration \(k\) when \(R(B_k)=B_k\). Relative stagnation occurs for a size functional \(s(B)>0\) when \(s(B_{k+1})/s(B_k)\to1\), so repeated reduction yields asymptotically vanishing fractional contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduction stagnates when a box is a fixed point, or when successive fractional contractions tend to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(R(B)\subseteq B\) for every box in its domain.
\(s(B)>0\) on every nonempty box considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stagnation is characterized by \(R(B_k)=B_k\) or asymptotically by \(s(B_{k+1})/s(B_k)\to1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-point and asymptotic criteria are clear definitions of exact and relative stagnation, with consistent notation, but no authoritative source and locator are supplied.

children.title: Cost-Contraction Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Boundaries governing whether expected contraction justifies reduction effort.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost-Contraction Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Efficiency comparison under additive costs and multiplicative box-size contractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For reduction method \(i\), let \(C_i>0\) be its cost and let \(q_i=s(R_i(B))/s(B)\in(0,1]\) be its contraction factor. Under a model in which sequential costs add and contraction factors multiply, the logarithmic contraction per unit cost is \(E_i=-\log(q_i)/C_i\). For a fixed small cost budget and repeatable effects, selecting a method with maximal \(E_i\) maximizes modeled contraction efficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With additive costs and multiplicative contractions, compare reductions by negative log contraction per unit cost.
assumptions_latex: Reduction costs add across applications.
Contraction factors multiply and are repeatable over the comparison horizon.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A modeled cost-efficient choice lies in \(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_i[-\log(q_i)/C_i]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The efficiency rule is coherent under the stated additive-cost, multiplicative-contraction, and repeatability assumptions and fits the tradeoff leaf, but it is model dependent and unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Spatial Partitioning Calculus
children.top_down_role: Subdivision geometries, branching objects, split locations, and refinement-quality boundaries.

children.title: Partition Geometry Families
children.top_down_role: Canonical regional shapes used to cover and refine continuous domains.

children.title: Axis-Aligned Box Partition Family
children.top_down_role: Axis-aligned regional decomposition and nested box refinement.

children.title: Binary Box Bisection
children.top_down_role: Two-way axis-aligned subdivision of a regional box.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Box Bisection
