knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-child axis-aligned subdivision at an interior coordinate cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a box \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[l_i,u_i]\), choose an index \(j\) with \(l_j<u_j\), and choose \(c\in(l_j,u_j)\), commonly \(c=(l_j+u_j)/2\). Output \(B^-=[l_j,c]\times\prod_{i\ne j}[l_i,u_i]\) and \(B^+=[c,u_j]\times\prod_{i\ne j}[l_i,u_i]\). Then \(B=B^-\cup B^+\), while the children intersect only on their shared cutting face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split one coordinate interval at an interior point to obtain two boxes whose union is the parent box.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a nondegenerate axis-aligned box.
The selected cut satisfies \(l_j<c<u_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output boxes satisfy \(B=B^-\cup B^+\) and \(\operatorname{int}(B^-)\cap\operatorname{int}(B^+)=\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm correctly defines two-child axis-aligned bisection and its partition properties, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Multiway Grid Partition Family
children.top_down_role: Subdivision into several rectangular descendants or structured grids.

children.title: Multiway Box Partitions
children.top_down_role: Rectangular subdivision producing several descendants in one refinement event.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiway Box Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite tensor partition induced by arbitrary coordinate cut sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[l_i,u_i]\). For each coordinate choose cuts \(l_i=t_{i,0}<t_{i,1}<\cdots<t_{i,m_i}=u_i\). The associated multiway box partition consists of all cells \(B_{k_1,\ldots,k_n}=\prod_{i=1}^n[t_{i,k_i-1},t_{i,k_i}]\), where \(1\leq k_i\leq m_i\). Their union is \(B\), and distinct cells have disjoint interiors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate cut sets generate a finite collection of axis-aligned boxes covering the parent with disjoint interiors.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is an axis-aligned box.
Each coordinate cut sequence is finite and strictly increasing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cells form a partition of \(B\) into \(\prod_{i=1}^n m_i\) axis-aligned boxes.

notation.meaning: number of subintervals on coordinate i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition precisely describes a finite tensor-product box partition and uses the correct content kind, but it lacks a cited authoritative source and locator.

children.title: Grid Box Partitions
children.top_down_role: Rectangular subdivision organized by a structured grid.

knowledge_statements.title: Grid Box Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform Cartesian-grid representation of an axis-aligned regional box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[l_i,u_i]\) and integers \(m_i\geq1\), define \(h_i=(u_i-l_i)/m_i\). The uniform grid represents \(B\) as the union of cells \(B_{k_1,\ldots,k_n}=\prod_{i=1}^n[l_i+(k_i-1)h_i,l_i+k_i h_i]\), with \(1\leq k_i\leq m_i\). These \(\prod_{i=1}^n m_i\) cells have disjoint interiors and cover \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform Cartesian grid divides each coordinate interval equally and represents the box as the union of all product cells.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is an axis-aligned box.
Each \(m_i\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=\bigcup_{1\leq k_i\leq m_i}B_{k_1,\ldots,k_n}\), with pairwise disjoint cell interiors.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.3 Uniform Grid Search p. 48

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1.3 Uniform Grid Search p. 48

children.title: Adaptive Grid Refinement
children.top_down_role: Selective refinement of structured box grids according to regional search information.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Grid Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selective refinement of grid cells using a regional priority indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite box partition \(\mathcal P_0\), a nonnegative indicator \(\eta(B)\), and tolerance \(\tau\geq0\). At iteration \(k\), select a cell \(B_k\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{B\in\mathcal P_k}\eta(B)\). If \(\eta(B_k)\leq\tau\), return \(\mathcal P_k\); otherwise partition \(B_k\) into finitely many boxes with disjoint interiors and union \(B_k\), replace it by its children, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly refine the cell with largest indicator until every cell's indicator is at most the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P_0\) is a finite box partition.
Every refinement exactly covers its parent with finitely many interior-disjoint children.
\(\eta(B)\geq0\) for every active cell.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On termination, \(\max_{B\in\mathcal P_k}\eta(B)\leq\tau\), and \(\mathcal P_k\) still partitions the original region.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selective-refinement algorithm is internally consistent, preserves the partition invariant, and states its termination conclusion conditionally, but no authoritative source and locator are supplied.

children.title: Adaptive Rectangular Partitions
children.top_down_role: Nonuniform box refinement guided by regional information.

assumptions_latex: The initial domain is a nondegenerate box \(B^0=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\).
Each refinement replaces one current leaf by finitely many axis-aligned boxes with pairwise disjoint interiors and the same union.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\mathcal P_k\) is a rectangular partition of \(B^0\), while refinement depth and box diameters may vary spatially.

notation.meaning: rectangular leaf partition after k refinements
regional information available for a leaf box

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard leaf-replacement definition of adaptive rectangular refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite adaptive axis-aligned partitions; no convergence or fairness rule is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adaptive rectangular partition is a sequence \((\mathcal P_k)_{k\geq0}\) with \(\mathcal P_0=\{B^0\}\). At iteration \(k\), a selection rule depending on regional information \(I_k(B)\) chooses a leaf \(B_k\in\mathcal P_k\), and a finite rectangular partition \(\mathcal C_k(B_k)\) of \(B_k\). The update is \[\mathcal P_{k+1}=(\mathcal P_k\setminus\{B_k\})\cup\mathcal C_k(B_k).\] The partition is nonuniform because neither the selected leaf nor its subdivision pattern must be spatially uniform.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive rectangular partition repeatedly replaces an information-selected box by smaller axis-aligned boxes, allowing different regions to attain different depths and resolutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Rectangular Partitions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the adaptive rectangular-partition leaf, but no inspectable citation supports the specific information-guided refinement formulation.

children.title: Simplicial Partitions
children.top_down_role: Triangulation and simplex-subdivision families.

children.title: Edge-Based Simplex Subdivision
children.top_down_role: Simplex refinement organized around selected edges.

assumptions_latex: The parent is a nondegenerate simplex \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\).
A selected edge \([v_i,v_j]\) contains a point \(q=(1-t)v_i+t v_j\) with \(0<t<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two children form a simplicial partition of \(S\) and share the facet generated by \(q\) and all vertices outside the selected edge.

notation.meaning: interior point of the selected edge

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard edge split of a simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-edge binary subdivision of a nondegenerate finite-dimensional simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The edge-based subdivision of \(S\) at \(q\in(v_i,v_j)\) consists of \[S_i=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\{q\}\cup\{v_r:r\neq i\}\bigr),\qquad S_j=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\{q\}\cup\{v_r:r\neq j\}\bigr).\] Both children are nondegenerate simplices, \(S=S_i\cup S_j\), and their interiors are disjoint. Thus selecting an edge and an interior split point defines a binary simplicial refinement; midpoint bisection is the special case \(t=1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting a selected simplex edge at an interior point produces two child simplices whose union is the parent and whose interiors do not overlap.
knowledge_statements.title: Edge-Based Simplex Subdivision

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary edge split is mathematically standard and correctly scoped, but the record supplies no source or locator.

children.title: Simplex Reference-Point Subdivision Family
children.top_down_role: Simplex refinement organized around vertices, centroids, or other interior points.

children.title: Vertex-Based Simplex Subdivision
children.top_down_role: Simplex refinement organized around a selected vertex.

assumptions_latex: The parent simplex is \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,ldots,v_n\}\).
A vertex \(v_i\) is selected, and the opposite facet \(F_i=\operatorname{conv}\{v_j:j\neq i\}\) has a simplicial partition \(\mathcal T_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coning every cell of \(\mathcal T_i\) to \(v_i\) yields a simplicial partition of \(S\).

notation.meaning: simplicial partition of the opposite facet

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: recursive vertex-coning interpretation of vertex-based simplex subdivision
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex-coning subdivision induced by a triangulation of the opposite facet.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The vertex-based subdivision associated with \(v_i\) and \(\mathcal T_i\) is \[\mathcal T(S;v_i)=\{\operatorname{conv}(\{v_i\}\cup T):T\in\mathcal T_i\}.\] Every member is an \(n\)-simplex when every \(T\in\mathcal T_i\) is a nondegenerate \((n-1)\)-simplex. Moreover, the children cover \(S\), and any two children intersect only in a common face inherited from \(\mathcal T_i\). The selected vertex is shared by all children.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vertex-based subdivision triangulates the facet opposite a selected vertex and cones each facet cell to that vertex.
knowledge_statements.title: Vertex-Based Simplex Subdivision

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The vertex-coning construction is plausible, but the intended meaning of “vertex-based subdivision” requires a source. The first assumption also has malformed LaTeX: “ldots” should be “\ldots”.

children.title: Interior-Point Simplex Subdivision
children.top_down_role: Simplex refinement organized around a centroid or another interior point.

assumptions_latex: The parent is a nondegenerate simplex \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\).
The reference point \(c\) lies in \(\operatorname{int}S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The \(n+1\) children \(S_i\) constitute a simplicial partition of \(S\).

notation.meaning: child simplex over the opposite facet

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard stellar subdivision of a simplex at an interior point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stellar subdivision at one strictly interior reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(i\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\), let \(F_i=\operatorname{conv}\{v_j:j\neq i\}\) and define \(S_i=\operatorname{conv}(\{c\}\cup F_i)\). The interior-point subdivision is the family \(\{S_0,\ldots,S_n\}\). Each \(S_i\) is nondegenerate, \[S=\bigcup_{i=0}^n S_i,\qquad \operatorname{int}S_i\cap\operatorname{int}S_j=\varnothing\quad(i\neq j).\] Hence joining \(c\) to every facet partitions the parent into \(n+1\) simplices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joining a strictly interior point to every facet divides an n-simplex into n+1 nonoverlapping child simplices.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Simplex Subdivision

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated stellar subdivision is mathematically standard and matches the leaf, but no cited source with a locator is supplied.

children.title: Simplex Center Selection
children.top_down_role: Geometric criteria for choosing the organizing point of a simplex refinement.

assumptions_latex: The input is a nondegenerate simplex \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\).
The selected point will be used for interior-point simplex subdivision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any rule satisfying \(c(S)\in\operatorname{int}S\) produces nondegenerate stellar children; the barycentric rule is affine-equivariant.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: admissibility and affine-equivariance conditions for simplex reference points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible center rules for stellar simplex subdivision, with the barycenter as canonical choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A simplex center-selection rule is subdivision-admissible when \[c(S)\in\operatorname{int}S.\] It is affine-equivariant when \(c(A S+b)=A c(S)+b\) for every invertible affine map \(x\mapsto Ax+b\). The barycentric rule \[c_{\mathrm{bar}}(S)=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum_{i=0}^n v_i\] satisfies both conditions. If geometry-dependent centers such as incenters or circumcenters are used, strict interiority must be checked separately before forming stellar children.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subdivision center must lie strictly inside the simplex; affine-equivariant rules behave consistently under coordinate changes, and the barycenter is the canonical example.
knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Center Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The admissibility condition and barycentric example fit center selection, but no source is supplied. The warning groups incenters with circumcenters even though a simplex incenter is automatically strictly interior.

children.title: Conical Partitions
children.top_down_role: Cone-covering and cone-subdivision families used in canonical global-optimization geometry.

assumptions_latex: The domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and a common apex \(a\in D\) are fixed.
Each cell is \(D\cap K_r\), where \(K_r\) is a convex cone with apex \(a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cells form a conical partition exactly when they cover \(D\) and have pairwise disjoint relative interiors.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite cone-induced partitions restricted to a global-search domain.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Partition Methods on General Convex and Star Sets p. 119

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conical partition of \(D\) with apex \(a\) is a finite family \(\mathcal C=\{C_r\}_{r=1}^m\) such that \(C_r=D\cap K_r\), each \(K_r\) is a convex cone translated to apex \(a\), and \[D=\bigcup_{r=1}^m C_r,\qquad \operatorname{relint}C_r\cap\operatorname{relint}C_s=\varnothing\quad(r\neq s).\] A conical subdivision replaces one cell by finitely many cells induced by subcones whose union equals its generating cone over the relevant directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conical partition covers a domain by cone-induced cells sharing an apex, with no overlap between distinct relative interiors.
knowledge_statements.title: Conical Partitions

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Partition Methods on General Convex and Star Sets p. 119

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and cone-induced geometry fit the leaf, but the available locator has not been shown to support the common-apex definition or the stated conical-subdivision clause.

children.title: General-Geometry Set Partitions
children.top_down_role: Partition interfaces beyond boxes, simplices, and cones.

children.title: Convex-Set Partitions
children.top_down_role: Spatial subdivisions whose regional cells retain convex geometry.

assumptions_latex: The domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
The partition family is finite and its cells are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cell and every segment joining two points of the same cell remain inside that cell.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite partitions whose individual cells preserve convexity.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Partition Methods on General Convex and Star Sets p. 119

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex-set partition of \(D\) is a finite family \(\mathcal P=\{P_1,\ldots,P_m\}\) of convex subsets of \(D\) satisfying \[D=\bigcup_{r=1}^m P_r,\qquad \operatorname{relint}P_r\cap\operatorname{relint}P_s=\varnothing\quad(r\neq s).\] Convexity means that for every \(x,y\in P_r\) and \(t\in[0,1]\), one has \((1-t)x+ty\in P_r\). Shared boundaries are permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex-set partition finitely covers a convex domain by convex cells whose relative interiors are pairwise disjoint; cells may share boundaries.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Set Partitions

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Partition Methods on General Convex and Star Sets p. 119

children.title: Star-Shaped-Set Partitions
children.top_down_role: Spatial subdivisions whose regional cells are organized around star centers.

assumptions_latex: The domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is star-shaped.
Each nonempty cell is assigned at least one star center.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cell is visible by line segments from its assigned center, although different cells need not share a center or be convex.

notation.meaning: star center assigned to cell r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite partitions with cellwise, not necessarily common, star centers.

source_refs.locator: 2.6.5 General Star-Shaped Sets p. 129

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A star-shaped-set partition of \(D\) is a finite family \(\mathcal P=\{P_1,\ldots,P_m\}\) satisfying \[D=\bigcup_{r=1}^m P_r,\qquad \operatorname{relint}P_r\cap\operatorname{relint}P_s=\varnothing\quad(r\neq s),\] together with points \(a_r\in P_r\) such that \([a_r,x]\subseteq P_r\) for every \(x\in P_r\). The centers \(a_r\) may differ, and the cells need not be convex. Shared cell boundaries are allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A star-shaped-set partition covers the domain by cells with disjoint relative interiors, each visible along line segments from its own star center.
knowledge_statements.title: Star-Shaped-Set Partitions

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6.5 General Star-Shaped Sets p. 129

children.title: General-Set Partitions
children.top_down_role: Partition interfaces for regional cells lacking box, simplex, cone, convex, or star-shaped restrictions.

assumptions_latex: The domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty.
Cells are measurable when integration, probability, or volume-based selection is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining requirements are coverage and pairwise disjointness; no convexity, connectedness, or star-shapedness is implied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic partitions without cell geometry assumptions.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Partition Methods on General Convex and Star Sets p. 119

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A general-set partition of \(D\) is a finite or countable indexed family \(\mathcal P=\{P_r:r\in R\}\) such that \[P_r\subseteq D,\qquad D=\bigcup_{r\in R}P_r,\qquad P_r\cap P_s=\varnothing\quad(r\neq s).\] If an implementation stores closed cells with shared boundaries, the last condition is replaced by disjoint relative interiors together with a deterministic boundary-assignment convention. No regularity or geometric shape is otherwise required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general-set partition covers a domain by disjoint cells without imposing convexity or connectedness; closed-cell representations need an explicit shared-boundary convention.
knowledge_statements.title: General-Set Partitions

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Partition Methods on General Convex and Star Sets p. 119

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited section concerns convex and star-shaped partition methods and has not been shown to support the broader finite-or-countable set-theoretic definition or boundary-assignment convention. The formula also does not explicitly require nonempty cells.

children.title: Branching Object Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of variable, expression, direction, or disjunction responsible for spatial refinement.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Nonlinear branching candidates and branching scores

children.title: Domain-Width Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching priorities based on remaining regional widths.

assumptions_latex: The active region is \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\), with finite bounds and at least one positive width.
Positive scaling factors \(s_i\) are fixed when coordinate units differ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule branches on a coordinate having maximal remaining normalized width.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard longest-side spatial branching rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Longest-normalized-side branching for bounded rectangular regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B\), compute \(w_i(B)=(u_i-\ell_i)/s_i\) and select \[i^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{1\leq i\leq n} w_i(B),\] using a fixed tie-breaking rule. Choose a split value \(\xi\in(\ell_{i^*},u_{i^*})\), commonly the midpoint, and replace \(B\) by the two boxes obtained by imposing respectively \(x_{i^*}\leq\xi\) and \(x_{i^*}\geq\xi\). Stop branching a box when its maximal normalized width is below the prescribed spatial tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Domain-width branching splits an active box along a coordinate with greatest remaining normalized width, using a fixed tie rule and an interior split point.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Width Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The longest-normalized-width algorithm and algorithm content kind fit the branching leaf, but no source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Error-Violation Branching Priorities
children.top_down_role: Branching priorities derived from relaxation mismatch or nonlinear violation.

children.title: Relaxation-Error Branching
children.top_down_role: Candidate priorities derived from regional relaxation mismatch.

assumptions_latex: For every branching object \(j\), a relaxation supplies a relaxed value \(z_j\) and an original-term evaluation \(h_j(z_j)\).
A nonnegative discrepancy measure \(e_j\) and deterministic tie rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected object maximizes the measured local discrepancy between the original model and its relaxation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic maximum relaxation-gap branching rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic error-score branching; the discrepancy formula depends on the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At the current relaxation solution, compute for each eligible object \(j\) a nonnegative error \(e_j\) that vanishes when its relaxed representation agrees with the original relation. For example, for a relaxed graph variable \(y_j\) representing \(h_j(z_j)\), use \(e_j=|y_j-h_j(z_j)|/\sigma_j\) with \(\sigma_j>0\). Select \[j^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_j e_j,\] apply the prescribed spatial split for \(j^*\), and stop error-driven branching when \(\max_j e_j\leq\varepsilon_{m err}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation-error branching scores eligible objects by disagreement between original and relaxed relations, then branches on a maximum-score object until errors meet tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Error Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits relaxation-error branching, but its error metric, stopping rule, and mapping to a spatial split are model-dependent and unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Violation-Based Branching
children.top_down_role: Candidate priorities derived from nonlinear or structural violation.

assumptions_latex: Constraints are written as \(g_j(x)\leq0\), with positive normalization constants \(\sigma_j\).
A candidate point \(\bar x\) and a mapping from each constraint to eligible spatial branching objects are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method prioritizes a branch associated with a maximally normalized violated constraint.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard maximum normalized-violation priority rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum normalized constraint-violation branching at a candidate point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(v_j(\bar x)=[g_j(\bar x)]_+/\sigma_j\), where \([t]_+=\max\{t,0\}\). If \(\max_j v_j(\bar x)\leq\varepsilon_{m feas}\), violation-driven branching stops. Otherwise choose \[j^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_j v_j(\bar x)\] with deterministic tie-breaking, select an eligible spatial object occurring in \(g_{j^*}\) according to the prescribed secondary score, and subdivide its current domain. Normalization prevents constraint units alone from determining priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Violation-based branching selects a maximally normalized violated constraint, maps it to an eligible spatial object, and subdivides that object's current domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Violation-Based Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The maximum normalized-violation rule fits the leaf, but the secondary mapping from a violated constraint to a spatial branching object and the stopping rule require source support.

children.title: Error-Violation Priority Reconciliation
children.top_down_role: Branching regimes that reconcile competing mismatch and violation signals.

assumptions_latex: The current region is a box \(B=\prod_{j=1}^n[\ell_j,u_j]\) with candidate branching objects \(J\).
For every \(j\in J\), a relaxation-error score \(e_j\ge 0\) and a constraint-violation score \(v_j\ge 0\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected object is \(j^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{j\in J}p_j\).

notation.meaning: Normalized reconciled priority of branching object j.
Nonnegative weights assigned to error and violation.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalized weighted scoring is a standard deterministic reconciliation of heterogeneous branching signals
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scale-invariant weighted reconciliation rule; ties may be resolved deterministically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given weights \(\alpha,\beta\ge 0\) with \(\alpha+\beta>0\) and safeguard \(\varepsilon>0\), compute \[p_j=\alpha\frac{e_j}{\max_{k\in J}e_k+\varepsilon}+\beta\frac{v_j}{\max_{k\in J}v_k+\varepsilon},\qquad j\in J.\] Select any \(j^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{j\in J}p_j\); under a deterministic implementation, resolve ties by a fixed ordering of \(J\). Each term lies in \([0,1]\), so neither score dominates solely because of its physical scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize error and violation scores separately, combine them with nonnegative weights, and branch on an object attaining the largest combined priority.
knowledge_statements.title: Error-Violation Priority Reconciliation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but the particular normalization, safeguard, and weighted reconciliation rule are design choices rather than a canonical definition. A source specific to this spatial-branching formulation is required.

children.title: Strong-Reliability Spatial Branching
children.top_down_role: Look-ahead and accumulated-history approaches for continuous branching candidates.

children.title: Strong Spatial Branching
children.top_down_role: Continuous branching candidates assessed through limited look-ahead evaluation.

assumptions_latex: A finite candidate set \(J\) and admissible trial split points \(s_j\in(\ell_j,u_j)\) are given.
The parent relaxation has lower bound \(L\), and both child relaxations can be solved or safely bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Branch on an object maximizing a prescribed aggregation of the two trial bound improvements.

notation.meaning: Lower bounds from the two trial child regions for candidate j.
Nonnegative child-bound improvements over the parent.
Positive balancing parameter in the score.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: strong branching conventionally compares candidates by explicit trial child relaxations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full two-child trial evaluation for spatial branch selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(j\in J\), form the children \(B_j^-=B\cap\{x:x_j\le s_j\}\) and \(B_j^+=B\cap\{x:x_j\ge s_j\}\), and compute valid relaxation bounds \(L_j^-\) and \(L_j^+\). Set \(\Delta_j^-=\max\{0,L_j^--L\}\), \(\Delta_j^+=\max\{0,L_j^+-L\}\), and \[S_j=\max\{\Delta_j^-,\Delta_j^+\}+\mu\min\{\Delta_j^-,\Delta_j^+\},\qquad \mu>0.\] Choose \(j^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{j\in J}S_j\), create its two children, and retain the trial bounds as their initial lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporarily solve both children for every candidate, score their lower-bound improvements, and branch on the candidate with the best balanced improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Spatial Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Strong trial evaluation fits the leaf and algorithm kind, but the stated max-plus-mu-min score is convention-dependent and does not unambiguously express the claimed balanced improvement without restrictions on mu. The spatial specialization and score require authoritative support.

children.title: Reliability Spatial Branching
children.top_down_role: Continuous branching candidates assessed using accumulated outcome history.

assumptions_latex: Each candidate \(j\) has observation counts \(r_j^-,r_j^+\) and estimated unit effects \(q_j^-,q_j^+\ge 0\).
A reliability threshold \(R\in\mathbb N\) and predicted branch displacements \(d_j^-,d_j^+>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Candidates with insufficient history are trial-evaluated; reliable candidates are scored from accumulated unit effects.

notation.meaning: Directional observation counts for candidate j.
Estimated lower-bound improvement per unit displacement.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reliability branching combines strong trials for immature estimates with history-based prediction for mature estimates
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reliability branching with directional history and strong evaluation below threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(j\), if \(\min\{r_j^-,r_j^+\}<R\), perform the two strong trial evaluations and use their improvements \(\widehat\Delta_j^-,\widehat\Delta_j^+\), updating each observed unit effect by \(\widehat\Delta_j^\sigma/d_j^\sigma\) for \(\sigma\in\{-,+\}\). Otherwise predict \(\widehat\Delta_j^\sigma=q_j^\sigma d_j^\sigma\). Compute \[S_j=\max\{\widehat\Delta_j^-,\widehat\Delta_j^+\}+\mu\min\{\widehat\Delta_j^-,\widehat\Delta_j^+\},\qquad \mu>0,\] branch on a maximizer, and update history when actual child information becomes available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use strong trial solves until both directional estimates are sufficiently sampled, then rank mature candidates using predicted bound improvements from accumulated history.
knowledge_statements.title: Reliability Spatial Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits reliability spatial branching, but the directional reliability test, unit-effect update, prediction rule, and aggregation are variant-specific and unsupported. A source is needed to determine the intended formulation.

children.title: Strong-to-Reliability Transition
children.top_down_role: Policies governing the shift from look-ahead evaluation to history-based scoring.

assumptions_latex: Directional estimates for candidate \(j\) are updated only from valid observed child-bound improvements.
The reliability threshold satisfies \(R\ge 1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Candidate \(j\) changes from strong evaluation to history prediction exactly when \(\min\{r_j^-,r_j^+\}\ge R\).

notation.meaning: Required number of observations in each direction.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a directional observation threshold is the standard strong-to-reliability switching predicate
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional reliability requires sufficient evidence on both children.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the maturity predicate \[M_j\;\Longleftrightarrow\;r_j^-\ge R\ \text{ and }\ r_j^+\ge R.\] While \(M_j\) is false, candidate \(j\) is evaluated by explicit strong trial branching whenever it is considered, and every valid directional observation increments the corresponding count. Once \(M_j\) becomes true, subsequent scores for \(j\) may use the stored directional unit-effect estimates without mandatory trial solves. Because the counts are nondecreasing, the transition is irreversible unless the history is explicitly invalidated after a model or scaling change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Switch a candidate from trial evaluation to history-based prediction only after each branch direction has accumulated at least the reliability threshold of valid observations.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-to-Reliability Transition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the transition leaf, but the requirement that both directional counts reach R, the mandatory-trial policy, and irreversibility are implementation-specific claims needing a source.

children.title: Structure-Aware Spatial Branching
children.top_down_role: Priorities based on expression incidence, nonlinear participation, separability, or sparsity.

assumptions_latex: The factorable model has branching candidates \(J\), nonlinear expression nodes \(T\), and an incidence relation between them.
Nonnegative structural weights are fixed before selecting a branching object.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A candidate maximizing the weighted structural score is selected.

notation.meaning: Nonlinear expression nodes containing candidate j.
Nonnegative importance weight of expression node t.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: incidence-weighted scoring directly formalizes structure-aware branching under sparsity and separability
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incidence-based priority for factorable sparse models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I(j)=\{t\in T:j\text{ occurs nonlinearly in }t\}\). Assign each \(t\in T\) a weight \(w_t\ge 0\), and optionally assign a separability factor \(c_j>0\) that discounts candidates whose split affects many independent blocks. Compute \[S_j=c_j\sum_{t\in I(j)}w_t.\] Restrict attention to candidates with positive domain width and nonzero nonlinear incidence, then choose \(j^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{j}S_j\). The weights may encode expression depth, relaxation error, or constraint importance, but must be fixed for the current selection step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score each candidate by its weighted nonlinear-expression incidence, optionally discounting cross-block coupling, and select the highest-scoring eligible candidate.
knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Aware Spatial Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An algorithm is appropriate for this topic, but the incidence sum and optional separability discount are a proposed heuristic, not a uniquely determined structure-aware branching rule. The exact score and eligibility policy require support.

children.title: Branching-Point Selection
children.top_down_role: Families for locating a split within the selected domain or direction.

children.title: Geometry-Balanced Split Family
children.top_down_role: Split locations designed primarily to control descendant geometry.

children.title: Midpoint Splits
children.top_down_role: Split locations placed at regional interval midpoints.

assumptions_latex: The selected coordinate interval is finite and nondegenerate: \(-\infty<\ell_j<u_j<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The midpoint split produces two children of equal width \((u_j-\ell_j)/2\).

notation.meaning: Midpoint of the selected coordinate interval.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: midpoint bisection of a finite interval is elementary and unambiguous
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coordinate bisection of a finite box.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a box \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) and selected coordinate \(j\), the midpoint split uses \[m_j=\frac{\ell_j+u_j}{2}.\] It replaces \(B\) by \(B^-=B\cap\{x:x_j\le m_j\}\) and \(B^+=B\cap\{x:x_j\ge m_j\}\). Their interiors are disjoint, their union is \(B\), and both child intervals in coordinate \(j\) have width \((u_j-\ell_j)/2\); every other coordinate interval is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bisect the selected finite coordinate interval at its midpoint, yielding two equal-width child boxes whose union is the parent box.
knowledge_statements.title: Midpoint Splits

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The midpoint definition and geometric claims are precise and the content kind fits, but the cited locator concerns the structure of global-optimization models and does not specifically support midpoint spatial subdivision. A directly relevant section or page is required.

children.title: Geometry-Balanced Splits
children.top_down_role: Split locations chosen to balance descendant geometric size or shape.

assumptions_latex: The selected interval \([\ell_j,u_j]\) is finite with width \(w_j=u_j-\ell_j>0\).
A balance parameter \(\rho\in(0,1/2]\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both child widths lie between \(\rho w_j\) and \((1-\rho)w_j\).

notation.meaning: Parent width in the selected coordinate.
Minimum retained fraction in either child.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fractional interiority is the standard complete predicate for a uniformly balanced interval split
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform fractional balance, with midpoint bisection as the limiting case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A split location \(s_j\in(\ell_j,u_j)\) is \(\rho\)-geometry-balanced when \[\ell_j+\rho w_j\le s_j\le u_j-\rho w_j.\] Equivalently, the child widths \(w_j^-=s_j-\ell_j\) and \(w_j^+=u_j-s_j\) satisfy \[\rho w_j\le\min\{w_j^-,w_j^+\}\le\max\{w_j^-,w_j^+\}\le(1-\rho)w_j.\] For \(\rho=1/2\), the only admissible location is the midpoint; smaller \(\rho\) permits controlled asymmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A split is geometry-balanced when its location stays at least a fixed fraction of the parent width away from both endpoints.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Balanced Splits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically precise and fits the leaf, but no citation supports the use of this fractional-interiority predicate as the intended meaning of geometry-balanced spatial splits.

children.title: Balanced-Split Distortion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regional geometries where nominally balanced locations yield poorly balanced descendants.

assumptions_latex: Each split of an interval of width \(w>0\) occurs at fraction \(\theta\in(0,1)\) of that width.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform geometric contraction holds exactly when split fractions remain uniformly separated from \(0\) and \(1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the contraction boundary follows directly from the exact child-width ratios
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp endpoint boundary for uniform one-step width contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Writing \(s=\ell+\theta w\), the larger child has width \[q(\theta)w,\qquad q(\theta)=\max\{\theta,1-\theta\}.\] If \(\theta\in[\rho,1-\rho]\) for some \(\rho\in(0,1/2]\), then \(q(\theta)\le1-\rho<1\), giving uniform contraction. Conversely, if no positive \(\rho\) bounds the split fractions away from the endpoints, there exists a sequence \(\theta_k\to0\) or \(\theta_k\to1\) for which \(q(\theta_k)\to1\). Hence no uniform contraction factor below one can then be guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balanced splits contract the larger child uniformly; allowing split fractions to approach either endpoint destroys every uniform contraction factor below one.
knowledge_statements.title: Balanced-Split Distortion Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the converse concerns a family or sequence of split fractions whose quantification is only implicit. A source is needed to establish the intended uniform-contraction boundary and its scope.

children.title: Relaxation-Solution Splits
children.top_down_role: Split locations tied to the current regional relaxation solution.

assumptions_latex: The current regional relaxation has an optimal solution \(\bar x\in B\).
A selected coordinate satisfies \(\ell_j<\bar x_j<u_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The split point is \(s_j=\bar x_j\), and the two resulting boxes cover the parent.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: splitting at an interior relaxation solution is a standard relaxation-guided spatial partition rule
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior relaxation optimizer determines the coordinate split point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the relaxation over \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) and choose an eligible coordinate \(j\). Set \(s_j=\bar x_j\), then create \[B^-=B\cap\{x:x_j\le s_j\},\qquad B^+=B\cap\{x:x_j\ge s_j\}.\] The children have disjoint interiors and union \(B\). If \(\bar x_j\) is an endpoint or violates a prescribed balance margin, this rule is undefined without a fallback; a midpoint or projected balanced point must then be specified separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split the selected coordinate at the current relaxation optimizer, using a separately specified fallback when that value is too close to an endpoint.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Solution Splits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches relaxation-solution splitting, but the exact rule and the suggested midpoint or projected-balance fallback are unsupported implementation choices. A spatial global-optimization source is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded constrained nonlinear programs equipped with AlphaBB convex relaxations on subrectangles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given tolerances \(\epsilon_c,\epsilon_f\), initialize a rectangular search region and global bounds \(LBD,UBD\). At each iteration: locally solve the nonconvex NLP and update \(UBD\) with any \(\epsilon_f\)-feasible objective value; bisect the current rectangle at the midpoint of a longest side; recompute the positive AlphaBB parameters \(\alpha_{i,k}^j\) on both children; solve the convex AlphaBB relaxation on each child and retain every child whose lower-bound value is below \(UBD\); set \(LBD\) to the smallest retained lower bound and select its rectangle next. Continue while \(UBD-LBD>\epsilon_c\); otherwise return the incumbent attaining \(UBD\) as the \(\epsilon_c\)-converged global solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm maintains global lower and upper bounds, improves the upper bound with feasible local NLP solutions, bisects a longest side, rebuilds and solves AlphaBB convex relaxations on both children, and next processes the retained child with the smallest lower bound. It stops when the bound gap is at most the convergence tolerance and returns the incumbent attaining the upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \epsilon_c>0
\epsilon_f>0
x\in[x^{LBD},x^{UBD}]
\text{AlphaBB parameters and the convex relaxation can be computed on each child rectangle}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: UBD-LBD\le\epsilon_c\quad\Longrightarrow\quad (f^*,x^*)\text{ is returned from an incumbent attaining }UBD

source_evidence.locator: THE αBB APPROACH FOR GENERAL CONSTRAINED TWICE-DIFFERENTIABLE NLPS : THEORY / 12. THE αBB APPROACH FOR GENERAL CONSTRAINED TWICE-DIFFERENTIABLE NLPS : THEORY / Algorithm 12-extra-4

children.title: Adaptive History-Guided Splits
children.top_down_role: Split locations informed by previous branch outcomes or nonlinear behavior.

children.title: Adaptive Split Locations
children.top_down_role: Split positions adjusted to current regional nonlinear behavior.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), an eligible interval \([\ell_j,u_j]\), a target proposal \(t_{j,k}\), and a balance margin \(\rho_k\in(0,1/2]\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection of the proposal yields a valid \(\rho_k\)-balanced adaptive split.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: projecting an adaptive proposal onto a balanced admissible interval preserves both adaptation and geometric validity
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic adaptive proposal with an explicit geometric safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w_j=u_j-\ell_j\) and define the admissible interval \(A_{j,k}=[\ell_j+\rho_k w_j,u_j-\rho_k w_j]\). Choose \[s_{j,k}=\operatorname{proj}_{A_{j,k}}(t_{j,k}),\] where \(t_{j,k}\) may depend only on information available through iteration \(k\). Split the box at \(s_{j,k}\), record the subsequent child outcomes, and use them when constructing later proposals. The projection guarantees both child widths are at least \(\rho_k w_j\), regardless of the unconstrained proposal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Construct a split proposal from current information, project it into a balanced interior interval, branch there, and feed the observed outcome into future proposals.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Split Locations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projected adaptive split is internally coherent and algorithmically appropriate, but the proposal-generation policy is unconstrained beyond information availability, and no source identifies this construction as the intended adaptive method.

children.title: History-Based Split Locations
children.top_down_role: Split positions informed by outcomes from prior branching decisions.

assumptions_latex: For candidate \(j\), past normalized split fractions \(z_{j,r}\in[0,1]\) have nonnegative relevance weights \(a_{j,r}\).
The total historical weight is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The weighted historical fraction determines the next split, subject to a balance projection.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalized weighted averaging is a verifiable history-based split-location rule
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted transfer of past normalized locations to the current interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute the historical target \[\widehat z_j=\frac{\sum_r a_{j,r}z_{j,r}}{\sum_r a_{j,r}}.\] For the current interval \([\ell_j,u_j]\), choose a margin \(\rho\in(0,1/2]\), set \(z_j^*=\min\{1-\rho,\max\{\rho,\widehat z_j\}\}\), and split at \[s_j=\ell_j+z_j^*(u_j-\ell_j).\] After evaluating the children, append the realized normalized location and its prescribed relevance weight to the history. Zero-weight observations do not affect future locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average past normalized split positions using relevance weights, clip the result to a balanced range, and map it onto the current interval.
knowledge_statements.title: History-Based Split Locations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted normalized-history algorithm fits the leaf, but the averaging rule, relevance weights, and history update are particular modeling choices without cited support.

children.title: Split-Location History Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of split-location experience across related regions or search depths.

assumptions_latex: A source interval \([\ell^s,u^s]\) and target interval \([\ell^t,u^t]\) are finite and nondegenerate.
A stored source split satisfies \(s^s\in[\ell^s,u^s]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Affine normalized transfer preserves the split fraction and commutes with interval rescaling.

notation.meaning: Transferred split in the target interval.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine normalization is the canonical scale-invariant representation of an interval location
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine transfer between compatible coordinate intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the source location by its normalized fraction \[z=\frac{s^s-\ell^s}{u^s-\ell^s}\in[0,1].\] Transfer it to the target interval by \[s^t=\ell^t+z(u^t-\ell^t).\] Then \((s^t-\ell^t)/(u^t-\ell^t)=z\), so relative position is invariant under translation and positive rescaling. If a target balance margin \(\rho\in(0,1/2]\) is required, replace \(z\) by \(\min\{1-\rho,\max\{\rho,z\}\}\) before mapping. Transfer is valid only between semantically compatible coordinates or branching objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize a historical split to its fractional interval position, then map that fraction affinely to a compatible target interval, optionally enforcing balance.
knowledge_statements.title: Split-Location History Transfer

children.title: Partition Refinement Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Geometric phenomena affecting bound improvement and exhaustive refinement.

children.title: Persistent-Diameter Partition Failures
children.top_down_role: Refinement patterns that fail to reduce relevant regional diameters effectively.

children.title: Nonshrinking Partition Sequences
children.top_down_role: Refinement sequences that fail to reduce relevant regional diameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonshrinking Partition Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines failure of diameter decay along a nested descendant sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space and let \((C_k)_{k\geq 0}\) be nonempty sets satisfying \(C_{k+1}\subseteq C_k\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(C_0)<\infty\). The sequence is nonshrinking when
\[
\inf_{k\geq 0}\operatorname{diam}(C_k)>0.
\]
Because the diameters form a nonincreasing nonnegative sequence, this is equivalent to \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\operatorname{diam}(C_k)=\delta\) for some \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested descendant sequence is nonshrinking when its cell diameters converge to a strictly positive value rather than to zero.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a metric space.
\(C_{k+1}\subseteq C_k\neq\varnothing\) for every \(k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{k\geq0}\operatorname{diam}(C_k)>0\).

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

children.title: Unbalanced Descendant Geometry
children.top_down_role: Refinements producing descendants with persistently disproportionate geometric scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbalanced Descendant Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Axis-aligned descendants contract some coordinates while retaining positive width in another.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_k=\prod_{j=1}^n[a_{k,j},b_{k,j}]\) be nested nonempty boxes and set \(w_{k,j}=b_{k,j}-a_{k,j}\). Their descendant geometry is unbalanced if there are indices \(p,q\) and a constant \(\varepsilon>0\) such that
\[
w_{k,p}\geq\varepsilon\quad\text{for all }k,
\qquad
w_{k,q}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Then \(\operatorname{diam}(C_k)\geq\varepsilon\), while \(\max_jw_{k,j}/\min_jw_{k,j}\to\infty\) whenever every width remains positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Descendants are unbalanced when at least one coordinate never contracts while another contracts to zero, producing persistent diameter and unbounded aspect ratio.
assumptions_latex: \(C_{k+1}\subseteq C_k\) are nonempty axis-aligned boxes in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(w_{k,j}>0\) when the aspect ratio is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_k\operatorname{diam}(C_k)\geq\varepsilon\), and the aspect ratios diverge.

notation.meaning: width of cell k in coordinate j

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

children.title: Persistent-Diameter Failure
children.top_down_role: Search regimes where geometric imbalance prevents effective diameter reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Diameter Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the convergence obstruction created by a positive-diameter infinite branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((X,d)\) be compact and let \((C_k)\) be nested nonempty compact cells with \(\inf_k\operatorname{diam}(C_k)=\delta>0\). Then the intersection \(C_\infty=\bigcap_k C_k\) has diameter at least \(\delta\). Consequently there exists a continuous, indeed Lipschitz, function \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) for which
\[
\inf_k\bigl(\sup_{x\in C_k}f(x)-\inf_{x\in C_k}f(x)\bigr)>0.
\]
Thus refinement alone cannot guarantee vanishing cellwise uncertainty along this branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact infinite branch whose diameter stays positive admits a Lipschitz objective with nonvanishing variation, so refinement cannot ensure local resolution.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is compact.
\(C_{k+1}\subseteq C_k\) are nonempty compact sets.
\(\inf_k\operatorname{diam}(C_k)=\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists Lipschitz \(f\) whose oscillation on \(C_k\) is bounded away from zero.

notation.meaning: intersection of all cells on the branch

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

children.title: Partition Cell Degeneracy Classes

children.title: Degenerate Partition Cells
children.top_down_role: Cells suffering dimensional collapse or loss of usable geometric extent.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Partition Cells
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses affine dimension to define degeneracy of convex cells in Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nonempty convex partition cell \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is degenerate when
\[
\dim(\operatorname{aff}C)<n.
\]
Equivalently, \(C\) has empty Euclidean interior. If \(C\) is measurable, this condition is also equivalent to its \(n\)-dimensional Lebesgue measure being zero. Degeneracy is relative to the declared ambient dimension; the same set may be full-dimensional inside its affine hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex cell is degenerate when it lies in a proper affine subspace of the declared ambient space.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is degenerate exactly when \(\dim(\operatorname{aff}C)<n\).

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

children.title: Ill-Shaped Partition Cells
children.top_down_role: Cells with extreme aspect, angle, or conditioning characteristics.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Shaped Partition Cells
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines poor cell shape through the circumradius-to-inradius ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a compact convex cell \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) with nonempty interior, let \(R(C)\) be the radius of a smallest enclosing Euclidean ball and \(r(C)\) the radius of a largest enclosed Euclidean ball. Its shape ratio is
\[
\kappa(C)=\frac{R(C)}{r(C)}.
\]
A sequence \((C_k)\) is ill-shaped when \(\sup_k\kappa(C_k)=\infty\). A partition family is uniformly shape-regular precisely when this supremum is finite over all its cells.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-dimensional convex cells are ill-shaped when their enclosing-radius to inscribed-radius ratios become arbitrarily large.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_k\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is compact, convex, and has nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ill-shapedness is characterized by \(\sup_k R(C_k)/r(C_k)=\infty\).

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

children.title: Cell-Geometry Numerical Failures
children.top_down_role: Numerical difficulties induced by degenerate or poorly conditioned regional geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Cell-Geometry Numerical Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank decisions for simplex cells become uncertifiable near floating-point singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent an \(n\)-simplex by the edge matrix \(B=[v_1-v_0,\ldots,v_n-v_0]\). Suppose floating-point construction produces \(\widehat B=B+E\) with \(\lVert E\rVert_2\leq\eta\). If \(\sigma_{\min}(B)\leq\eta\), the error ball contains a singular matrix, so the data and error bound cannot certify that the exact simplex is full-dimensional. In relative arithmetic, the corresponding danger criterion is \(\kappa_2(B)u\gtrsim1\), where \(u\) is unit roundoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simplex is numerically uncertifiable when perturbation error reaches its smallest edge-matrix singular value; rank and volume decisions may then fail.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is the simplex edge matrix.
\(\widehat B=B+E\) and \(\lVert E\rVert_2\leq\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\sigma_{\min}(B)\leq\eta\), full dimensionality cannot be certified from the perturbed data alone.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: matrix perturbation distance to singularity is standard, but supplied locators do not specifically support the numerical threshold

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A source is required before the numerical threshold can be retained. The statement also centers the uncertainty argument inconsistently: data of the form hat B = B + E with a bound on E define an uncertainty ball around the observed hat B, so certification normally depends on sigma_min(hat B) relative to eta, whereas sigma_min(B) concerns the unknown exact matrix. The relative condition-number criterion likewise needs a specified error model and authoritative locator.

children.title: Ineffective Branching Directions
children.top_down_role: Search growth caused by splits that do not materially improve bounds or inference.

assumptions_latex: \(L(D)\) is a valid lower bound for every parent or child cell \(D\).
The children form a finite cover or partition of \(C\).
\(\tau\geq 0\) is a prescribed negligible-gain tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bound-ineffectiveness is the predicate \(\Delta_j(C)\leq 0\), and \(\tau\)-ineffectiveness is the predicate \(\Delta_j(C)\leq\tau\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound over cell C
replacement lower-bound change from branching direction j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measures whether a split improves the parent lower bound used for pruning.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a live cell \(C\) have valid lower bound \(L(C)\), and let branching in direction \(j\) produce children \(C_1^{(j)},\ldots,C_m^{(j)}\) whose union covers \(C\). Define the replacement bound change by
\[
\Delta_j(C)=\min_{1\leq i\leq m}L(C_i^{(j)})-L(C).
\]
Direction \(j\) is bound-ineffective at \(C\) when \(\Delta_j(C)\leq0\). For a prescribed tolerance \(\tau\geq0\), it is \(\tau\)-ineffective when \(\Delta_j(C)\leq\tau\). Thus directions that leave the replacement bound unchanged, worsen it, or improve it by at most the declared tolerance are classified as ineffective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching direction is ineffective when the weakest child lower bound fails to improve the parent lower bound; it is tolerance-ineffective when that improvement is no greater than the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Ineffective Branching Directions

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

children.title: Node Selection
children.top_down_role: Search-order families for choosing among unresolved spatial regions.

children.title: Best-Bound Search
children.top_down_role: Node ordering directed toward improvement of the global dual bound.

assumptions_latex: \(C_0\) contains the feasible domain \(D\), and \(f^*=\inf_{x\in D}f(x)\) is finite.
For every live cell \(C\), \(L(C)\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in C\cap D\}\).
\(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent in \(D\).
The children of a selected cell form a finite cover of its feasible portion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever a live cell is selected, it belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{C\in\mathcal A}L(C)\); if the active set becomes empty under the stated pruning rule, the returned incumbent satisfies \(0\leq U-f^*\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound over a cell
infimum of the objective over the feasible domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound node selection by the smallest currently valid lower bound.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f\) over a feasible domain \(D\subseteq C_0\). Given a tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), valid cell lower bounds \(L\), and a finite feasible incumbent value \(U\), initialize \(\mathcal A=\{C_0\}\). Repeatedly delete every \(C\in\mathcal A\) satisfying \(L(C)\geq U-\varepsilon\). If \(\mathcal A=\varnothing\), return the incumbent. Otherwise select
\[
C^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{C\in\mathcal A}L(C),
\]
remove \(C^\star\), replace it by finitely many children covering \(C^\star\cap D\), evaluate their bounds and available feasible points, update \(U\), and continue. If the active set becomes empty, then, with \(f^*=\inf_{x\in D}f(x)\), the returned incumbent satisfies \(0\leq U-f^*\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best-bound search processes a live cell with the smallest valid lower bound. It prunes cells whose lower bounds cannot beat the incumbent beyond the requested tolerance, and an empty active set certifies the returned incumbent within that tolerance of the global infimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Best-Bound Search

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

children.title: Depth-First Search
children.top_down_role: Node ordering favoring rapid descent, compact active lists, and state reuse.

knowledge_statements.title: Depth-First Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LIFO node management for descending one branch before visiting alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a rooted subdivision tree and a last-in-first-out stack \(S\), initialize \(S=(C_0)\). While \(S\neq\varnothing\), pop its top cell \(C\). Prune \(C\) if its valid bound meets the prescribed pruning test; otherwise evaluate it, update the incumbent, branch it when required, and push its unpruned children in a fixed order. The next selected cell is therefore the most recently pushed live child. Stop when \(S=\varnothing\) or another declared global stopping condition holds, and return the incumbent and any remaining stack.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Depth-first search uses a stack, repeatedly selecting the newest live child and exhausting a branch before returning to deferred siblings.
assumptions_latex: The search tree is rooted at \(C_0\).
Each processed cell has finitely many ordered children.
The pruning test is valid for the optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selection follows last-in-first-out order among live cells.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

children.title: Layer-Coverage Search Family
children.top_down_role: Node ordering based on depth, refinement layers, or coordinated coverage.

children.title: Breadth-Oriented Search
children.top_down_role: Node ordering emphasizing broad coverage across the active tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Breadth-Oriented Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: FIFO node management that prioritizes older, shallower live cells.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given root \(C_0\), initialize a first-in-first-out queue \(Q=(C_0)\). While \(Q\neq\varnothing\), remove its head cell \(C\). If \(C\) is not pruned, evaluate it, update the incumbent, branch it when required, and append its live children to the tail of \(Q\). With every child assigned depth one greater than its parent, selected depths are nondecreasing. Stop when the queue is empty or a declared global stopping test holds, and return the incumbent and any unprocessed queue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Breadth-oriented search uses a FIFO queue, so cells are processed in nondecreasing tree depth and siblings receive coverage before deeper descendants.
assumptions_latex: Every child has parent depth plus one.
Children are appended only after all previously queued cells.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence of selected node depths is nondecreasing.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

children.title: Layered Tree Search
children.top_down_role: Node ordering coordinated by depth or refinement layer.

knowledge_statements.title: Layered Tree Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth buckets permit arbitrary priority rules within each currently active layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain buckets \(B_d\) of live cells at depth \(d\), initialized by \(B_0=\{C_0\}\) and \(B_d=\varnothing\) for \(d>0\). At each iteration let \(d^\star=\min\{d:B_d\neq\varnothing\}\), select a cell from \(B_{d^\star}\) using a declared within-layer priority rule, and prune or branch it. Insert every live child into \(B_{d^\star+1}\). Do not select a deeper bucket while \(B_{d^\star}\neq\varnothing\). Stop when all buckets are empty or a declared global stopping test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Layered search exhausts the shallowest nonempty depth bucket, while allowing an independent priority rule among cells in that layer.
assumptions_latex: The rooted tree assigns an integer depth to every cell.
Every child of a depth-\(d\) cell has depth \(d+1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No cell at depth \(d+1\) is selected while a live cell remains at depth \(d\).

notation.meaning: bucket of live cells at depth d

children.title: Layer-Coverage Coordination
children.top_down_role: Policies balancing within-layer coverage against progression to deeper layers.

knowledge_statements.title: Layer-Coverage Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fairness invariant coordinating progress across successive finite tree layers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A node-selection policy has strict layer coverage when, for every \(d\geq0\), no node of depth greater than \(d\) is selected until every generated node of depth at most \(d\) has been processed or validly pruned. If the tree is finitely branching and each node evaluation terminates, then every finite generated layer is exhausted after finitely many selections. Hence no live node at a fixed finite depth can be postponed forever by deeper search activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict layer coverage prevents deeper work from indefinitely postponing any generated node at a fixed finite depth.
assumptions_latex: The search tree is finitely branching.
Processing or pruning any selected node terminates in finite time.
The policy satisfies strict layer coverage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generated finite-depth layer is exhausted after finitely many selections.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

children.title: Adaptive Hybrid Search Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies that change emphasis between primal discovery and dual-bound closure.

children.title: Hybrid Search Policies
children.top_down_role: Node-selection policies combining multiple primal or proof-oriented priorities.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Search Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic node selection combining bound-oriented exploration with depth-oriented exploitation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite active-node set \(\mathcal A_t\), node lower bounds \(L_t(v)\), depths \(d(v)\), and an incumbent value \(U_t\), choose weights \(\alpha_t,\beta_t\ge 0\), not both zero, and normalize the two scores to \(\widehat L_t(v),\widehat d_t(v)\in[0,1]\). Select \[v_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in\mathcal A_t}\{\alpha_t\widehat L_t(v)-\beta_t\widehat d_t(v)\},\] using a fixed deterministic tie rule. Process \(v_t\), remove it from \(\mathcal A_t\), insert every child not pruned by \(L_t(w)\ge U_t\), update \(U_t\), and repeat until \(\mathcal A_t=\varnothing\) or a prescribed global-gap test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select each active region using a weighted combination of its lower bound and depth, then update children, pruning, and the incumbent until exhaustion or certified termination.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A_t\) is finite at every iteration.
Every active node has a valid lower bound and finite depth.
Score normalization and tie breaking are fixed before selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule defines one reproducible hybrid node choice whenever \(\mathcal A_t\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for node v

review_flags: Exact hybrid scoring and normalization conventions vary by implementation; a supporting node-selection source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but the weighted score, normalization, pruning convention, and stopping interface are implementation-specific and unsupported by cited evidence.

children.title: Adaptive Search Switching
children.top_down_role: Dynamic changes in node-selection emphasis as search conditions evolve.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Search Switching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-dependent switching between exploration and exploitation policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) and \(D\) be deterministic selection rules on nonempty active-node sets. Maintain a mode \(m_t\in\{E,D\}\), a stagnation count \(s_t\), and an exploitation-run length \(r_t\). Given thresholds \(S,R\in\mathbb N_{>0}\), set \[m_{t+1}=\begin{cases}D,&m_t=E,\ s_t\ge S,\ E,&m_t=D,\ r_t\ge R,\ m_t,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}\] Select the next node using \(m_{t+1}\). Reset \(s_t\) after a strict incumbent improvement and reset \(r_t\) upon entering \(E\); otherwise increment the applicable counter. Stop under the search algorithm's ordinary exhaustion or gap criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Switch from exploration after sustained incumbent stagnation and return from exploitation after a bounded dive, with counters reset by improvement or mode changes.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(D\) return an active node whenever the active set is nonempty.
\(S\) and \(R\) are positive finite integers.
Incumbent improvement is measured using a fixed numerical tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every nonterminal iteration has a uniquely determined mode and node-selection rule.
review_flags: Threshold-based switching is a precise admissible policy, but the intended canonical transition rule lacks a supplied source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic fit, but the threshold rule and timing of counter resets and increments are not canonically determined or sourced.

children.title: Search-Policy Transition Criteria
children.top_down_role: Signals governing changes between incumbent-oriented and bound-oriented search.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Policy Transition Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete predicates governing transitions between bound search and depth search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iteration \(t\), let \(s_t\) count consecutive iterations without an incumbent decrease exceeding \(\varepsilon_I>0\), let \(r_t\) be the current depth-search run length, and let \(g_t=U_t-\min_{v\in\mathcal A_t}L_t(v)\). For fixed \(S,R\in\mathbb N_{>0}\) and \(\varepsilon_g\ge0\), define \[T_{E\to D}(t)\iff s_t\ge S\ \land\ g_t>\varepsilon_g,\qquad T_{D\to E}(t)\iff r_t\ge R\ \lor\ \mathcal D_t=\varnothing,\] where \(\mathcal D_t\) is the eligible continuation set of the current dive. No policy transition occurs when the applicable predicate is false.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enter depth search after significant stagnation while the global gap remains open; return after the dive limit or when no eligible continuation exists.
assumptions_latex: Every active node has a valid lower bound.
\(U_t\) is finite whenever the gap predicate is evaluated.
Counters and tolerances use fixed update conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed predicates partition each mode's iterations into transition and continuation cases.

notation.meaning: eligible children or descendants continuing the current dive
predicate for transition from policy p to policy q

review_flags: The criteria are implementation-level design choices; no supplied locator establishes these particular predicates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predicates fit the transition-criteria leaf, but they are unsupported design choices. Moreover, the definition of the gap requires the active set to be nonempty, which is not stated.

children.title: Active-Node Pool
children.top_down_role: Storage, prioritization, suspension, and reactivation of unresolved regions.

children.title: Priority-Queue Node Pools
children.top_down_role: Active-region management keyed by bounds or composite priorities.

knowledge_statements.title: Priority-Queue Node Pools
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active regions represented by a heap ordered by valid bounds or composite priorities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the finite active-node pool \(\mathcal A\) by a priority queue \(Q\) containing exactly one entry \((k(v),\tau(v),v)\) for every \(v\in\mathcal A\). Here \(k(v)\in\mathbb R\) is a lower-bound or composite priority and \(\tau(v)\) is a unique insertion index. Order entries lexicographically by \((k(v),\tau(v))\). The operation \(\operatorname{extract}(Q)\) removes and returns the node with minimum key, insertion and deletion preserve the representation invariant, and changing a node's priority replaces its stored key. With a binary heap, insertion, deletion, and extraction require \(O(\log |Q|)\) comparisons, while minimum inspection requires \(O(1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store each active node once in a deterministically tie-broken min-priority queue; a binary heap supports logarithmic updates and extraction.
assumptions_latex: The active pool is finite.
Priority keys are totally ordered real values.
Insertion indices are unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The queue minimum is exactly \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in\mathcal A}(k(v),\tau(v))\).
review_flags: A binary-heap priority queue and its operation bounds are standard, but a precise supporting locator is still needed.
