children.title: Depth-Oriented Node Pool Family
children.top_down_role: Search-state organization for depth-oriented traversal.

children.title: Stack Node Pools
children.top_down_role: Last-in-first-out organization of active regional nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Stack Node Pools
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Last-in-first-out storage implementing depth-oriented processing of active nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the active-node pool by a finite sequence \(S=(v_1,\ldots,v_m)\). Define \(\operatorname{push}(S,v)=(v_1,\ldots,v_m,v)\) and, for \(m>0\), \(\operatorname{pop}(S)=(v_m,(v_1,\ldots,v_{m-1}))\). When processing a node, push its unpruned children in the reverse of a fixed preferred order. Consequently, the preferred child is processed next, and descendants continue to be processed before nodes stored below their ancestor's siblings. Array-backed push and pop take amortized \(O(1)\) time and the representation occupies \(O(m)\) node references.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store active nodes in last-in-first-out order, pushing children in reverse preference order so the preferred branch is explored first and deeply.
assumptions_latex: Each processed node has finitely many children.
Child preference and insertion order are deterministic.
Pruned children are not pushed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever \(S\ne()\), selection returns the most recently pushed unprocessed node.
review_flags: LIFO semantics and standard array-stack bounds are routine, but no exact source locator was supplied.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Diving Node Pools
children.top_down_role: Pool organization supporting persistent traversal along selected descendant paths.

knowledge_statements.title: Diving Node Pools
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth-first continuation along a preferred child with deferred alternatives retained for backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a current node \(v\) and an empty stack \(S\). After processing \(v\), form its ordered list of unpruned children \((w_1,\ldots,w_k)\). If \(k>0\), push \(w_k,\ldots,w_2\) onto \(S\) and set \(v\leftarrow w_1\). If \(k=0\) and \(S\ne()\), set \(v\leftarrow\operatorname{pop}(S)\). If \(k=0\) and \(S=()\), terminate. Continue until termination or the enclosing global-search stopping test holds. Thus one preferred branch is followed without interruption while every deferred unpruned alternative remains available for later backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Follow the preferred unpruned child repeatedly, stack alternative children, and backtrack to the latest deferred alternative when the dive cannot continue.
assumptions_latex: Each node generates a finite ordered child list.
Pruning decisions are final for the current search state.
The initial node is eligible for processing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generated unpruned node is either current, stored exactly once in \(S\), or already processed.
review_flags: The depth-first invariant is standard, but a global-optimization source for this diving-pool formulation is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm accurately describes a depth-first diving pool and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports this particular global-search formulation and invariant.

children.title: Dive Backtracking State
children.top_down_role: Search-state organization for returning from interrupted or exhausted dives.

knowledge_statements.title: Dive Backtracking State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal state sufficient to resume deferred branches after a depth-oriented dive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), represent dive state by \(B_t=(v_t,S_t,\rho_t)\), where \(v_t\) is the current node, \(S_t\) is an ordered stack of deferred unpruned nodes, and \(\rho_t\) stores the incumbent and pruning revision under which the stack was formed. The invariant is that each generated but unprocessed node is either \(v_t\) or occurs exactly once in \(S_t\). On backtracking, repeatedly discard any top entry made ineligible by the current incumbent or pruning revision; then pop the first eligible entry as the new current node. The dive is exhausted exactly when no current node exists and \(S_t\) is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track the current node, deferred alternatives, and pruning revision; backtracking discards newly ineligible entries and resumes the latest eligible alternative.
assumptions_latex: Pruning eligibility can be reevaluated from a stored node and the current search state.
Each deferred node is inserted at most once.
Stack order is deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The state \(B_t\) determines either the next backtracking node or exhaustion of the dive.
review_flags: The minimal revision metadata is implementation-dependent and lacks a supporting source locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but the claimed revision metadata and the rule for determining newly ineligible entries are implementation-dependent and not formally specified or sourced.

children.title: Multi-Queue Adaptive Pool System
children.top_down_role: Separate pools for distinct search priorities or processing regimes.

children.title: Multiple-Queue Node Pools
children.top_down_role: Separate active-node queues serving distinct search priorities.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Queue Node Pools
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One active-node set indexed simultaneously by several search-policy queues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) be a finite active-node set and let \(k_1,\ldots,k_q\) be priority functions. Represent the pool by queues \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_q\), where each \(Q_j\) contains a handle to every node \(v\in\mathcal A\), ordered by \((k_j(v),\tau(v))\). A shared status record identifies whether \(v\) remains active. Inserting a node creates one handle in every queue. Selecting from \(Q_j\) repeatedly removes stale minima until an active handle is found; the selected node is then marked inactive globally. This lazy-deletion representation preserves \[\{v:\text{an active handle to }v\text{ exists in }Q_j\}=\mathcal A\] for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Index every active node under several priority orders, using shared status and lazy deletion so any queue can select without duplicating logical activity.
assumptions_latex: The number \(q\) of queues is finite and positive.
Every priority function is totally ordered after deterministic tie breaking.
Status changes are visible to all queues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each queue represents the same logical active set while exposing a different minimum-priority node.

notation.meaning: priority function used by queue j
unique tie-breaking index of node v

review_flags: The lazy multi-index representation is precise but no source specifically supporting global-search multiple-queue pools was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is coherent and fits the multiple-queue leaf, but its shared-status and lazy-deletion design is a particular implementation without supporting evidence or an explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Adaptive Pool Rebalancing
children.top_down_role: Dynamic reassignment of attention or capacity among active-node pools.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Pool Rebalancing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feedback update reallocating selection opportunities among node-pool policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q\) queues, maintain positive weights \(w_{j,t}\) with \(\sum_{j=1}^q w_{j,t}=1\). After a block of selections, assign each queue a bounded reward \(r_{j,t}\in[0,1]\), such as normalized incumbent improvement or bound progress, and update \[\widetilde w_{j,t+1}=w_{j,t}\exp(\eta r_{j,t}),\qquad w_{j,t+1}=(1-\gamma)\frac{\widetilde w_{j,t+1}}{\sum_{i=1}^q\widetilde w_{i,t+1}}+\frac{\gamma}{q},\] where \(\eta>0\) and \(0<\gamma\le1\). Use \(w_{j,t+1}\) as queue-selection frequencies during the next block; remove stale entries before extracting a node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the selection share of queues producing progress while retaining a positive exploration share for every queue.
assumptions_latex: Rewards satisfy \(r_{j,t}\in[0,1]\).
Initial weights are positive and sum to one.
\(\eta>0\) and \(0<\gamma\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated weights sum to one and satisfy \(w_{j,t+1}\ge\gamma/q>0\) for every queue.

notation.meaning: observed progress reward for queue j
learning rate and mandatory exploration rate

review_flags: This multiplicative-weights rebalancing rule is one valid specification, but the taxonomy does not identify it as the intended canonical rule.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiplicative-weights algorithm fits adaptive rebalancing, and its stated weight bound is correct, but the rule is a noncanonical design choice. The mechanism translating weights into queue-selection frequencies is also unspecified.

children.title: Cross-Queue Arbitration
children.top_down_role: Selection regimes governing competition among multiple active-node queues.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Queue Arbitration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic arbitration among candidate minima proposed by distinct node queues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), let each nonempty queue \(Q_j\) propose its first active node \(v_{j,t}\). Compute an arbitration score \(a_{j,t}=A_t(j,v_{j,t})\in\mathbb R\), where \(A_t\) uses only information available before selection. Choose \[j_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j:Q_j\ne\varnothing}(a_{j,t},j),\qquad v_t=v_{j_t,t}.\] Mark \(v_t\) inactive in the shared pool, remove its live handles or leave them for lazy deletion, process the node, and update all affected priorities. If every queue is empty after stale entries are removed, report pool exhaustion. The index tie rule makes arbitration deterministic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each queue proposes its best active node; a common score and fixed tie rule choose one proposal and deactivate that node globally.
assumptions_latex: All queues index one shared logical active set.
Every nonempty logical pool yields at least one live proposal.
Arbitration scores are finite and computed before selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the logical pool is nonempty, arbitration selects exactly one active node reproducibly.

notation.meaning: active candidate proposed by queue j

review_flags: The generic arbitration interface is unambiguous, but the intended scoring function requires domain-specific sourcing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits cross-queue arbitration, but the arbitrary score function leaves the substantive arbitration policy unspecified, and no source supports this interface as the intended knowledge statement.

children.title: Tree-Integrated Incumbent Search
children.top_down_role: Search mechanisms for obtaining and improving globally valid feasible solutions.

children.title: Node-Local Optimization
children.top_down_role: Regional nonlinear optimization used to seek feasible points.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Local Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional nonlinear optimization for producing feasible incumbent candidates inside a search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a node region \(X_v\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), solve the local nonlinear program \[\min_{x\in X_v} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_i(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\quad h_j(x)=0\ (j=1,\ldots,p)\] from a prescribed start \(x_v^0\in X_v\), using a terminating local solver. If the returned point \(\widehat x_v\) satisfies \(g_i(\widehat x_v)\le\varepsilon_f\), \(|h_j(\widehat x_v)|\le\varepsilon_f\), and \(\widehat x_v\in X_v\), accept it as a feasible candidate. Replace the incumbent \((U,x^I)\) by \((f(\widehat x_v),\widehat x_v)\) exactly when \(f(\widehat x_v)<U-\varepsilon_I\); otherwise retain the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run a local nonlinear solver within the node, verify feasibility explicitly, and update the incumbent only after a sufficient objective improvement.
assumptions_latex: The node region \(X_v\) and constraint residuals are evaluable.
The local solver terminates with a point or failure status.
Feasibility and improvement tolerances are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any accepted update is feasible to tolerance within \(X_v\) and improves the incumbent by more than \(\varepsilon_I\).

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 'Globalized' Local Optimization Strategies, Combined with Grid Search or Random Search p. 24

review_flags: The locator supports combining global and local optimization provisionally; the exact node-local acceptance interface remains to be checked.

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.2 'Globalized' Local Optimization Strategies, Combined with Grid Search or Random Search p. 24

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits node-local incumbent search and is mathematically coherent, but the cited section only provisionally supports combining global and local optimization; it does not establish the exact node-restricted solve, tolerance checks, or incumbent-update interface.

children.title: Relaxation-Solution Repair
children.top_down_role: Restoration, projection, and rounding interfaces starting from relaxation solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Solution Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection, rounding, and restoration of a node-relaxation solution into a feasible incumbent candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation solution \(x^R\in X_v\), first apply a prescribed rounding or structural map \(R\) to obtain \(y^0=R(x^R)\). Then solve the restoration problem \[y^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in X_v}\left\{\|y-y^0\|_2^2+\lambda\left(\sum_{i=1}^m[g_i(y)]_+^2+\sum_{j=1}^p h_j(y)^2\right)\right\},\] with \(lambda>0\), respecting all required discrete restrictions. Accept \(y^*\) only if the original constraints satisfy the prescribed feasibility tolerance. If accepted and \(f(y^*)<U-\varepsilon_I\), update the incumbent; otherwise return repair failure without changing \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round the relaxation point, minimize distance plus constraint violation, verify original feasibility, and update the incumbent only upon sufficient improvement.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation solution \(x^R\) belongs to the node relaxation region.
The map \(R\) enforces required discrete structure or flags failure.
The restoration subproblem terminates with a candidate or failure status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful repair returns a tolerance-feasible point satisfying all required discrete restrictions; an incumbent update also strictly improves \(U\).
review_flags: The repair template is mathematically complete, but no supplied source supports this particular penalty-restoration formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the repair leaf, but the particular penalty-restoration model is unsupported. Required discrete restrictions are not represented in the displayed feasible domain and may be lost during restoration; additionally, the statement writes \(lambda>0\) instead of \(\lambda>0\).

children.title: Dive-Neighborhood Incumbent Search
children.top_down_role: Restricted searches directed toward rapid incumbent improvement.

children.title: Diving Search
children.top_down_role: Restricted incumbent searches following selected descendant paths.

knowledge_statements.title: Diving Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree-integrated primal heuristic for a minimization search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an active node region \(R_0\), set \(k=0\). Solve its relaxation, choose a preferred child \(R_{k+1}\subset R_k\) using relaxation values, constraint propagation, or pseudocosts, and continue without returning intervening siblings to the selection queue. Stop when a feasible point \(x\in F\cap R_k\) is obtained, the current region is certified infeasible, a prescribed depth or effort limit is reached, or no child remains. Return the feasible point only when \(f(x)<U\); otherwise return failure. Unexplored siblings remain valid tree nodes, so the dive itself neither proves their exclusion nor changes valid global bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly follow preferred children to seek a feasible improving point. The dive may update the incumbent but cannot discard unexplored siblings without separate certificates.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\) is the feasible set and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is minimized.
\(U\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is the current incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful dive returns \(x\in F\) with \(f(x)<U\); otherwise it supplies no optimality certificate.

notation.meaning: region at depth k of the selected dive path

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Diving Search leaf and is internally coherent, but its particular child-selection, queue-handling, and stopping policy is one of several possible diving variants and has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Neighborhood Search
children.top_down_role: Restricted incumbent searches exploring a localized region around a candidate.

knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent-centered primal search within a prescribed neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible incumbent \(\hat x\in F\) and a neighborhood operator \(N\), form the restricted problem \(\min\{f(x):x\in F\cap N(\hat x)\}\). Apply an exact or explicitly effort-limited local solver to this restriction. If it produces \(y\in F\cap N(\hat x)\) with \(f(y)<f(\hat x)\), replace \(\hat x\) by \(y\) and optionally repeat with \(N(y)\). Stop after no accepted improvement or after the effort limit. Unless the restricted problem is solved globally, failure to improve certifies neither neighborhood optimality nor global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search a prescribed region around an incumbent, accept only feasible improvements, and claim neighborhood optimality only when the restricted problem is solved exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\) is the feasible set and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is minimized.
\(N(x)\subseteq X\) is defined for every incumbent considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted update satisfies \(y\in F\) and \(f(y)<f(\hat x)\).

notation.meaning: search neighborhood centered at the incumbent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches incumbent-centered neighborhood search and appropriately limits optimality claims, but no source supports this generic exact-or-effort-limited formulation or its coordination policy.

children.title: Dive-Neighborhood Coordination
children.top_down_role: Search regimes transferring candidates or effort between dives and local neighborhoods.

knowledge_statements.title: Dive-Neighborhood Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordination rule combining pathwise diving with incumbent-centered refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select an active tree region and run a bounded dive. For every feasible dive output \(x_d\), set \(z=x_d\) and run neighborhood search from \(z\). Among all feasible points produced, choose \(y\) of least objective value and update the incumbent by \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,f(y)\}\). Return all unexplored dive siblings to the active pool unless independently fathomed. Information from either heuristic may guide priorities, but a region is removed only by a valid fathoming certificate. Stop the coordinated heuristic at its effort limit and return the best feasible point found, if any.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use diving to generate candidates and neighborhood search to refine them, while keeping heuristic decisions separate from certified tree pruning.
assumptions_latex: The diving and neighborhood procedures return only points verified to lie in \(F\).
\(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent or \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update preserves feasibility and gives \(U_{\mathrm{new}}\leq U_{\mathrm{old}}\) without weakening tree validity.

notation.meaning: feasible point produced by a dive

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local scope fit, and the incumbent and pruning safeguards are sound. The prescribed dive-then-neighborhood policy is noncanonical and requires a source establishing this specific coordination scheme.

children.title: Concurrent Search-Tree Coordination
children.top_down_role: Concurrent regional processing and coordination of search-wide information.

children.title: Shared-Memory Tree Search
children.top_down_role: Concurrent node processing with shared proof state.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Memory Tree Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent regional processing with synchronized shared proof state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a shared active pool with the root region, incumbent \(U=+\infty\), and a lock or atomic protocol. Each worker atomically removes one active region \(R\), computes valid bounds and feasible candidates, atomically decreases \(U\) when an improving feasible point is found, and atomically publishes every unfathomed child. A worker may discard \(R\) only using a valid certificate evaluated against an incumbent value no larger than the one read. Terminate only when the active pool is empty and no worker owns unpublished work. The returned incumbent is globally optimal when every processed region was either exhaustively resolved or validly fathomed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers process nodes concurrently through a synchronized pool and incumbent, terminating only when no queued, owned, or unpublished region remains.
assumptions_latex: Every generated child family covers its parent feasible region.
Shared-pool and incumbent operations are linearizable.
Every regional bound and fathoming certificate is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the incumbent is globally optimal over the root region, provided a feasible incumbent exists.

notation.meaning: regional subproblem owned by a worker

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits shared-memory tree search, but its concurrency, linearizability, work-publication, termination, and global-optimality conditions constitute a nontrivial parallel-correctness claim without cited support.

children.title: Distributed Node Farming
children.top_down_role: Allocation of regional subproblems across workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Node Farming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributed allocation and recovery of regional subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coordinator maintains identifiers for pending, assigned, completed, and fathomed regions. It assigns each pending region \(R\) to a worker, records the assignment durably, and accepts returned children, bounds, certificates, and feasible candidates only after checking their region identifier. An assignment lost through worker failure is returned to pending status unless its result was durably committed. Duplicate execution is permitted, but duplicate results are incorporated idempotently. The search terminates only when no pending or assigned region remains and all generated descendants are durably accounted for. Under valid subdivision and fathoming, the best returned feasible point is then globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Farm identified regions to workers, recover lost assignments, merge duplicate results idempotently, and terminate only after all generated work is accounted for.
assumptions_latex: Every subdivision covers the parent feasible region.
Committed certificates and bounds are valid for their identified regions.
Lost assignments are eventually detected and reassigned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhaustive accounting of all regional identifiers preserves completeness and yields a globally optimal incumbent at termination.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits distributed node farming, but durable assignment, failure recovery, idempotent integration, termination detection, and completeness depend on a distributed failure model and protocol for which no source is supplied.

children.title: Asynchronous Proof-State Exchange
children.top_down_role: Delayed communication of incumbents, lower bounds, and active-work status.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Proof-State Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety invariant for delayed incumbent, bound, and work-status messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In asynchronous minimization, incumbent messages may only replace \(U\) by a verified feasible value \(U'\leq U\), and regional lower-bound messages may only replace \(L(R)\) by a valid value \(L'(R)\geq L(R)\). A worker using stale \(U_s\geq U\) may miss pruning but remains safe when it fathoms only if \(L(R)\geq U_s\). Global termination or a reported lower bound must additionally account for every queued, in-transit, and worker-owned region; absence of local work alone is insufficient. Thus delayed monotone proof information affects efficiency, whereas unaccounted work can invalidate completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delayed monotone bounds and incumbents preserve pruning safety, but global termination requires accounting for queued, owned, and in-transit work.
assumptions_latex: Every incumbent value communicated is attained by a feasible point.
Every communicated \(L(R)\) is a valid lower bound on region \(R\).
Messages are eventually delivered or their loss is detected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stale proof values delay progress but do not cause invalid fathoming when \(L(R)\geq U_s\) is required.

notation.meaning: possibly stale incumbent value read by a worker
valid lower bound for region R

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle correctly distinguishes monotone stale proof information from unaccounted work, but the asynchronous safety and termination claims require authoritative support and a more explicit communication/failure model.

children.title: Global Fathoming Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Logical removal of regions and construction of verifiable global-search certificates.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Global Optimization: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Global Optimization: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications

children.title: Fathoming Families
children.top_down_role: Classical logical reasons for permanently removing a regional subproblem.

children.title: Bound-Dominance Fathoming
children.top_down_role: Regional exclusion by comparison of a valid node bound with incumbent information.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Dominance Fathoming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional exclusion using a valid lower bound and feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization over \(F\subseteq X\), let \(R\subseteq X\) be an active region, let \(L(R)\) satisfy \(L(R)\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap R\}\), and let \(U=f(\hat x)\) for some \(\hat x\in F\). If \(L(R)\geq U\), then every feasible point in \(R\) has objective value at least \(U\). Consequently, removing \(R\) cannot eliminate a point strictly better than the incumbent. The certificate consists of the verifiable lower-bound derivation, the feasible incumbent, and the comparison \(L(R)\geq U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region is safely discarded when its valid lower bound is no better than the value of a verified feasible incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(L(R)\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap R\}\).
\(\hat x\in F\) and \(U=f(\hat x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(R)\geq U\) implies that \(R\) contains no point with objective value below \(U\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

children.title: Infeasibility Fathoming
children.top_down_role: Regional exclusion through certified infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Fathoming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional exclusion by a checkable certificate of empty feasibility intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) and \(J\) be index sets, let \(F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\leq 0\text{ for every }i\in I,\ h_j(x)=0\text{ for every }j\in J\}\), and let \(R\subseteq X\) be active. An infeasibility certificate for \(R\) is a checkable derivation whose validity implies \(F\cap R=\varnothing\), such as a valid relaxation of the regional constraints that is itself infeasible. Once the certificate is verified, \(R\) may be removed independently of the incumbent value because it contains no feasible point. Failure of a feasibility search is not such a certificate unless that search is complete for the regional feasibility problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discard a region only after a verifiable argument establishes that it contains no feasible point; unsuccessful heuristic search is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(J\) index the inequality and equality constraints, respectively.
Every constraint relaxation used by the certificate contains \(F\cap R\).
The certificate-checking procedure is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A verified certificate implying \(F\cap R=\varnothing\) permits unconditional fathoming of \(R\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

children.title: Resolved-Region Fathoming
children.top_down_role: Removal of a region whose remaining optimization status is certified.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolved-Region Fathoming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fathoming after the regional optimization problem has been completely resolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an active region \(R\), suppose a sound regional procedure certifies either that \(F\cap R=\varnothing\) or that a feasible point \(x_R\in F\cap R\) attains \(v_R=\min\{f(x):x\in F\cap R\}\). In the second case update the incumbent by \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,v_R\}\). The region may then be removed because its entire feasible contribution has been represented by its certified optimum; no descendant of \(R\) can improve the updated incumbent. A merely stationary or locally optimal point does not resolve \(R\) unless additional conditions certify regional global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region may be removed once it is certified infeasible or its exact regional optimum has been found and incorporated into the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The regional solver's infeasibility or global-optimality certificate is sound.
Any certified regional optimizer is verified feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After incorporating \(v_R\), fathoming \(R\) cannot remove a point better than the updated incumbent.

notation.meaning: certified global minimum value over the region

source_refs.locator: 8.4 Proof of Convergence to the Global Minimum p. 282

source_witnesses.locator: 8.4 Proof of Convergence to the Global Minimum p. 282

children.title: Relational Fathoming Family
children.top_down_role: Removal based on equivalence or dominance relations among regions.

children.title: Dominance Fathoming
children.top_down_role: Regional removal based on a validated dominance relation.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Fathoming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relational exclusion through an objective-nonworsening map into covered search space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be active and let \(S\) be a region already retained or completely processed. A dominance certificate is a checkable map \(T:F\cap R\to F\cap S\) satisfying \(f(Tx)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\cap R\). If all feasible possibilities in \(S\) remain represented in the proof state, then every feasible point removed with \(R\) has a represented counterpart of no greater objective value. Hence \(R\) may be fathomed without changing the global minimum value. The certificate must establish feasibility preservation, objective dominance, and coverage of the image region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discard a region when every feasible point in it maps to a retained or processed feasible point having no worse objective value.
assumptions_latex: \(T(F\cap R)\subseteq F\cap S\).
\(f(Tx)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\cap R\).
The proof state still represents all feasible possibilities in \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Removing \(R\) preserves the global minimum value.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mapping certificate fits dominance fathoming and states feasibility, objective, and image-coverage requirements. Its proof-state representation condition and preservation claim are nontrivial and uncited.

children.title: Symmetry Fathoming
children.top_down_role: Regional removal based on validated search-space equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry Fathoming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbit-based exclusion under exact problem symmetries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a group \(G\) act on \(X\) such that \(gF=F\) and \(f(gx)=f(x)\) for every \(g\in G\) and \(x\in F\). If active region \(R\) satisfies \(R=gS\) for some \(g\in G\), where the orbit-representative region \(S\) is retained or completely processed, then \(x\mapsto g^{-1}x\) maps \(F\cap R\) bijectively to \(F\cap S\) without changing objective values. The group element, regional equivalence, feasibility invariance, objective invariance, and continued representation of \(S\) form a certificate permitting \(R\) to be fathomed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region symmetric to a retained representative may be discarded when the symmetry preserves feasibility and objective values exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(gF=F\) and \(f(gx)=f(x)\) for every relevant \(g\in G\).
\(R=gS\) for a retained or completely processed region \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fathoming \(R\) preserves the set of attainable objective values and therefore the global minimum.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact group-action formulation is mathematically coherent and fits symmetry fathoming, but no source supports the regional equivalence and representative-retention certificate used here.

children.title: Relation-Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions limiting safe use of dominance or symmetry information.

knowledge_statements.title: Relation-Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure mechanisms for relational fathoming certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Relational fathoming is unsafe if feasibility preservation, objective nonworsening, or image coverage fails. Concretely, let \(F=\{a,b\}\), \(R=\{a\}\), \(S=\{b\}\), \(f(a)=0\), and \(f(b)=1\). The claimed relation \(T(a)=b\) preserves feasibility but violates \(f(Ta)\leq f(a)\); processing \(S\) and fathoming \(R\) therefore loses the unique global minimizer. Likewise, even an objective-preserving symmetry cannot justify deletion when its representative region has also been discarded without resolution. Valid relational pruning consequently requires the stated relation on every feasible point removed and durable representation of every image.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relational pruning can lose the optimum if the relation fails to preserve feasibility, objective dominance, or a durably represented image.
assumptions_latex: Relational fathoming is proposed using a map from \(F\cap R\) into a representative region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of any required relation predicate can make fathoming \(R\) eliminate the global minimizer.

children.title: Primal Certificate Components

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Certificate Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal side of a deterministic minimization certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the problem \(f^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\), a primal certificate consists of a point \(\hat x\), evidence that \(\hat x\in F\) under the declared feasibility tolerances, and a reproducible objective evaluation \(U=f(\hat x)\). These components certify \(f^*\le U\). If objective or constraint computations are inexact, the certificate must instead provide a validated enclosure proving feasibility and an outward-rounded upper bound \(U\ge f(\hat x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A validated feasible incumbent and a rigorous upper objective bound certify an upper bound on the global minimum.

\(f:F\to\mathbb R\) is the minimization objective.

children.title: Cross-Component Consistency
children.top_down_role: Compatibility requirements between primal evidence and proof-side evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Component Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition joining primal and dual certificate data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), and define \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). A primal-dual certificate is cross-component consistent when its incumbent, regional bounds, feasibility rules, objective convention, and tolerances refer to this same minimization problem; the certified regions cover all of \(F\); \(U\) is a valid upper bound on \(f^*\); and \(L\) is derived only from valid regional lower bounds. Under these conditions, \(L\le f^*\le U\), so \(G=U-L\ge0\) and \(0\le U-f^*\le G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal and dual data must use the same model, tolerances, and exhaustive search state; their certified gap then bounds the upper-bound error.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), and \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).
The primal and dual components use identical model and tolerance conventions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le f^*\le U\) and \(0\le U-f^*\le U-L\).

children.title: Absolute-Gap Certificates
children.top_down_role: Accuracy certification on an absolute objective scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute-Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive global-optimality certification for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\hat x\in F\) be a certified feasible incumbent, let \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), and suppose \(L\le f^*\le f(\hat x)\le U\). For a prescribed tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\ge0\), the inequality \(U-L\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\) is an absolute-gap certificate. It implies \(0\le f(\hat x)-f^*\le U-L\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\), so \(\hat x\) is globally optimal within additive objective error \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a certified feasible incumbent lies between rigorous lower and upper bounds whose gap is at most the absolute tolerance, its objective error is at most that tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\hat x\in F\) and \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).
\(L\le f^*\le f(\hat x)\le U\).
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-L\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\Rightarrow 0\le f(\hat x)-f^*\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\).

children.title: Relative-Gap Certificates
children.top_down_role: Scale-aware accuracy certification and its near-zero boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware certificate with an explicit denominator floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\tau>0\) and define the symmetric relative gap by \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}=(U-L)/\max\{\tau,|U|,|L|\}\) for certified bounds \(L\le f^*\le U\). For \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\), the condition \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\) certifies \(U-f^*\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{\tau,|U|,|L|\}\). The values of the denominator convention and \(\tau\) are indispensable certificate data, particularly near zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative certificate divides the certified gap by a declared scale floor and records that convention explicitly.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le f^*\le U\).
\(\tau>0\) and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\Rightarrow U-f^*\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{\tau,|U|,|L|\}\).

children.title: Mixed Absolute–Relative Certificates
children.top_down_role: Combined accuracy conventions used in solver-facing termination.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Absolute–Relative Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-facing certificate combining additive and scale-dependent tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For certified bounds \(L\le f^*\le U\), choose \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\) and a declared nonnegative scale \(s(U,L)\). The stopping inequality \(U-L\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}s(U,L)\) certifies \(U-f^*\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}s(U,L)\). A common explicit choice is \(s(U,L)=\max\{|U|,|L|\}\); the certificate must record the chosen scale rather than treating formulations as interchangeable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certified gap may be bounded by an additive tolerance plus a declared objective-dependent relative term.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le f^*\le U\).
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\).
\(s(U,L)\ge0\) is fixed by the certificate convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-f^*\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}s(U,L)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the conclusion follows directly from certified primal-dual ordering and the stated mixed stopping inequality

children.title: Certificate Integrity
children.top_down_role: Reliability boundaries for bounds, feasibility claims, gaps, and distributed search state.

children.title: Invalid Lower-Bound Failure
children.top_down_role: Loss of certification through invalid relaxations or unsafe numerical treatment.

knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Lower-Bound Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certification fails when any asserted lower bound is not rigorous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x:0\le x\le1\}\), whose optimum is \(f^*=0\). The feasible incumbent \(\hat x=1/2\) gives \(U=1/2\). If an unsafe relaxation or numerical computation reports \(L=0.49\), then \(U-L=0.01\), but \(L\le f^*\) is false and the incumbent's true error is \(U-f^*=0.5\). Thus a small computed gap is not a certificate unless every lower-bound inequality is validated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small gap formed with an invalid lower bound can drastically understate the incumbent's true global error.
assumptions_latex: The optimization problem and reported bounds are as displayed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-L=0.01\) does not imply \(U-f^*\le0.01\) because \(L>f^*\).

children.title: False or Numerically Infeasible Incumbents
children.top_down_role: Primal-bound corruption caused by insufficient feasibility validation.

knowledge_statements.title: False or Numerically Infeasible Incumbents
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal certification requires validated, not merely approximate, feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M>0\), consider minimizing \(f(x)=-Mx\) subject to \(x=0\), so \(f^*=0\). If a feasibility test accepts \(\hat x=\delta>0\) because \(|\delta|\) is below an unchecked tolerance, it may report \(U=-M\delta\). This is not an upper bound because \(\hat x\notin F\); moreover, \(M\delta\) can be arbitrarily large while \(\delta\) remains small. Consequently, an incumbent cannot support a global certificate without validated feasibility and objective evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tiny constraint violation can produce arbitrarily corrupt primal bounds when objective sensitivity is large.
assumptions_latex: The exact feasible set is \(F=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat x\notin F\), so \(U=-M\delta\) is not a certified upper bound on \(f^*=0\).

children.title: Near-Zero Gap-Scaling Pathologies

children.title: Gap Scaling Conventions
children.top_down_role: Normalization choices used when interpreting relative or mixed optimality gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap Scaling Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit absolute, relative, and mixed gap normalizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For certified minimization bounds \(L\le f^*\le U\), define the absolute gap by \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}=U-L\). Given a declared floor \(\tau>0\), define the symmetric relative gap by \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}=(U-L)/\max\{\tau,|U|,|L|\}\). Given tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\), define mixed acceptance by \(U-L\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{|U|,|L|\}\). These are distinct conventions and must be stored with every reported certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gap values are meaningful only together with their absolute, relative, or mixed normalization convention and scale floor.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le f^*\le U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed formulas uniquely determine the reported gap convention.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: formulas explicitly define internally consistent gap conventions
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulas are internally consistent and definition is the correct kind, but the selected relative and mixed conventions and the universal storage requirement lack an authoritative citation.

children.title: Near-Zero Objective Regimes
children.top_down_role: Certificate behavior when primal or bound reference values approach zero.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Zero Objective Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure relative normalization degenerates when objective bounds approach zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the unregularized convention \(r=(U-L)/\max\{|U|,|L|\}\), the pair \(L=0\), \(U=\delta>0\) has absolute gap \(\delta\to0\) but relative gap \(r=1\) for every \(\delta\). At \(L=U=0\), the expression is undefined. Hence pure relative stopping is discontinuous or undefined near a zero objective scale; a positive denominator floor or an absolute tolerance is required for stable certification there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near zero, arbitrarily small absolute gaps can retain unit relative gap, and the zero-zero case is undefined.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le U\).
The denominator has no positive floor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: As \(\delta\downarrow0\), \(U-L\to0\) while \(r=1\), and \(r\) is undefined at \(L=U=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit limiting family establishes the near-zero pathology
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The limiting example is correct, but the broader claim that a floor or absolute tolerance is required for stable certification is unsourced and depends on the adopted stopping convention.

children.title: Scaling-Induced Certificate Instability
children.top_down_role: Ambiguous or unstable certificate outcomes caused by poorly matched scaling conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Induced Certificate Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap acceptance can change under equivalent objective rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replace an objective by \(f'(x)=af(x)+b\) with \(a>0\). Certified bounds transform as \(L'=aL+b\) and \(U'=aU+b\), so \(U'-L'=a(U-L)\). Thus a fixed absolute tolerance is not invariant under changes of objective units. Moreover, relative normalization by \(\max\{|U|,|L|\}\) is not invariant under translation \(b\), although the minimizers are unchanged. Certificate stability therefore requires tolerances and denominator floors to be transformed with the declared objective scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent affine changes of objective scale can alter absolute or relative stopping decisions unless tolerances transform consistently.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le f^*\le U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U'-L'=a(U-L)\), while translation can change the relative denominator without changing minimizers.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct affine transformation of certified bounds establishes the instability
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine transformation formulas are correct, but the prescriptive certificate-stability requirement and its convention-level interpretation require an authoritative source.

children.title: Incomplete Search-State Failure
children.top_down_role: Premature certification when unresolved nodes or pending distributed work are omitted.

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Search-State Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global bounds require every unresolved region and pending task.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x:-1\le x\le1\}\) and the partition \(Q_1=[-1,0]\), \(Q_2=[0,1]\). The feasible incumbent \(\hat x=0\) gives \(U=0\). If the search state accidentally omits \(Q_1\), the valid lower bound \(L_2=0\) on \(Q_2\) produces a reported zero gap, although \(f^*=-1\). Therefore the minimum of recorded node bounds is global only when recorded, active, queued, and in-flight regions collectively cover the entire feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting one unresolved region can create a false zero gap even when all retained regional bounds are valid.
assumptions_latex: The partition and optimization problem are as displayed.
Only \(Q_2\) is included in the reported search state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reported gap is \(U-L_2=0\), but the true incumbent error is \(U-f^*=1\).

notation.meaning: Spatial subregions of the feasible interval.
Valid lower bound on the retained region only.

children.title: Domain Compactness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Bounded-domain settings supporting exhaustive spatial refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Compactness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact feasible-domain hypothesis used by deterministic spatial subdivision convergence arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be the feasible search domain and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\). The compact-domain regime holds when \(X\) is nonempty and compact. In finite-dimensional Euclidean space this is equivalent to \(X\) being closed and bounded. If, additionally, \(f\) is lower semicontinuous and finite at some point of \(X\), then \(f\) attains its minimum on \(X\); hence the global solution set \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty compact feasible set supports finite spatial coverings; with a proper lower-semicontinuous objective, it also guarantees existence of a global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and compact.
\(f\) is lower semicontinuous and finite somewhere on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\) is nonempty and compact.

children.title: Domain Covering Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covering structures used to organize regional refinement over the search domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Covering Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite, vanishing-mesh covering condition for spatial subdivision on a compact domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each iteration \(k\), let \(\mathcal P_k\) be a finite family of nonempty compact regions satisfying \(X\subseteq\bigcup_{R\in\mathcal P_k}R\). A vanishing-mesh covering regime requires \(h_k:=\max_{R\in\mathcal P_k}\operatorname{diam}(R)\to0\). If subdivision is nested, it additionally requires every \(R'\in\mathcal P_{k+1}\) to lie in some \(R\in\mathcal P_k\). Consequently, for every \(x\in X\), there exist covering regions \(R_k\in\mathcal P_k\) with \(x\in R_k\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite regional covers resolve the whole domain increasingly finely when their maximum diameter tends to zero; nested subdivision also assigns every child to a preceding parent.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty compact subset of \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
Each \(\mathcal P_k\) is a finite compact cover of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x\in X\;\exists R_k\in\mathcal P_k:\ x\in R_k\text{ and }\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0\).

notation.meaning: maximum regional diameter at iteration k

children.title: Noncompact-Domain Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Search settings where absent compactness requires additional domain-control structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncompact-Domain Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of compact-domain convergence conclusions without attainment or a compact localization argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the noncompact domain \(X=[0,\infty)\), take \(f(x)=e^{-x}\). Then \(\inf_{x\in X}f(x)=0\), but no \(x\in X\) attains this value. A subdivision method may exhaust every bounded interval and generate feasible points \(x_k\to\infty\) with \(f(x_k)\to0\), yet it cannot converge to a global minimizer in \(X\). Thus compact-domain covering results do not extend merely by using expanding compact covers; one additionally needs attainment, such as that supplied by a nonempty compact sublevel set containing all improving iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expanding covers can approximate the infimum on a noncompact domain while all iterates escape and no optimizer exists; compact localization or another attainment condition is necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}f(x)=0\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)=\varnothing\).

children.title: Regional Lower-Bound Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity of lower-bound information over each represented region.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the feasible domain and \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
\(R\) is a search region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(R\cap X\ne\varnothing\), then \(L(R)\le\inf_{x\in R\cap X}f(x)\); if \(R\cap X=\varnothing\), fathoming requires a sound infeasibility certificate.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a feasible domain, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and let \(R\) be a search region. When \(R\cap X\ne\varnothing\), a value \(L(R)\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) is a valid regional lower bound if and only if \(L(R)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in R\cap X\), equivalently \(L(R)\le\inf_{x\in R\cap X}f(x)\). When \(R\cap X=\varnothing\), the algorithm may declare the region infeasible, or represent its lower value by \(+\infty\), only when emptiness of \(R\cap X\) has been soundly certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a region containing feasible points, a valid lower bound cannot exceed any feasible objective value there. A region with no feasible points may be discarded or assigned an infinite lower value only under a sound infeasibility certificate.

\(x\in X\) satisfies \(f(x)<+\infty\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic exactness of valid regional bounds along regions shrinking to a feasible point with finite objective value.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a feasible domain, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and let \(L\) be a valid regional lower-bounding rule. The rule \(L\) is pointwise consistent at a point \(x\in X\) with \(f(x)<+\infty\) if, for every nested sequence of nonempty compact regions \(R_1\supseteq R_2\supseteq\cdots\) satisfying \(x\in R_j\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(R_j)\to0\), one has \(L(R_j)\to f(x)\). Since validity gives \(L(R_j)\le f(x)\), this is equivalent to \(f(x)-L(R_j)\to0\). The rule is pointwise consistent for \(f\) if it is pointwise consistent at every \(x\in X\) with \(f(x)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid lower-bounding rule is pointwise consistent when its bound approaches the finite objective value at every feasible point along every nested sequence of compact regions shrinking to that point.

children.title: Bound-Consistency Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Regional approximation behavior that prevents reliable closure of bound gaps.

assumptions_latex: \(X=[0,1]\), \(f(x)=x^2\), and \(R\subseteq X\) is nonempty.
Consistency is understood only for valid lower-bounding rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{over}}\) violates regional lower-bound validity, while \(L_{\mathrm{loose}}\) is valid but violates pointwise consistency at \(x=1\).

notation.meaning: regions shrinking to the point one

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two elementary failures: an invalid overestimating rule and a valid rule with a persistent pointwise gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\) and \(f(x)=x^2\). For every nonempty region \(R\subseteq X\), define \(L_{\mathrm{over}}(R)=\inf_{x\in R}f(x)+1\) and \(L_{\mathrm{loose}}(R)=-1\). The rule \(L_{\mathrm{over}}\) is not a valid lower-bounding rule. The rule \(L_{\mathrm{loose}}\) is valid, but for every sequence of regions \((R_j)_{j\ge1}\) shrinking to \(x=1\), one has \(L_{\mathrm{loose}}(R_j)=-1\not\to f(1)=1\). These examples exhibit invalid overestimation and failure of asymptotic exactness as distinct bound failure modes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An overestimating rule can violate lower-bound validity, while a uniformly loose valid rule can fail to become exact on shrinking regions. These are distinct failure modes.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Consistency Failure Modes

children.title: Refinement-Fairness Convergence Coupling
children.top_down_role: Branching and node-selection properties preventing unresolved regions from being ignored indefinitely.

children.title: Exhaustive Regional Refinement
children.top_down_role: Coverage behavior ensuring that persistent unresolved regions receive progressively finer partitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive Regional Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric refinement requirement imposed on every infinite lineage that survives fathoming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a rooted subdivision tree whose node \(v\) represents a compact region \(R_v\). Refinement is exhaustive if every infinite parent-child lineage \(v_0,v_1,\ldots\) that is never validly fathomed satisfies \(\operatorname{diam}(R_{v_j})\to0\). A stronger sufficient form requires a constant \(q\in(0,1)\) such that every child \(w\) of \(v\) obeys \(R_w\subseteq R_v\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(R_w)\le q\operatorname{diam}(R_v)\). The condition concerns infinite depth, not merely repeated subdivision elsewhere in the tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every surviving infinite branch must contain regions whose diameters tend to zero; repeatedly refining unrelated branches does not satisfy exhaustive refinement.
assumptions_latex: Each tree node \(v\) represents a nonempty compact region \(R_v\).
Child regions are contained in their parent region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_0\prec v_1\prec\cdots\text{ and no }v_j\text{ is fathomed}\implies\operatorname{diam}(R_{v_j})\to0\).

children.title: Fair Node Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection policies preventing eligible unresolved nodes from being deferred indefinitely.

assumptions_latex: For every iteration \(k\), \(A_k\) is the finite active-node set before selection.
For every iteration \(k\), \(s_k\in A_k\) is the selected node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall v\;\forall k_0:\bigl[(\forall k\ge k_0:\ v\in A_k)\implies(\exists k\ge k_0:\ s_k=v)\bigr]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: No-starvation condition for eligible regions in an infinite spatial search.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every iteration \(k\), let \(A_k\) be the finite set of active, unfathomed nodes before selection, and let \(s_k\in A_k\) be the selected node. The selection policy is fair if, for every node \(v\) and every iteration \(k_0\), persistence of \(v\) in the active set implies a later selection: \(\bigl(\forall k\ge k_0:\ v\in A_k\bigr)\implies\bigl(\exists k\ge k_0:\ s_k=v\bigr)\). If a processed node can remain active and eligible, repeated-selection fairness instead requires \(\bigl(\forall k\ge k_0:\ v\in A_k\bigr)\implies\bigl(\forall m\ge k_0\;\exists k\ge m:\ s_k=v\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fair policy eventually selects every node that remains continuously eligible. If processing can leave a node eligible, the repeated-selection version requires that node to be selected infinitely often.

Every infinite child lineage generated by subdivision has vanishing regional diameter.
The node-selection policy is fair.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational coupling ensuring that persistent regions undergo arbitrarily deep and geometrically exhaustive refinement.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a subdivision search in which every generated, unfathomed node remains active until selected, and every selected node is either validly fathomed or replaced by finitely many active children. Suppose the selection policy is fair and every infinite child lineage \(v_0,v_1,\ldots\) generated by subdivision satisfies \(\operatorname{diam}(R_{v_j})\to0\). Then every lineage that survives fathoming is processed to arbitrary finite depth, and its associated regions have vanishing diameter. Thus the geometric refinement condition and the no-starvation selection condition jointly provide usable spatial resolution along every surviving infinite lineage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When unfathomed nodes remain active until selection, fair selection processes every surviving branch to arbitrary depth; the exhaustive geometric rule then makes its regions shrink to zero diameter.

children.title: Incumbent-Fathoming Validity Coupling
children.top_down_role: Primal-feasibility and safe-discard requirements supporting correctness of the surviving tree.

children.title: Incumbent Feasibility Validity
children.top_down_role: Reliability of primal solutions used to establish search cutoffs.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Feasibility Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition making the incumbent value a genuine global upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), an incumbent pair \((\hat x_k,U_k)\) is valid when \(\hat x_k\in X\) and \(U_k=f(\hat x_k)\). It then satisfies \(U_k\ge f^*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\). After evaluating a new feasible point \(y_k\in X\), the valid update is \(U_{k+1}=\min\{U_k,f(y_k)\}\), with \(\hat x_{k+1}\) chosen as a feasible point attaining that displayed value. Hence every finite incumbent is feasible, is an upper bound on \(f^*\), and the sequence \((U_k)\) is nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incumbent must come from an evaluated feasible point. Its value is therefore a global upper bound, and retaining the better feasible value makes incumbents nonincreasing.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the feasible domain and \(f^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).
Every incumbent objective value is evaluated at its recorded point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat x_k\in X,\ U_k=f(\hat x_k)\ge f^*,\text{ and }U_{k+1}\le U_k\).

children.title: Safe Fathoming Validity
children.top_down_role: Regional discard decisions that preserve every potentially improving solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Fathoming Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-search certificate permitting removal of a region without losing a strictly improving feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_k=f(\hat x_k)\) for a feasible incumbent \(\hat x_k\), and let \(L(R)\) be valid for region \(R\). The region may be safely fathomed if either \(R\cap X=\varnothing\) is certified or \(L(R)\ge U_k\). In the latter case, every \(x\in R\cap X\) satisfies \(f(x)\ge L(R)\ge U_k\), so \(R\) contains no point strictly improving the incumbent. Equality is safe for retaining at least one global minimizer, although it may discard alternative minimizers having the same value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region is safely removable when certified infeasible or when its valid lower bound is no better than the feasible incumbent; no strictly improving point is then lost.
assumptions_latex: \(U_k=f(\hat x_k)\) with \(\hat x_k\in X\).
\(L(R)\le\inf_{x\in R\cap X}f(x)\) for every feasible region \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(R)\ge U_k\implies\forall x\in R\cap X:\ f(x)\ge U_k\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for region R

children.title: Incumbent–Fathoming Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between incumbent quality, pruning thresholds, plus surviving-tree correctness.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the feasible domain, \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and \(f^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).
\(U_k=f(\hat x_k)\) for some \(\hat x_k\in X\).
\(L(R)\le\inf_{x\in R\cap X}f(x)\) whenever \(R\cap X\ne\varnothing\).
Objective-bound fathoming is permitted only when \(L(R)\ge U_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(\exists x\in R\cap X:\ f(x)<U_k\bigr)\implies R\text{ is not fathomed by the objective-bound test}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility invariant linking feasible incumbent upper bounds to valid lower-bound pruning.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a feasible domain, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and define \(f^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\). Assume every incumbent value \(U_k\) is attained by a feasible point, every regional bound \(L(R)\) is valid, and objective-bound fathoming occurs only when \(L(R)\ge U_k\). For every region \(R\), if there exists \(x\in R\cap X\) with \(f(x)<U_k\), then \(L(R)<U_k\), so the objective-bound test does not fathom \(R\). If the infimum is attained and \(U_k>f^*\), every region containing a global minimizer is therefore protected from objective-bound fathoming.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible incumbents and valid regional lower bounds make pruning compatible: a region containing a point better than the incumbent survives the objective-bound test. When a global minimizer exists and the incumbent is still worse, every region containing such a minimizer is protected.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent–Fathoming Compatibility

children.title: Partition-Refinement Convergence

children.title: Rectangular Refinement Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence regimes for nested box and multidimensional interval partitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular Refinement Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform-mesh convergence for deterministic sampling over nested rectangular partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a compact rectangle and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous. For each \(k\geq 0\), let \(\mathcal P_k\) be a finite rectangular partition of \(X\), with \(\mathcal P_{k+1}\) refining \(\mathcal P_k\), and choose \(x_B\in B\) for every \(B\in\mathcal P_k\). If \(\Delta_k:=\max_{B\in\mathcal P_k}\operatorname{diam}(B)\to0\), then
\[
U_k:=\min_{B\in\mathcal P_k}f(x_B)\longrightarrow f^*:=\min_{x\in X}f(x).
\]
Thus every nested rectangular refinement whose maximum cell diameter vanishes produces globally convergent best sampled values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact box, sampling every cell of nested rectangular partitions converges to the global minimum whenever the maximum cell diameter tends to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a compact rectangle and \(f\) is continuous.
\(\mathcal P_{k+1}\) is a finite rectangular refinement of \(\mathcal P_k\).
\(x_B\in B\) is sampled for every cell and \(\Delta_k\to0\).

notation.meaning: rectangular partition at refinement level k
maximum diameter of a level-k cell
best sampled objective value at level k

children.title: Simplicial Refinement Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence regimes for triangulations and simplex subdivision.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplicial Refinement Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform-mesh convergence for sampling over nested triangulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact and triangulable, and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous. For each \(k\), let \(\mathcal T_k\) be a finite triangulation of \(X\), let \(\mathcal T_{k+1}\) subdivide \(\mathcal T_k\), and select \(x_S\in S\) for every simplex \(S\in\mathcal T_k\). If
\[
\Delta_k:=\max_{S\in\mathcal T_k}\operatorname{diam}(S)\longrightarrow0,
\]
then the best sampled value \(U_k:=\min_{S\in\mathcal T_k}f(x_S)\) satisfies \(U_k\to f^*:=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). No shape-regularity assumption is needed for this value-convergence conclusion beyond vanishing diameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling every simplex in successively finer triangulations converges to the global minimum when the largest simplex diameter vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and triangulable, and \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
\(\mathcal T_{k+1}\) is a finite simplicial subdivision of \(\mathcal T_k\).
\(x_S\in S\) is sampled for every simplex and \(\Delta_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{S\in\mathcal T_k}f(x_S)\to\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).

source_witnesses.locator: 8.4 Proof of Convergence to the Global Minimum p. 282

children.title: General-Cover Refinement Convergence

knowledge_statements.title: General-Cover Refinement Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value convergence for finite, possibly overlapping regional covers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a compact metric space and let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. For each \(k\), let \(\mathcal C_k\) be a finite cover of \(X\) by nonempty sets, and choose \(x_C\in C\) for every \(C\in\mathcal C_k\). If
\[
\Delta_k:=\max_{C\in\mathcal C_k}\operatorname{diam}(C)\longrightarrow0,
\]
then \(U_k:=\min_{C\in\mathcal C_k}f(x_C)\) converges to \(f^*:=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). The conclusion applies to conical, star-shaped, and other regional covers; neither disjointness nor nesting is required when the entire cover is sampled at every level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling every member of finite covers with vanishing maximum diameter yields objective values converging to the global minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a compact metric space and \(f\) is continuous.
\(\mathcal C_k\) is a finite cover of \(X\) by nonempty sets.
\(x_C\in C\) is sampled for every cover member and \(\Delta_k\to0\).

notation.meaning: finite regional cover at level k
best value sampled from the level-k cover

children.title: Search-Policy Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence behavior associated with node-selection and active-pool policies.

children.title: Best-Bound Search Convergence
children.top_down_role: Proof progress under global lower-bound node ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Bound Search Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic branch-and-bound convergence under global lower-bound selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimization of \(f\) on compact \(X\). At iteration \(k\), let the active regions cover every point not validly pruned, let each region \(B\) have a valid bound \(L(B)\leq\inf_{x\in B}f(x)\), and select \(B_k\in\arg\min_B L(B)\). Suppose an optimal point is never invalidly pruned and processing \(B_k\) produces a feasible value \(v_k\) such that
\[
v_k-L(B_k)\longrightarrow0.
\]
With \(U_k\) the best feasible value obtained through iteration \(k\), one has \(U_k\to f^*\). Consequently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), the global bound gap eventually satisfies \(U_k-\min_B L(B)\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best-bound processing converges when bounds are valid, optimal regions remain covered, and the processed node's feasible-to-lower-bound gap vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact, an optimizer exists, and no region containing every optimizer is invalidly pruned.
\(L(B)\leq\inf_{x\in B}f(x)\) for every active region.
\(B_k\) minimizes the active lower bounds and \(v_k-L(B_k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k\to f^*\) and \(U_k-\min_B L(B)\to0\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for region B
active region selected at iteration k
incumbent feasible value after iteration k

children.title: Fair Hybrid Search Convergence

knowledge_statements.title: Fair Hybrid Search Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of heuristic–proof hybrids satisfying eventual processing fairness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a spatial search minimize continuous \(f\) over compact \(X\), using valid regional lower bounds and feasible incumbents. The policy may interleave arbitrary heuristic selections with proof-oriented selections. Assume every active region that is never pruned is eventually processed, descendants containing any fixed optimizer are generated with diameters tending to zero, and processing such descendants yields feasible values converging to \(f^*\). Then the incumbent sequence \((U_k)\) converges to \(f^*\). If the algorithm periodically performs a globally best-bound step and every persistently active region is reached by these steps, the required fairness condition holds despite arbitrarily many intervening heuristic steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid policy remains globally convergent if every persistently active region is eventually processed and refinement along an optimizer becomes arbitrarily fine.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact, \(f\) is continuous, and all regional lower bounds are valid.
Every persistently active region is eventually processed.
Regions generated along an optimizer have vanishing diameter and yield feasible values approaching \(f^*\).

notation.meaning: best feasible objective value through iteration k
