children.title: Node Relaxation Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Maintenance and reuse of regional lower-bounding models across related nodes.

children.title: Incremental Relaxation Updates
children.top_down_role: Updating estimators, cuts, and domain-dependent relaxation objects after regional changes.

assumptions_latex: A child region \(B'\) satisfies \(B'\subseteq B\).
Every stored relaxation object records its validity domain and structural dependencies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated relaxation remains valid on \(B'\), while unaffected valid objects are reused without changing the regional feasible-point containment guarantee.
review_flags: A source is needed for dependency-aware incremental relaxation maintenance and validity filtering.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency-aware update of node relaxations after domain contraction or subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(R(B)\) and \(B'\subseteq B\), retain every constraint and cut whose recorded validity domain contains \(B'\). Discard or revalidate objects whose validity cannot be established on \(B'\). Recompute bounds, envelopes, coefficients, and propagated domains only for objects depending on quantities changed by the restriction. Insert the resulting replacements, propagate any further bound changes to a fixed point or prescribed update limit, and solve the updated relaxation. Output the updated relaxation together with its regional lower bound and the retained-object validity records.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a regional change, reuse still-valid relaxation objects and recompute only objects whose bounds, domains, or dependencies changed.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Relaxation Updates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches incremental relaxation updates, but dependency-aware reuse, revalidation, and fixed-point propagation safeguards are unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Node-Local Strengthening Cycle
children.top_down_role: Regional strengthening triggered by current relaxation information.

children.title: Node-Local Separation
children.top_down_role: Cuts or constraints generated from information specific to the current node.

assumptions_latex: \(F_B\) is the original feasible set restricted to node region \(B\).
\(\bar x\) solves the current relaxation and an oracle can test or separate \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted cut preserves \(F_B\) and excludes the current relaxation point whenever that point violates the cut.
review_flags: A source is needed for the node-valid separation cycle and stopping safeguards.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut generation restricted to validity within one spatial node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the node relaxation and obtain \(\bar x\). Query a separation oracle for an inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) satisfying \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) for every \(x\in F_B\) and \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x>b\). If such an inequality is returned, record its validity domain as \(B\), add it to the relaxation, and resolve. Repeat until no sufficiently violated cut is found, a cut or time limit is reached, or the node is fathomed. Output the strengthened relaxation and its valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly separate the node relaxation solution with inequalities valid for all original feasible points inside that node.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Local Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The node-local separation algorithm and validity conclusion are coherent, but the separation cycle and stopping safeguards require a source.

children.title: Node-Local Spatial Refinement
children.top_down_role: Regional partition strengthening targeted to weaknesses detected at the current node.

assumptions_latex: The node region \(B\) has a valid relaxation and a measurable spatial relaxation defect.
A chosen partition \(B_1,,,B_q\) covers \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(B\) by its children preserves all feasible points, and each child receives a valid region-specific relaxation.
review_flags: A source is needed for the defect-driven node-local refinement rule and regional update requirements.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial refinement selected and applied within a single active node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Estimate the relaxation defect attributable to each eligible coordinate or nonconvex component and choose \(j^*\) with maximal admissible score. Select split points within the current bounds and form finitely many children \(B_1,\ldots,B_q\) satisfying \(B=\bigcup_{r=1}^qB_r\). For each child, restrict variable bounds, propagate implied bounds, retain inherited objects valid on that child, and rebuild affected regional estimators. Replace \(B\) in the active list by all nonempty, unfathomed children; stop refining when the prescribed defect, width, or resource threshold is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split one node along a high-defect coordinate or component, then rebuild affected regional relaxations for covering child domains.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Local Spatial Refinement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits node-local spatial refinement, but the defect-driven rule and regional rebuilding requirements are unsupported; the assumption containing B_1,,,B_q is also malformed and must be corrected.

children.title: Separation–Refinement Coordination
children.top_down_role: Choice between local relaxation strengthening, spatial subdivision, or combined node processing.

assumptions_latex: At a node \(B\), both valid cuts and covering spatial refinements may be available.
Each candidate action has an estimated bound improvement \(G(a)\) and positive cost \(C(a)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every executed action preserves node validity; the cycle stops only under its declared fathoming, tolerance, or resource condition.

notation.meaning: Estimated gain and cost of an action.

review_flags: A source is needed for this gain-per-cost coordination policy and its lifecycle invariants.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive choice between node-valid separation and spatial refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At the current node, generate admissible separation and refinement actions. Estimate \(G(a)\) and \(C(a)>0\) for each action, and execute an action maximizing \(G(a)/C(a)\) among those meeting validity and resource requirements. After a cut, resolve the strengthened node relaxation and refresh action scores. After a refinement, create covering children and continue the cycle separately on retained children. Terminate the node cycle when it is fathomed, its relaxation defect meets tolerance, no admissible action has sufficient predicted gain, or the node resource limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate cuts and spatial splits by estimated bound gain per cost, refreshing decisions after each relaxation change.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation–Refinement Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits coordination, but the specific gain-per-cost policy and its lifecycle invariants appear as an uncited heuristic and require direct support.

children.title: Relaxation Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of solver state across parent, child, and neighboring regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-start protocol for related node relaxations in spatial branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a solved relaxation at region \(R\) with solver state \(s_R\), construct the relaxation for a related region \(R'\) and retain only state components whose referenced variables, constraints, and validity domains remain present in \(R'\). Map the retained state into the indexing of the new relaxation, repair components made infeasible by changed bounds, and initialize the solver with the resulting state \(s_{R'}^0\). Solve normally if the solver rejects \(s_{R'}^0\), numerical checks fail, or the initialized solve does not produce a valid relaxation bound. The output is a certified relaxation solution and bound for \(R'\); the inherited state itself is never a certificate of validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse compatible parent or neighboring solver state, repair it after model changes, and fall back to a cold solve whenever acceptance or numerical validation fails.
assumptions_latex: \(R,R'\subseteq D\) are regions with explicitly constructed valid relaxations.
\(s_R\) records solver state associated with the relaxation on \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_{R'}^0\) may accelerate the solve, but the returned bound must be certified by solving the valid relaxation on \(R'\).

notation.meaning: solver state produced at region R

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Warm starts affect initialization but cannot replace validation of the destination relaxation.

children.title: Search-State Inheritance
children.top_down_role: Validity-aware transfer of information from ancestors and related regions.

children.title: Bound-Change Scope Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Separation of region-specific contractions from globally valid reductions.

children.title: Node-Local Bound Changes
children.top_down_role: Bound contractions valid only within a node or its descendant region.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Local Bound Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines bound tightenings valid only within one search subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_v\) be the region represented by node \(v\). A bound change \(l_i'\le x_i\le u_i'\) is node-local at \(v\) when it is proved from assumptions valid throughout \(R_v\), satisfies \(l_i\le l_i'\le u_i'\le u_i\), and is not established for the entire root region. Its validity scope is \(R_v\), so the change may be imposed at \(v\) and every descendant \(w\) satisfying \(R_w\subseteq R_v\), but not at a node whose region is not contained in \(R_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-local tightening follows from that node’s assumptions and applies only to the node and descendants whose regions lie inside it.
assumptions_latex: \(R_v\) is a valid subregion of the root search domain.
\(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\) are the bounds before tightening.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(l_i'\le x_i\le u_i'\) is valid on every \(R_w\subseteq R_v\), with no claim outside \(R_v\).

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

source_witnesses.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

children.title: Globally Valid Bound Changes
children.top_down_role: Bound contractions valid throughout the active search domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Globally Valid Bound Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines bound tightenings valid throughout the root search domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the root feasible search region with current bound \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\). A tightening \(l_i'\le x_i\le u_i'\) is globally valid if every feasible point \(x\in D\) satisfies it and \(l_i\le l_i'\le u_i'\le u_i\). Such a change may be installed at the root and imposed in every open or subsequently created node relaxation. Applying it must not remove any globally feasible point, although it may render a node empty and thereby certify that node infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally valid tightening holds for every feasible point in the root domain and can therefore be applied throughout the search tree.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is the root search region.
\(F\subseteq D\) denotes the globally feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq\{x:l_i'\le x_i\le u_i'\}\), so the tightening is valid at every node.

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

source_witnesses.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

children.title: Bound-Change Scope Propagation
children.top_down_role: Transfer of bound changes according to regional validity plus tree ancestry.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Change Scope Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation rule determined by the proved validity region of each tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate every bound change \(b\) with a validity region \(V(b)\subseteq D\). The change may be installed at node \(w\) only if \(R_w\subseteq V(b)\). Consequently, a change derived at node \(v\) solely from assumptions valid on \(R_v\) propagates downward to descendants of \(v\), while a change proved on the root region \(D\) propagates to all nodes. Before applying inherited changes, intersect them with the destination-node bounds; an empty intersection certifies infeasibility only when every intersected change is valid on that destination region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate a bound change exactly to nodes contained in its validity region; an empty valid intersection certifies node infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(R_w\subseteq D\) is the destination-node region.
Each bound change \(b\) has a proved validity region \(V(b)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b\) is applicable at \(w\) only if \(R_w\subseteq V(b)\).

notation.meaning: validity region of bound change b

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

source_witnesses.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

children.title: Relaxation-Object Inheritance
children.top_down_role: Validity-aware reuse of relaxation objects across the tree.

children.title: Cut Inheritance
children.top_down_role: Reuse of valid relaxation cuts across descendants or broader portions of the tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Inheritance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions under which a relaxation cut can pass to another node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\beta\in\mathbb R\), and let the cut \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) be valid for every feasible \(x\) in a region \(V\subseteq D\). A destination node \(w\) with region \(R_w\subseteq D\) may inherit the cut when \(R_w\subseteq V\) and all variables and transformations in the inequality retain the same mathematical interpretation in the destination relaxation. These conditions ensure that adding the cut excludes no feasible point of \(R_w\). A cut whose validity relies on a source-node assumption must not be inherited outside the region where that assumption holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut may pass to a node when its validity region contains that node and its variables and transformations retain the same interpretation.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(V\subseteq D\), and \(R_w\subseteq D\).
\(a\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\beta\in\mathbb R\), and \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) is valid for every feasible \(x\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(R_w\subseteq V\) and the model interpretation is unchanged, then \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) remains valid for every feasible \(x\in R_w\).

notation.meaning: proved validity region of the cut

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

children.title: Estimator Inheritance
children.top_down_role: Reuse of regional underestimators or overestimators across compatible search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Estimator Inheritance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity test for reusing relaxation underestimators across nested regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:R\to\mathbb R\), and let \(g_R:R\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(g_R(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in R\). For a destination region \(R'\subseteq R\), the unchanged restriction of \(g_R\) to \(R'\) remains an underestimator: \(g_R(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in R'\). Operational inheritance additionally requires that the variables and fixed parameters defining \(g_R\) retain their mathematical interpretation. If \(R'\not\subseteq R\), or if the stored expression is altered using new bound-dependent parameters, the resulting estimator requires a new validity justification on \(R'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unchanged underestimator remains valid on a nested region; reuse outside that region or alteration using new parameters requires renewed validation.
assumptions_latex: \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(f:R\to\mathbb R\), and \(g_R:R\to\mathbb R\).
\(g_R(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in R\).
\(R'\subseteq R\) is the destination region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_R(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in R'\).

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

source_witnesses.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

children.title: Validity-Scope Filtering
children.top_down_role: Selection of reusable relaxation objects according to their geographic plus logical validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Validity-Scope Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filters inherited relaxation objects by destination-region validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a destination region \(R_w\) and relaxation objects \(o_1,\ldots,o_m\), each carrying a validity region \(V_j\) and required model signature \(M_j\). Initialize \(I=\varnothing\). For each \(j\), add \(o_j\) to \(I\) exactly when \(R_w\subseteq V_j\) and the destination relaxation satisfies \(M_j\); otherwise discard or regenerate it. Construct the node relaxation using only objects in \(I\), and independently validate the resulting bound. The output is the set of inherited objects whose recorded scope and model dependencies cover the destination node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep an inherited relaxation object only when its validity region contains the destination and its model dependencies still match.
assumptions_latex: Every object \(o_j\) has a recorded validity region \(V_j\).
Required model signatures can be checked at the destination node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I=\{o_j:R_w\subseteq V_j\text{ and the destination satisfies }M_j\}\).

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Inherited constraints and estimators must be filtered by their proved domains of validity.

children.title: Branching-History Inheritance
children.top_down_role: Accumulation of empirical information for later branching choices.

children.title: Pseudocost Inheritance
children.top_down_role: Transfer of empirical branching-value estimates across related nodes or candidate contexts.

knowledge_statements.title: Pseudocost Inheritance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers empirical branching-effect estimates while preserving their sample semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For variable \(i\) and direction \(d\in\{-,+\}\), store a cumulative normalized bound improvement \(S_i^d\) and observation count \(N_i^d\). After a branch changes \(x_i\) by magnitude \(\delta>0\) and produces a reliable bound improvement \(\Delta\ge0\), update \(S_i^d\leftarrow S_i^d+\Delta/\delta\) and \(N_i^d\leftarrow N_i^d+1\). The pseudocost is \(p_i^d=S_i^d/N_i^d\) when \(N_i^d>0\). Descendants may inherit these sufficient statistics unchanged; transfers to unrelated regions must retain counts and be suppressed or discounted when branching semantics, scaling, or relaxation type differs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inherit pseudocost sums and counts, update them with normalized reliable bound gains, and avoid unqualified transfer when branching semantics differ.
assumptions_latex: \(\delta>0\) is the realized branching displacement.
\(\Delta\ge0\) is a reliable improvement in a consistently defined node bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_i^d=S_i^d/N_i^d\) estimates normalized bound improvement from branching in direction \(d\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Pseudocosts are empirical averages of normalized branching gains.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The directional average is a plausible pseudocost representation, but update reliability, normalization, inheritance, discounting, and transfer across relaxation types are implementation-dependent variants requiring an authoritative source.

children.title: Branch-History Inheritance
children.top_down_role: Reuse of prior branching outcomes, frequencies, plus observed regional effects.

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-History Inheritance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-state representation for inherited branching observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the branch history at node \(v\) by \(H_v=(H_{\mathrm{global}},H_{\mathrm{path}}(v))\). The component \(H_{\mathrm{global}}\) contains observations declared comparable across the search, while \(H_{\mathrm{path}}(v)\) contains decisions and outcomes associated with the root-to-\(v\) path. For a child \(w\) of \(v\), set \(H_{\mathrm{path}}(w)=H_{\mathrm{path}}(v)\mathbin{\|}h_{v,w}\), where \(h_{v,w}\) records the new branch. Global statistics may be shared, but path-dependent facts are inherited only by descendants and must not be treated as valid constraints outside their path-defined region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch history separates globally comparable statistics from path-specific decisions; children append their branch while unrelated nodes do not inherit path facts.
assumptions_latex: \(w\) is a child of \(v\).
\(h_{v,w}\) records the branch from \(v\) to \(w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_w=(H_{\mathrm{global}},H_{\mathrm{path}}(v)\mathbin{\|}h_{v,w})\).

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

source_witnesses.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global/path decomposition is a coherent representation, but the cited generic branch-and-bound section does not establish this exact state model or its inheritance semantics.

children.title: History Transfer Across Regions
children.top_down_role: Policies controlling when empirical search information remains relevant after spatial subdivision.

knowledge_statements.title: History Transfer Across Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparability conditions for transferring empirical branching history between regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A branching observation collected in region \(R\) may be transferred to region \(R'\) only when its variables and branch directions have the same interpretation, its measured bound improvement uses the same relaxation and normalization convention, and the transfer policy declares \(R\) and \(R'\) comparable. Path-valid logical consequences additionally require \(R'\subseteq R\). Empirical observations transferred without containment are heuristic data rather than validity certificates; they may rank candidate branches but cannot justify pruning, feasibility, or a rigorous node bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer empirical history only between comparable regions, and never use nonlocal history alone to certify pruning, feasibility, or bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is the observation region and \(R'\) is the destination region.
Observation and destination use specified branching and normalization conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Transferred empirical history is ranking information unless its asserted logical consequence is independently valid on \(R'\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Empirical branching statistics guide choices but do not constitute rigorous bound certificates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between heuristic history and validity certificates is appropriate, but the criteria for comparable regions and permissible empirical transfer are policy- and solver-dependent and unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Numerical Robustness
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes affecting validity of bounds, reductions, fathoming, and certificates.

children.title: Scaling-Conditioning Robustness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Effects of poorly scaled expressions and relaxations on inference and bound reliability.

children.title: Expression Scaling
children.top_down_role: Magnitude normalization across variables, constraints, objectives, plus relaxation components.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent positive scaling of optimization constraints and objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(g_j(x)\le0\), choose finite scales \(s_j>0\) and replace them by \(\widehat g_j(x)=g_j(x)/s_j\le0\). The feasible set is unchanged because positive division preserves each inequality. For minimization of \(f(x)\), replacing the objective by \(\widehat f(x)=(f(x)-b)/s_0\), where \(s_0>0\), preserves minimizers; objective values and bounds transform by \(f=b+s_0\widehat f\). Scales should bring typical coefficients, residuals, or derivatives into comparable numerical ranges, but scaling does not repair an invalid relaxation or an intrinsically ill-posed model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive constraint scaling preserves feasibility, while positive affine objective scaling preserves minimizers and requires inverse transformation of reported bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_m>0\) are finite.
\(b\in\mathbb R\) is a fixed objective offset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_j(x)\le0\iff\widehat g_j(x)\le0\), and \(\arg\min f=\arg\min\widehat f\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Positive rescaling preserves inequality signs, and positive affine objective transformations preserve minimizers.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive rescaling identities are mathematically standard and the representation fits the leaf, but the numerical guidance about typical coefficients, residuals, and derivatives lacks the required inspectable source.

children.title: Relaxation Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of regional relaxation solves to numerical geometry plus coefficient disparities.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical conditioning criterion for computed node-relaxation bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a differentiable relaxation represented locally by residual equations \(F(z)=0\) and inequalities, and let \(J_F(z)\) be the Jacobian of the active residual system. At a regular point \(z\), define the local linearized condition number by \(\kappa(J_F(z))=\lVert J_F(z)\rVert\lVert J_F(z)^{-1}\rVert\) when the active Jacobian is square and nonsingular. The relaxation is numerically well-conditioned only relative to specified variable scaling, residual scaling, norms, and arithmetic tolerances, with moderate \(\kappa\). A large or undefined condition number signals that small data or rounding perturbations may cause large changes in computed primal-dual quantities, so a reported bound requires residual and certificate validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation conditioning is scaling- and norm-dependent; large Jacobian condition numbers demand explicit residual and bound-certificate checks.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is differentiable near the computed point \(z\).
The active Jacobian \(J_F(z)\) is identified under fixed scaling and norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Large or undefined \(\kappa(J_F(z))\) indicates sensitivity and prevents trusting a computed bound without independent validation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A square active-residual Jacobian condition number covers only a narrow formulation and does not by itself characterize conditioning of a general constrained relaxation or certify bound reliability. A variant-specific authoritative source and a more precise active-system definition are required.

children.title: Conditioning-Induced Bound Degradation
children.top_down_role: Loss of bound reliability or inference strength caused by poor numerical conditioning.

assumptions_latex: For every active region \(B\), \(L(B)\leq \inf_{x\in B\cap F}f(x)\) is an exact valid lower bound.
The computed value satisfies \(|\widehat L(B)-L(B)|\leq \delta(B)\), where \(\delta(B)\geq 0\) includes numerical and solver error.
The incumbent \(U\) is the objective value of a certified feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat L(B)-\delta(B)\) is a certified lower bound, whereas \(\widehat L(B)\) alone need not be. Consequently, pruning from \(\widehat L(B)\geq U-\varepsilon\) is sound only if the bound error has already been incorporated. In particular, whenever \(L(B)<U-\varepsilon\leq \widehat L(B)\), the uncorrected test discards a region that may contain an \(\varepsilon\)-improving point. If conditioning causes \(\delta(B)\) to grow, the corrected bound weakens by the same amount and may cease to support pruning or termination.

notation.meaning: Exact and computed regional lower bounds.
Certified error allowance for the computed bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic pruning with an explicit additive bound-error allowance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every active region \(B\), suppose \(L(B)\leq \inf_{x\in B\cap F}f(x)\) and \(|\widehat L(B)-L(B)|\leq \delta(B)\). Then \(\widehat L(B)-\delta(B)\) remains a valid lower bound. Using \(\widehat L(B)\) without correction can be unsound: if \(L(B)<U-\varepsilon\leq \widehat L(B)\), the test \(\widehat L(B)\geq U-\varepsilon\) prunes a region that can still improve the incumbent beyond tolerance. Thus increasing conditioning error \(\delta(B)\) degrades the usable bound additively and can prevent certified pruning or gap closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computed regional bound must be reduced by its certified numerical error. Poor conditioning enlarges that correction; ignoring it can wrongly prune a region containing a materially better solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning-Induced Bound Degradation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive correction argument is mathematically coherent and fits the failure-boundary container, but no inspectable source supports the conditioning-error model or its certification interpretation.

children.title: Certificate Tolerance Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of solver tolerances with pruning and certificate claims.

children.title: Bound Tolerance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerical margins governing bound comparison, cutoff decisions, plus gap closure.

assumptions_latex: Every active region \(B\) has a certified lower bound \(L_B\leq\inf_{x\in B\cap F}f(x)\).
The incumbent \(U\) is certified feasible.
The requested absolute and relative tolerances satisfy \(\varepsilon_a,\varepsilon_r\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With \(\tau_b(U)=\varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_r\max\{1,|U|\}\), a region may be tolerance-pruned when \(L_B\geq U-\tau_b(U)\). If \(L=\min_{B\in\mathcal A}L_B\) over the active regions and \(U-L\leq\tau_b(U)\), then the incumbent is globally \(\tau_b(U)\)-optimal relative to the covered domain. Exact certification is the special regime \(\varepsilon_a=\varepsilon_r=0\); positive tolerances certify only the stated approximate regime.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-plus-relative objective-gap convention for deterministic regional search.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\tau_b(U)=\varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_r\max\{1,|U|\}\), where \(\varepsilon_a,\varepsilon_r\geq0\). A region \(B\) with certified lower bound \(L_B\) is tolerance-prunable when \(L_B\geq U-\tau_b(U)\). If the active-region lower bound is \(L=\min_{B\in\mathcal A}L_B\), then termination under \(U-L\leq\tau_b(U)\) certifies that no point in the covered domain improves the feasible incumbent by more than \(\tau_b(U)\). The exact regime has \(\varepsilon_a=\varepsilon_r=0\); otherwise the certificate is explicitly approximate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound tolerances combine an absolute and relative objective allowance. Pruning or termination then certifies approximate, not exact, global optimality over the covered domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Tolerance Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

children.title: Feasibility Tolerance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerical margins governing acceptance of regional or incumbent feasibility.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \(F=\{x\in D:g_i(x)\leq0,\ i\in I,\ h_j(x)=0,\ j\in E\}\).
Constraint tolerances satisfy \(\eta_i^g,\eta_j^h\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tolerance-feasible set is \(F_\eta=\{x\in D:g_i(x)\leq\eta_i^g,\ |h_j(x)|\leq\eta_j^h\}\). Exact feasibility uses all tolerances equal to zero. Acceptance with positive tolerances certifies only membership in \(F_\eta\), unless a separate validated repair, projection, or error-bound argument produces a point in \(F\). Therefore an incumbent drawn merely from \(F_\eta\) must be labeled tolerance-feasible and cannot automatically support an exact global-optimality certificate for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise tolerances for inequality and equality constraints.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=\{x\in D:g_i(x)\leq0,\ i\in I,\ h_j(x)=0,\ j\in E\}\), define \(F_\eta=\{x\in D:g_i(x)\leq\eta_i^g,\ |h_j(x)|\leq\eta_j^h\}\), with nonnegative componentwise tolerances. Exact feasibility is the regime in which every tolerance is zero. With any positive tolerance, acceptance establishes only \(x\in F_\eta\). It establishes \(x\in F\) only when an additional validated repair, projection, or error-bound procedure supplies an exactly feasible point. Hence an uncorrected point in \(F_\eta\) cannot serve as an exact feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive constraint tolerances define an enlarged feasible set. A point accepted there is only tolerance-feasible unless validation or repair produces a point satisfying the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Tolerance Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

children.title: Cross-Tolerance Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Consistency among bound, feasibility, integrality, plus pruning tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Tolerance Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient compatibility through a feasibility error bound, objective Lipschitz estimate, and certified objective lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, and let an accepted point \(x\) satisfy \(v(x)\leq\eta\). Suppose \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\leq\kappa v(x)\) and \(|f(x)-f(y)|\leq K\|x-y\|\) on the relevant neighborhood. Let \(L\leq f^*:=\inf_{y\in F}f(y)\) be a certified lower bound satisfying \(f(x)-L\leq\tau_b\). Then there exists \(y\in F\) with \(\|x-y\|\leq\kappa\eta\), and \(f(y)-f^*\leq\tau_b+K\kappa\eta\). Hence \(\tau_b+K\kappa\eta\leq\varepsilon\) is sufficient for an \(\varepsilon\)-global feasible certificate. Without validated error-bound and Lipschitz estimates, feasibility and objective-gap tolerances are not quantitatively interchangeable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed feasible set, a feasibility error bound and a Lipschitz objective convert feasibility tolerance into an objective repair penalty. Adding that penalty to the certified bound gap gives a sufficient total certificate budget.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and closed, and the accepted point \(x\) satisfies \(v(x)\leq\eta\).
Near accepted points, \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\leq\kappa v(x)\), and the objective is \(K\)-Lipschitz.
A certified lower bound \(L\leq f^*:=\inf_{y\in F}f(y)\) satisfies \(f(x)-L\leq\tau_b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(y\in F\) with \(\|x-y\|\leq\kappa\eta\), so \(f(y)-f^*\leq\tau_b+K\kappa\eta\). Therefore \(\tau_b+K\kappa\eta\leq\varepsilon\) is sufficient for an \(\varepsilon\)-global feasible certificate.

notation.meaning: Feasibility error-bound and objective Lipschitz constants.
Certified objective lower bound and bound-gap allowance.

children.title: Tolerance-Induced Certificate Risk
children.top_down_role: Risk of unsupported pruning or optimality claims under incompatible numerical margins.

assumptions_latex: Consider \(\min\{x:-x\leq0,\ -1\leq x\leq1\}\).
A solver accepts \(-x\leq\eta\) for some \(0<\eta\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact feasible set is \([0,1]\) and its optimum is \(f^*=0\). The tolerance-feasible point \(x=-\eta\) is accepted and has reported value \(-\eta<f^*\), although it is infeasible for the original problem. Treating this value as an exact feasible incumbent can therefore produce a false objective gap, erroneous pruning, or a false global-optimality certificate. The discrepancy equals the feasibility tolerance in this scaled example and persists regardless of bound-solver accuracy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional counterexample showing a false incumbent from relaxed feasibility.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x:-x\leq0,\ -1\leq x\leq1\}\). Its exact feasible set is \([0,1]\) and \(f^*=0\). If feasibility is tested instead by \(-x\leq\eta\), where \(0<\eta\leq1\), then \(x=-\eta\) is accepted with objective \(-\eta<f^*\), despite being infeasible for the original problem. Using \(-\eta\) as an exact incumbent can create a false global gap and can cause valid regions to be pruned. Thus positive feasibility tolerance, without repair or objective correction, can invalidate an otherwise exact certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed feasibility test can accept an infeasible point whose objective beats the true optimum. Using it as an incumbent can invalidate pruning and the final certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Induced Certificate Risk

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

children.title: Relaxation-Solver Failure Handling
children.top_down_role: Search responses to unreliable statuses, numerical breakdown, or incomplete regional solves.

assumptions_latex: Each regional solve returns a status in \(\{\mathrm{certified\_bound},\mathrm{certified\_infeasible},\mathrm{uncertain}\}\).
Only mathematically validated bounds or infeasibility proofs receive certified statuses.
The subdivision rule eventually reduces every repeatedly selected region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Initialize the active list with the root region and a certified feasible incumbent when available. For a selected region \(B\), prune it only after \(\mathrm{certified\_infeasible}\) or after a certified lower bound meets the pruning test. On \(\mathrm{uncertain}\), retry with validated scaling or precision; if uncertainty remains, subdivide \(B\) and retain all children. Terminate with a global certificate only when every covered region has been certified pruned or the certified global gap meets tolerance; otherwise output the incumbent together with an unresolved-region status.

notation.meaning: Certified regional lower bound when returned.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative branch-and-bound response to unreliable regional solver outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the active list with the root region and retain a certified feasible incumbent \(U\) when one exists. For a selected region \(B\), accept pruning only if the solver returns certified infeasibility or a certified lower bound \(L_B\) satisfying the prescribed pruning test. If the status is uncertain, retry using validated rescaling, tighter tolerances, or higher precision; if no certified result is obtained, subdivide \(B\) and retain every child. Report a global certificate only after all covered regions are certified pruned or the certified global gap satisfies tolerance. Otherwise return \(U\), if available, and explicitly identify unresolved regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unreliable regional solve must not justify pruning. Retry it or subdivide the region, and issue a global certificate only after all relevant regions have certified outcomes.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Solver Failure Handling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conservative algorithm fits the failure-handling topic, but its status semantics and retry/subdivision policy have no inspectable authoritative support.

children.title: Geometric Search Failure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes causing invalid coverage, weak discrimination, or redundant exploration.

children.title: Domain Boundedness Failure Classes
children.top_down_role: Failure of finite covering and relaxation quality when useful variable bounds are absent.

children.title: Unbounded Variable Domains
children.top_down_role: Search domains lacking finite limits required by regional covering or relaxation construction.

assumptions_latex: The search domain is \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A variable \(x_i\) has an unbounded domain on \(D\) when \(\inf_{x\in D}x_i=-\infty\) or \(\sup_{x\in D}x_i=+\infty\). Equivalently, no finite interval \([\ell_i,u_i]\) contains its coordinate projection \(\{x_i:x\in D\}\). A domain is coordinatewise bounded exactly when every coordinate admits finite \(\ell_i\) and \(u_i\); otherwise finite-box spatial subdivision does not directly cover the entire domain.

notation.meaning: Finite coordinate bounds when they exist.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise boundedness in finite-dimensional deterministic global optimization.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), coordinate \(i\) is unbounded when \(\inf_{x\in D}x_i=-\infty\) or \(\sup_{x\in D}x_i=+\infty\). Equivalently, no finite interval \([\ell_i,u_i]\) contains the coordinate projection \(\{x_i:x\in D\}\). The domain is coordinatewise bounded precisely when finite bounds \(\ell_i\leq x_i\leq u_i\) exist for every \(i\). If any coordinate is unbounded, a finite initial box cannot cover all of \(D\) without an additional truncation or compactification argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable domain is unbounded when its coordinate projection has no finite lower or upper endpoint. Such a domain cannot be covered by one finite initial subdivision box.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Variable Domains

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

children.title: Poorly Bounded Variable Domains
children.top_down_role: Finite but excessively broad domains that weaken regional discrimination.

assumptions_latex: A finite search box is \(D=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\).
A nonempty relevant set \(R\subseteq D\), such as a feasible incumbent level set, has finite coordinate widths \(w_i(R)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For a chosen threshold \(\Gamma>1\), coordinate \(i\) is poorly bounded relative to \(R\) when \((u_i-\ell_i)/w_i(R)\geq\Gamma\), with the ratio interpreted as \(+\infty\) when \(w_i(R)=0<u_i-\ell_i\). The box is poorly bounded when this holds for at least one coordinate. This is a relative geometric regime: all declared bounds are finite, but the search width substantially exceeds the width of the region relevant to optimization.

notation.meaning: Optimization-relevant subset of the search box.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quantitative relative-width definition; the threshold is application dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\) be finite and let \(R\subseteq D\) be a nonempty optimization-relevant set. Write \(w_i(R)=\sup_{x\in R}x_i-\inf_{x\in R}x_i\). For a prescribed \(\Gamma>1\), coordinate \(i\) is poorly bounded relative to \(R\) when \((u_i-\ell_i)/w_i(R)\geq\Gamma\), interpreting the ratio as \(+\infty\) if \(w_i(R)=0<u_i-\ell_i\). The box is poorly bounded when at least one coordinate is poorly bounded. Thus poor boundedness is relative, despite every endpoint being finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite box is poorly bounded when its width in some coordinate greatly exceeds the width of the optimization-relevant region. The classification depends on a chosen ratio threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Poorly Bounded Variable Domains

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed width ratio is internally defined, but it is a threshold-dependent formalization rather than an established definition supported by evidence.

children.title: Coverage Failure from Missing Bounds
children.top_down_role: Breakdown of finite spatial coverage when useful variable limits are unavailable.

assumptions_latex: The subdivision algorithm starts from a finite box \(D_0\) and every generated region is a subset of its parent.
The original feasible set is \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generated region lies in \(D_0\), so the union of all regions ever searched is contained in \(D_0\). If \(F\nsubseteq D_0\), then feasible points in \(F\setminus D_0\) are never examined. In particular, if \(\inf_{x\in F\setminus D_0}f(x)<\inf_{x\in F\cap D_0}f(x)\), any claimed global optimum based solely on this subdivision is false for the original problem. Refining \(D_0\) cannot repair the missing coverage.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage limitation of descendant-only subdivision from a finite root box.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose subdivision begins from a finite box \(D_0\) and every child is contained in its parent. Then every region ever generated is contained in \(D_0\). If the original feasible set satisfies \(F\nsubseteq D_0\), points in \(F\setminus D_0\) receive no search coverage. Moreover, if \(\inf_{x\in F\setminus D_0}f(x)<\inf_{x\in F\cap D_0}f(x)\), optimization over the subdivision tree cannot certify the original global optimum. Arbitrarily fine refinement inside \(D_0\) does not remedy this omission; valid outer bounds or an exhaustive expansion mechanism are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Descendant subdivision never searches outside its initial box. If missing bounds exclude a better feasible point, refinement cannot restore coverage and the claimed global optimum is invalid.
knowledge_statements.title: Coverage Failure from Missing Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

children.title: Relaxation Degradation from Loose Bounds
children.top_down_role: Loss of regional bound quality caused by overly broad variable ranges.

assumptions_latex: The bilinear term is \(z=xy\) on \([\ell_x,u_x]\times[\ell_y,u_y]\).
Its lower relaxation is the McCormick convex envelope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The largest vertical gap between \(xy\) and its convex-envelope lower estimator equals \((u_x-\ell_x)(u_y-\ell_y)/4\). Hence enlarging either variable interval weakens the best convex lower relaxation available from the box alone. Under nested subdivision, this contribution closes only when \((u_x-\ell_x)(u_y-\ell_y)\to0\); loose bounds can therefore produce weak regional lower bounds and delay pruning even when they remain formally valid.

notation.meaning: Auxiliary variable representing the bilinear product.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact box-width dependence for the McCormick relaxation of one bilinear term.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z=xy\) on \([\ell_x,u_x]\times[\ell_y,u_y]\), let \(m(x,y)\) be the McCormick convex-envelope lower estimator. Then \(m(x,y)\leq xy\) throughout the box and \(\max_{x,y}\{xy-m(x,y)\}=(u_x-\ell_x)(u_y-\ell_y)/4\). Thus relaxation error scales with the product of the two interval widths. Loose finite bounds can make the regional lower bound arbitrarily weak, while nested refinement closes this bilinear contribution only if \((u_x-\ell_x)(u_y-\ell_y)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bilinear term, the maximum McCormick lower-envelope gap is one quarter of the product of the variable widths. Loose bounds therefore weaken regional relaxations quantitatively.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Degradation from Loose Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

children.title: Nonclosing Regional Relaxation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Failure of regional bounds to approach local problem values under refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosing Regional Relaxation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested-region definition allowing oscillatory relaxation gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(B)\leq\phi(B):=\inf_{x\in B\cap F}f(x)\). Along nested regions \(B_{k+1}\subseteq B_k\) satisfying \(B_k\cap F\neq\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(B_k)\to0\), the relaxation gap is nonclosing when \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}[\phi(B_k)-L(B_k)]>0\), equivalently when the nonnegative gaps do not converge to zero. If this limsup exceeds a certificate tolerance \(\varepsilon\), arbitrarily far along the sequence there are regions whose gaps exceed \(\varepsilon\). Thus diameter reduction alone does not guarantee eventual gap closure, although a closing subsequence may still exist; relaxation strengthening or another bounding construction may be required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regional relaxation gap is nonclosing when it fails to converge to zero along shrinking nested regions. A positive limsup prevents refinement alone from guaranteeing eventual closure, though some subsequence may still have small gaps.
assumptions_latex: For every region \(B\), \(L(B)\leq\phi(B):=\inf_{x\in B\cap F}f(x)\).
There is a nested sequence \(B_{k+1}\subseteq B_k\) with \(\operatorname{diam}(B_k)\to0\) and \(B_k\cap F\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation gap is nonclosing along \((B_k)\) when \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}[\phi(B_k)-L(B_k)]>0\). If this limsup exceeds \(\varepsilon\), gaps larger than \(\varepsilon\) occur arbitrarily far along the sequence, so shrinking diameters alone do not guarantee eventual certificate closure; this does not exclude a closing subsequence.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

children.title: Feasible-Region Geometry Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Feasible geometry frustrating local search, propagation, and balanced coverage.

children.title: Thin Feasible Regions
children.top_down_role: Narrow feasible geometry that is difficult to preserve through relaxation, contraction, or local search.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \(F\subseteq D\subset\mathbb R^n\), where \(D\) is bounded and has positive diameter.
The Euclidean inradius is \(r_D(F)=\sup\{r\geq0:\exists x,\ \overline B(x,r)\subseteq F\cap D\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\eta\geq0\), the feasible region is \(\eta\)-thin in \(D\) when \(r_D(F)\leq\eta\operatorname{diam}(D)\). The limiting regime \(\eta=0\) means that \(F\cap D\) contains no positive-radius Euclidean ball and therefore has empty interior relative to \(\mathbb R^n\). Small positive \(\eta\) describes feasible geometry whose largest inscribed ball is small compared with the ambient search scale.

notation.meaning: Feasible set and bounded ambient search domain.
Inradius of the feasible set within the domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inradius-based geometric definition, including lower-dimensional feasible sets at zero inradius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq D\subset\mathbb R^n\), with \(D\) bounded and \(\operatorname{diam}(D)>0\). Define \(r_D(F)=\sup\{r\geq0:\exists x\in\mathbb R^n,\ \overline B(x,r)\subseteq F\cap D\}\). For \(\eta\geq0\), call \(F\) \(\eta\)-thin in \(D\) when \(r_D(F)\leq\eta\operatorname{diam}(D)\). If \(\eta=0\), then \(F\cap D\) contains no positive-radius Euclidean ball and has empty interior in \(\mathbb R^n\). Small positive \(\eta\) quantifies a narrow feasible region relative to the search scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible region is thin when its largest inscribed ball is small relative to the search-domain diameter. Zero inradius includes lower-dimensional feasible sets with empty interior.
knowledge_statements.title: Thin Feasible Regions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inradius construction is internally coherent, but thin feasible regions admit several inequivalent formalizations and no source supports selecting this one for the terminal container.

children.title: Disconnected Feasible Regions
children.top_down_role: Separated feasible components requiring broad spatial coverage.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is compact.
\(F=F_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}F_2\subseteq X\), where \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) are nonempty closed sets with \(\operatorname{dist}(F_1,F_2)>0\).
\(f:F\to\mathbb R\) has a nonempty set of global minimizers contained in \(F_2\).
All initial or surviving search regions lie in \(U\subseteq X\), and descendants are subsets of their parent regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(U\cap F_2=\varnothing\) and \(\varnothing\ne\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\subseteq F_2\), then the search cannot recover a global minimizer.

notation.meaning: set containing every region accessible to the search
objective function on the feasible set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by restricting descendant regions to one separated feasible component.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(F=F_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}F_2\subseteq X\), where \(F_1,F_2\) are nonempty closed sets with \(\operatorname{dist}(F_1,F_2)>0\), and let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\). Consider a spatial search whose initial or surviving regions all lie in \(U\subseteq X\), where \(U\cap F_2=\varnothing\), and whose subdivision rule creates only subsets of existing regions. Every feasible point returned by the search then belongs to \(F_1\). Consequently, if \(\varnothing\ne\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\subseteq F_2\), the search cannot recover a global minimizer, irrespective of refinement within \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subdivision search confined away from one disconnected feasible component cannot find a global minimizer when every global minimizer lies in that omitted component.
knowledge_statements.title: Disconnected Feasible Regions

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

children.title: Hidden Feasible Regions
children.top_down_role: Feasible components that are poorly exposed by local search or weak regional inference.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a nonempty measurable subset of the feasible set \(F\subseteq X\).
\((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0}\) is the search-history filtration and each \(Z_k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable.
The stated conditional hit-probability bounds hold almost surely, with \(p_k\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The search never visits \(H\) almost surely in the zero-mass case and has positive probability of never visiting \(H\) in the summable-mass case.

notation.meaning: deterministic upper bound on the conditional probability of hitting H

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detection boundary for feasible regions invisible to the search distribution or region generator.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.3 Convergence of Global Random Search Algorithms p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\subseteq F\subseteq X\) be a nonempty measurable feasible region, let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0}\) be the search-history filtration, and let \(Z_k\) be the \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable point generated at iteration \(k\ge1\). If \(\mathbb{P}(Z_k\in H\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})=0\) almost surely for every \(k\), then \(H\) is never visited almost surely. More generally, if deterministic numbers \(p_k\in[0,1)\) satisfy \(\mathbb{P}(Z_k\in H\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\le p_k\) almost surely for every \(k\) and \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}p_k<\infty\), then the probability of never visiting \(H\) is at least \(\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}(1-p_k)>0\). Thus almost-sure discovery of \(H\) is not guaranteed when it receives insufficient search mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A measurable feasible region receiving zero search probability is never visited almost surely, while one receiving summably small conditional search probability can remain undiscovered with positive probability.
knowledge_statements.title: Hidden Feasible Regions

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1.3 Convergence of Global Random Search Algorithms p. 34

children.title: Feasible-Geometry Coverage Failures
children.top_down_role: Search imbalance or missed progress arising from difficult feasible-region geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\) is the feasible set and \(f:F\to\mathbb R\) has at least one global minimizer.
Future regions are generated only as descendants of active regions.
Regions removed from active search require valid infeasibility or objective-bound certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uncertified exclusion of every global minimizer from the maintained region cover destroys the guarantee of recovering a global minimizer.

notation.meaning: objective function on the feasible set
regions discarded with valid certificates by iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary geometric coverage invariant for complete spatial global search.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\) be the feasible set, let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), and assume that \(M=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\ne\varnothing\). At iteration \(k\), let \(\mathcal A_k\) be the active regions and \(\mathcal C_k\) the regions discarded with valid infeasibility or objective-bound certificates. A maintained geometric coverage invariant is \[F\subseteq\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal A_k\cup\mathcal C_k}B.\] Suppose future regions are generated only as descendants of \(\mathcal A_k\). If initialization gaps, subdivision gaps, numerical contraction, or uncertified deletion cause \[M\cap\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal A_k\cup\mathcal C_k}B=\varnothing,\] then subsequent search cannot examine any global minimizer. The guarantee of recovering a global minimizer is therefore lost unless the omission is repaired or an independent certificate establishes that an equivalent optimum remains represented.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A descendant-only spatial search loses its global-recovery guarantee when every global minimizer is omitted from both active regions and certifiably discarded regions without an independent certificate of an equivalent represented optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Geometry Coverage Failures

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

children.title: Symmetry-Duplication Search Failures
children.top_down_role: Redundant exploration of equivalent regions or representations.

children.title: Spatial Search Symmetry
children.top_down_role: Equivalent regional representations created by problem or formulation symmetry.

knowledge_statements.title: Spatial Search Symmetry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbit equivalence of spatial regions under finite problem symmetries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act bijectively on \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). Suppose feasibility and objective values are invariant: \(gF=F\) and \(f(gx)=f(x)\) for every \(g\in G\) and \(x\in X\). Then each feasible point orbit has constant objective value, and for every search region \(B\subseteq X\), \[\inf_{x\in B\cap F}f(x)=\inf_{x\in gB\cap F}f(x).\] Thus regions in the orbit \(G B\) represent equivalent optimization subproblems whenever the regional bounding and subdivision operations are equivariant under the same action.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invariant objective and feasibility data make symmetry-related regions equivalent optimization subproblems when search operations respect the symmetry.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite group acting bijectively on \(X\).
The feasible set and objective are invariant under \(G\).
Regional search operations are equivariant under \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every pair \(B\) and \(gB\) has the same feasible infimum and equivalent search status.

notation.meaning: image of region B under symmetry g

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invariance under a finite group directly induces orbitwise equality of feasible objective values
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role and finite-group invariance statement fit Spatial Search Symmetry, but the record has no citation with an inspectable locator. A dedicated source supporting orbitwise equivalence in optimization or symmetry-aware spatial search is required.

children.title: Duplicate Region Exploration
children.top_down_role: Repeated processing of equivalent or materially overlapping spatial regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Region Exploration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work inflation from independently processing symmetry-equivalent search regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) be distinct active regions in one symmetry orbit, and suppose an equivariant search performs the same sequence of bounding and subdivision operations on each region. If processing one representative through a fixed search depth costs \(W>0\) oracle or relaxation calls, processing all \(m\) orbit members costs \(mW\). Relative to representative-only exploration, the duplicate work is \((m-1)W\) and the multiplicative work inflation is \(m\). This bound concerns redundant computation; it does not by itself invalidate correctness when every processed region remains valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exploring all m symmetry-equivalent regions multiplies equivalent search work by m and adds (m−1) representative workloads.
assumptions_latex: The \(m\) regions are distinct members of one symmetry orbit.
Bounding and subdivision are equivariant.
\(W\) counts identical oracle or relaxation work per representative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Duplicate exploration uses \(mW\) work instead of \(W\), an excess of \((m-1)W\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: identical equivariant processing gives a direct multiplicative work count
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role is suitable because the record quantifies work inflation from duplicate orbit exploration. Its exact mW count is conditional on identical per-region work and is internally coherent, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Symmetry-Reduction Opportunities
children.top_down_role: Structural opportunities for selecting representative regions or eliminating equivalent search states.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Reduction Opportunities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient search retaining one canonical representative per symmetry orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite invariant symmetry group \(G\), initialize a dictionary \(D=\varnothing\) and an active queue containing the root region. For each generated region \(B\), compute a canonical representative \(c(B)\) satisfying \(c(B)=c(gB)\) for all \(g\in G\). Insert and process \(B\) only if \(c(B)\notin D\), then add \(c(B)\) to \(D\); otherwise discard \(B\) as an orbit duplicate. Apply equivariant bounds and branching to retained representatives. Stop under the original certified gap rule and map any representative solution through its orbit. Under exact canonicalization and invariance, the reduced search preserves the global optimum value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalize each generated region, explore one representative per symmetry orbit, and retain the original optimum under exact invariance and equivariance.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) preserves feasibility and objective values.
Canonicalization identifies exactly the region orbits.
Bounding, branching, and stopping rules are equivariant or orbit-invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Representative-only search preserves \(\min_{x\in F}f(x)\) while avoiding orbit-duplicate regions.

notation.meaning: canonical orbit representative of region B
set of previously encountered canonical representatives

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact quotienting by an invariant finite-group action preserves orbitwise objective values
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the symmetry-reduction opportunity leaf, and the assumptions identify the main correctness requirements. The optimum-preservation claim and canonical representative procedure require a dedicated source with a specific locator.

children.title: Duplicate-Detection Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on recognizing equivalent regions when representations, histories, or local relaxations differ.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Detection Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary for signatures used to merge or discard allegedly equivalent regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s(B,q)\) be a duplicate-detection signature for region \(B\) and search state \(q\). Pruning one of two states after observing equal signatures is sound only if \[s(B,q)=s(B',q')\ \Longrightarrow\ (B',q')=g(B,q)\] for some problem symmetry \(g\) preserving feasibility, objective values, bounds, and all future branching decisions. If two nonequivalent states collide and the pruned state contains a global minimizer absent from the retained state's symmetry orbit, duplicate pruning removes the only represented route to that minimizer. Approximate geometric equality or equal bounds alone therefore cannot certify duplication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate pruning is safe only when equal signatures certify full symmetry equivalence of regions and their future-relevant search states.
assumptions_latex: Duplicate detection may cause one search state to be pruned.
A valid symmetry must preserve the problem and future search behavior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A signature collision between nonequivalent states can destroy global completeness.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: pruning requires an equivalence relation preserving every correctness-relevant quantity
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role correctly captures unsound duplicate detection. The stated full-state symmetry implication is a strong sufficient soundness condition, but the record supplies no inspectable citation for this pruning boundary.

children.title: Proof-Progress Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Search regimes in which primal, dual, or reduction progress stalls.

children.title: Primal Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Persistent failure to obtain or improve validated feasible incumbents.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed operational condition for failure to obtain or improve a validated incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_k\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the objective value of the best validated feasible incumbent available after iteration \(k\), so \(U_{k+1}\le U_k\). For a window length \(w\ge1\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon_p\ge0\), primal stagnation at iteration \(k\ge w\) holds when either \(U_k=+\infty\), meaning that no feasible incumbent has been validated, or \[0\le U_{k-w}-U_k\le\varepsilon_p.\] Persistent primal stagnation means that this predicate holds for every sufficiently large \(k\), despite continued node processing or candidate generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal stagnation means no validated incumbent exists or its objective improves by at most a chosen tolerance over each monitoring window.
assumptions_latex: Incumbents are feasible and independently validated.
\(U_k\) records the best incumbent value monotonically.
\(w\) and \(\varepsilon_p\) are fixed monitoring parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed predicate identifies finite-window or persistent primal stagnation.

notation.meaning: best validated incumbent value after iteration k

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

children.title: Dual Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Persistent weakness of regional lower bounds despite tree growth.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed operational condition for persistent failure of the certified global lower bound to improve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, let \(L_k\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) be the certified global lower bound obtained from all active regional relaxations after iteration \(k\), with \(L_{k+1}\ge L_k\). Given \(w\ge1\) and \(\varepsilon_d\ge0\), dual stagnation at iteration \(k\ge w\) holds when either \(L_k=-\infty\), or \[0\le L_k-L_{k-w}\le\varepsilon_d,\] while at least one region has been processed during that window. It is persistent when the predicate holds for all sufficiently large \(k\); tree growth alone then supplies negligible certified lower-bound progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual stagnation occurs when the certified global lower bound remains absent or improves negligibly across windows containing actual search work.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\) is a valid monotone global lower bound.
At least one region is processed in each assessed window.
\(w\) and \(\varepsilon_d\) are fixed monitoring parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed predicate identifies finite-window or persistent dual stagnation.

notation.meaning: certified global lower bound after iteration k

children.title: Domain-Reduction Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Repeated contraction effort with negligible domain or relaxation improvement.

assumptions_latex: Each contraction satisfies \(B'_j\subseteq B_j\).
The size function \(v\) is monotone under inclusion, and \(0<v(B_j)<\infty\).
The regional lower bounds \(\ell_j,\ell'_j\) are finite, valid, and satisfy \(\ell'_j\ge\ell_j\).
The tolerances \(\varepsilon_v\) and \(\varepsilon_\ell\) are fixed nonnegative monitoring parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two tolerance inequalities characterize a geometrically and relaxation-wise stagnant domain-reduction pass.

notation.meaning: monotone size function for search regions
valid finite regional lower bounds before and after reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational condition for contractions producing negligible geometric and relaxation improvement.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a domain-reduction pass maps a region \(B_j\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) to \(B'_j\subseteq B_j\). Let \(v\) be a size function that is monotone under set inclusion and satisfies \(0<v(B_j)<\infty\). Suppose the pass changes a finite valid lower bound from \(\ell_j\) to \(\ell'_j\ge\ell_j\). For tolerances \(\varepsilon_v,\varepsilon_\ell\ge0\), pass \(j\) is stagnant when \[0\le 1-\frac{v(B'_j)}{v(B_j)}\le\varepsilon_v\quad\text{and}\quad 0\le\ell'_j-\ell_j\le\varepsilon_\ell.\] Domain-reduction stagnation over a nonempty window of attempted passes occurs when every attempted pass in that window is stagnant; persistence means this holds for all sufficiently late such windows despite repeated contraction effort.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Domain reduction stagnates when each attempted pass in a monitoring window yields neither meaningful region shrinkage nor meaningful strengthening of its finite valid regional lower bound.
